[p. 436]

**Sūrat "al-Zumar"**

Its purpose is to demonstrate that He, glorified and exalted, is true to His promise, and that He is dominant over everything. Therefore He does not hasten, for nothing escapes Him, and He places things in their most fitting positions. This is known to those of understanding (*ulū al-albāb*), who distinguish between the husk and the kernel. Its name "al-Zumar" (The Troops) indicates this, for it points to the fact that He sends each of those gathered (on the Day of Resurrection) to the abode prepared for him, after giving warning in admonition, and judging between them by what their deeds deserved, as a justice from Him, glorified is He, toward the people of the Fire, and as a bounty upon the pious and righteous. Likewise its name "Tanzīl" (The Revelation) is for one who reflects upon its verses and grasps its expression and allusion. Likewise "al-Ghuraf" (The Chambers), for it points to His judgment concerning the two groups: the people of the fiery canopies and the people of the luminous chambers. This is naming a thing by its most noble part, so what is said about them is the same as what is said about "al-Zumar." The people of the chambers have the added closing of their verse: ﴿The promise of God; God does not fail in His promise.﴾

**"In the name of God"**, who has perfected His word so His command is mighty; **"the Most Merciful"** (al-Raḥmān), who placed His general mercy in the most perfect arrangement, so its secret is subtle to people of understanding; **"the Most Compassionate"** (al-Raḥīm), who singled out His friends with success in obeying Him, so His goodness encompassed them.

When it became clear from the threat in "Ṣād" that He, glorified is He, is capable of what He wills, He then concluded it by saying that the Qur'an is a reminder for all worlds, and that everything in it must surely be seen, because it is certainly going to happen, but without haste. Some of their obstinate ones may have said: "What is the matter with Him? If He is capable, why does He not hasten what He wills after a while?" He explained this by saying ﴿it is a revelation﴾, that is, by way of gradual progression, in accordance with the suitability of benefits at their proper times and to bring it close to understanding, despite its loftiness, until it became a reminder for all worlds. He placed the phrase ﴿the Book﴾ in the position of a pronoun, to indicate that it gathers every goodness; that is, all of what is in it must be seen. For the great matter is that its sending down was in the manner of gradual revelation (*tanjīm*), to bring its understanding close, and to place each thing in it at its best time, without haste or delay. Then He informed about this revelation by saying ﴿from God﴾, that is, the One characterized by all attributes of perfection; ﴿the Mighty﴾, so nothing overcomes Him, and He overcomes everything; ﴿the Wise﴾, who places things in the positions most suited to them. Because it is from Him, and not from another, it is a reminder for all worlds, true in everything it reports, and wise in all of its matters.

Abū Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When "Ṣād" was built upon the mention of the polytheists, their obstinacy, their evil conduct, and their adoption of rivals and partners, what the opening of "al-Zumar" begins with was suitable: the command to sincerity (*ikhlāṣ*), which is the opposite of the state of those who came before, and the mention of what the Book leads to. So He (exalted) said: ﴿The revelation of the Book is from God, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ ﴿Indeed We have sent down to you the Book in truth; so worship God, sincere to Him in religion.﴾ [al-Zumar: 2] ﴿Is it not for God that sincere religion is due?﴾ [al-Zumar: 3] And His saying (exalted): ﴿And those who take protectors other than Him﴾ [al-Zumar: 3], etc., came in the context of: "Be upon sincerity, and leave those who associate and are not sincere; you will see their state." And will their excuse, by saying ﴿We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to God in position﴾ [al-Zumar: 3], benefit them? These are the ones upon whom "Ṣād" was built. Then God (exalted) rebuked them and reproached them, saying: ﴿Had God desired to take a son, He would have chosen whom He wills from what He creates﴾ [al-Zumar: 4], etc. He thus exonerated Himself of their grave offense by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿He is God, the One, the Subduer﴾ [al-Zumar: 4]. Then He reminded them of what contains the greatest evidence: the creation of the heavens and the earth, the wrapping of the night over the day and the wrapping of the day over the night, and the mention of the two signs, the day and the night. Then the creation of all human beings from a single soul, which is the soul of Ādam, peace be upon him. When He (exalted) moved them to reflection upon the greatness of these signs, which were the clearest thing and the most indicative evidence, He followed that with what points to the meaning of wonder at their hesitation after the evidences had become clear. Then God (exalted) made clear that He is independent of all, by His saying: ﴿If you disbelieve, indeed God is without need of you﴾ [al-Zumar: 7]. Then He said: ﴿And He does not approve disbelief for His servants﴾ [al-Zumar: 7]. Thus He made clear that whoever He chose, drew near, and selected from among the servants, He does not approve disbelief for him. From this arises the implication of the statement: that disbelief which occurs happens by His will and approval for whomever He tests with it. Then He comforted those who believed and did not follow the path of Satan and his band, from among those referred to earlier in the sūrah, saying (exalted): ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [al-Zumar: 7]; ﴿If you do good, you do good for yourselves﴾ [al-Isrā': 7]; ﴿And every soul earns only against itself﴾ [al-An'ām: 164]. Then the verses interlocked and the sentences joined until the end of the sūrah. End.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 2:

When He had informed that it (the Book) is from Him, He gave the reason for that by that through which all the good that has passed is established. So He said, turning the speech away from the third person (ghayba) and drawing attention to the increase in His greatness by mentioning His sending it down a second time, presenting it in the style of majesty, informing that He specially chose for it the greatest of His creation, expressing the sending down in a manner that is apparent for all, metaphorically (tajawwuzan) for the firm, decisive judgment that cannot be turned back:

﴿Indeed, We﴾; i.e., with the majesty that is Ours. ﴿have sent down﴾; i.e., by the majesty that is Ours. He joined this majesty with the particle of the limit (ila), which requires an intermediary, indicating that this (sending down) was at the beginning, as shown by its being followed by the command to worship; unlike what comes in this surah, for it (the sending down) is for the end, in that it became a disposition (khuluq) of him (ﷺ); so the particle of elevation ('ala) was more fitting for it, showing that its weight, which causes the feet to crack and the (cause of) the (ﷺ) to be sleepless, is specific to him (ﷺ) and to whoever is near him; (p-440) and its ease and facility for his community. So He said: ﴿to you﴾; i.e., specifically, through the intermediary of the angel. No one among the creation can claim to share with you in any of that, for his claim would necessarily cause a kind of confusion. He made explicit the place of the pronoun, for magnification, by alerting to what it contains of the gathering of the roots and branches, the subtleties and the knowledge. ﴿the Book﴾; i.e., the one that gathers every good, together with decisive clarification and firm judgment regarding the past, the future and the present, being clothed ﴿in truth﴾. Truth is the correspondence of reality with all its reports; reality follows its reports. No report of it is seen except that it corresponds to it with a correspondence in which there is no concealment of any of them. It has no ornament nor garment except the truth. So there is no proof more indicative that it is from Him than this. Let them therefore follow its report, and let them look at its essence and its effect.

When it was established by this that He, glory be to Him, specially chose for him something that everyone is unable to attain, it was established that He, glory be to Him, is God alone. Therefore there followed from this His saying, turning the speech away from the locus of majesty to something greater than it, by considering all the attributes of perfection, for the sake of worship, glorifying its rank because it is the goal in itself:

﴿So worship God﴾; i.e., the One possessing all the attributes of perfection, while you are ﴿sincere﴾; and sincerity is intending God in the intention without any cause; ﴿to Him﴾; i.e., alone; ﴿the religion﴾; by embracing the command with the utmost submission. Because He specially chose you with this great command, He is worthy of that from you; and He has humbled the enemies away from you, so none of them can reach you to weaken any part of your affair. So be sincere, that you may be the head of the sincere ones, of whom it was mentioned at the end of surah Sad that there is no way for Satan over them, and many of their leaders were mentioned, and there was an exhortation to follow them, through what was mentioned of their praises, for the sake of their patience in their sincerity. Al-Razi said: al-Junayd said: sincerity is the root of every deed; it is tied to the first of the deeds, which is the purification of the intention, and it is bound to the last of the deeds by not turning toward them, nor speaking of them, and concealing them in all states; and it is the singling out of God in the deed. And in a report: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners from partnership."

[p. 442] When He, glory be to Him, commanded him with this command, He announced His own entitlement to it, that He seeks nothing but His own right, and that it cannot be conceived that this belongs to anyone else. In answer to one who might ask, "Why did He forbid him from turning to anything other than Him?", He said, calling out, to indicate that He has no equal, so that no one who hears this call can do anything but submit, willingly or unwillingly:

﴿Surely, to God belongs pure devotion﴾. That is, the Sovereign, the Most High, alone. "Pure devotion" (al-din al-khalis) because to Him belong command and creation, and no one shares in this with Him. Just as He alone created you and created everything you possess, so you should devote worship to Him alone. And because when someone worships Him sincerely, He suffices him in everything, whereas if someone were to devote himself sincerely to anything else, it would not be possible for that thing to suffice him in anything, let alone in everything. The religion that is fit for sincerity is Islam, which has been in every community, built upon the five pillars, established on pure sincerity, arising from vigilance in obeying and avoiding what God commanded and forbade, and in everything that pleases the Lawgiver or angers Him in matters of religion. Thus its entirety belongs to God, without any apparent or hidden desire, whether for fame or for anything else. He alone, glory be to Him, deserves this to the exclusion of anyone else, because He is the One who legislated it, and no one has any command alongside Him. How then could someone who has no command in any way share it with Him? As for any act in which there is even the slightest association, it is rejected from its doer, and God is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.

This, as you see, is a call, by my life, before which necks bow and heads are lowered, and to which no response can be given except "Yes, by His might," and "Indeed, by His majesty and greatness."

Al-Qushayri said: Whatever share the servant has in it is far from sincerity, except when it is by His command. For when He commands the servant to seek reward for his obedience and he obeys Him, he does not depart from seeking reward by seeking reward for obeying His command. Were it not so, there could be no sincere person in the world.

Ibn Burjan said: All of this, that is, abandoning sincerity, derives from love of remaining in this world and forgetting the meeting with God (exalted is He). Then he said, in substance: This is association (shirk), and it has three types. The first is association in divinity, which is to see another god alongside God, as in the shirk of the Magians, the anthropomorphists, and the idolaters; and the error of the Qadariyya resembles it. The second is association in worship, through showing off (riya') and attributing the deed to oneself. The third is hidden association, which is hidden desire: that one conceals the deed, fears its being revealed, and loves to be seen doing it and to be praised for his secret deeds. Among the best aids to sincerity is shyness before God, [p. 443] that you should adorn yourself for others with a deed that He inspired in you and strengthened you to perform, while you were deceived by it and imagined you were seeking nearness to Him. Then your enemy Iblis, who is hostile to you, comes to you, and you obey him in what harms you and does not benefit you. So seek help in your worship through concealment: conceal your good deeds just as you conceal your bad ones, for the deed done in secret exceeds the deed done in public by seventy times. This is like a tree: when its roots are exposed, its sap weakens, and the heat and cold of the air harm it, and it is exposed to calamities, such as cutting, drying, and other things; its branches do not flourish, its leaves become sparse, and its benefit diminishes. But when its roots sink deep, it is out of reach of calamities and safe from being cut by human hands, so its sap increases and its water flows through it. Its branches multiply accordingly, its leaves turn green, its goodness increases, and its fruit becomes pleasant to the one who picks it. Likewise, a deed that has hidden roots in the heart is purified in itself, cleansed of impurities, its goodness increases, and its reward becomes pleasant to its doer. When it is made manifest, it is not safe from the eyes of observers; when it is hidden, nothing remains to be feared from it except self-admiration and the love of being seen, which is the hidden desire.

Among their sayings: "Whoever knows God after having been astray, knows sincerity after showing off, and places death in its proper station, will not neglect death and preparation for it with whatever he is able." End of quotation.

When He, glory be to Him, informed of what belongs to Him alone, and since the focus of human command, indeed of all living beings, is guidance to their benefits so that they may do them, and to their harms so that they may avoid them, and the context [p. 444] indicates that the implied meaning is: whoever devotes his religion sincerely to Him, He guides him in all his affairs, even when difficulties intensify and the paths of error multiply, He followed this with information about those who cling to error, deviation, and absurdity. Warning against the likes of their condition, by what has been decreed concerning their outcome, He said:

﴿And those who﴾. Since humans are created to submit to the Sovereign, the Judge, and they turn to others only by struggling against the self with its desires and transgressions, He used the verbal form of ittikhadha (ta'akhudh, "to take"), saying ﴿have taken﴾. That is, they worked their minds until they turned them away from God, and so they took. He alerted them to their error in being content with the lesser instead of the Highest, by His saying ﴿besides Him﴾, and it is known that everything is besides Him. ﴿Protectors﴾: that is, they entrust their affairs to them. This includes those who took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God, even though they acknowledged that God alone created them and provides for them.

Since their act is indeed a wondrous marvel, He explained what they used to justify their act, so that it would be a clear sign that they have no guidance. So He said: ﴿"We do not worship them"﴾, that is, they say to those who devote their religion sincerely to Him, when these deny them the right to take protectors besides Him: "We do not worship them for anything, ﴿except that they may bring us near﴾." Glory be to Him, He indicated their distance from the truth by using the greatest Name together with the particle of limit, saying ﴿to God﴾, to Whom belong the foundations of might and the assemblies of greatness, ﴿a great nearness﴾, gradually, ﴿and bring us close in rank﴾, that is, a good nearness, easy, bright, increasing, growing, and elevated. Al-Qushayri said: They did not say this on God's authority, nor with His permission; they only judged this from their own selves. So God refuted them. In this is an indication of what the servant does of nearness [p. 445] by the energy of his own soul, without the judgment of the moment requiring it; all of that is following desire. End of quotation.

The verse is of the type called ihtibak: He mentioned the verb of bringing near first, as an indication of the verb of bringing close in rank second, and the noun of bringing close in rank second, as an indication of the noun of nearness first. Its secret is that they intended by this an excuse that silences them about the ugliness of their conduct. So He, glory be to Him, in relating their words, used emphasis in the most eloquent way, because indicating the meaning with two words is more fitting for its firmness and multiplication than a single word. And He began with the lighter of the two verbs, the more famous, the lighter, and the clearer. By my life, a people who adopted the most corrupt doctrines have lost the utmost loss, and made their excuse this verse with which God condemned the one who offers excuses. On this basis, their excuse has gained currency with many minds through this verse, and they are the people of ittihad (unity of being, the doctrine that God and creation are one), whose minds are not more foolish, nor their intellects more dull.

Since the focus of their religion is only desire, and everyone who follows desire cannot be free of turmoil within himself, how much more so when others are with him? How much more so when they are many? Disagreement and dispute multiply, and even if this does not happen in actuality, it exists potentially. That is why each tribe among those who worship idols had an idol different from the idol of another tribe. Some tribes worshiped Sirius, some worshiped the angels, and some worshiped other things. [p. 446] ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you have nothing to do with them﴾ [al-An'am: 159]; ﴿So they divided their affair among themselves into sects, each faction rejoicing in what it has﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 53]. He alerted to this, warning them by His saying, informing and emphasizing, because of their denial: ﴿Surely God﴾, that is, the One who possesses all attributes of perfection. Since He did not restrict the judgment to the Resurrection, and since they acknowledged that calamities in this world come from Him, He said ﴿will judge between them﴾, without any further emphasis. That is, among all who differ in religions and other matters, among those who take protectors besides Him, and among the sincere ones and others. So He will surely grant victory to the people of truth over all the people of falsehood.

Since they were scattered groups, most of their tribes differing from what the others believed, He said ﴿concerning that in which﴾, that is, in the religion which... and the matter which... Since their appeal to desire provides a strong motive for their disagreement, and since the act of taking protectors, upon which the speech is built, has a great concern for treating the inner self, unlike Surat Yunus, He affirmed the pronoun here, saying ﴿they﴾, that is, with their inner selves, ﴿are in it disputing﴾. That is, they have no principle that restrains them, so they return to nothing but division, however they turn, because they are enclosed in that work whose basis is desire, which is the source of disagreement. How much more so when the dissent of the sincere ones and their rejection of them is added, which their excuse points to? From this it becomes clear that the disagreement of the imams in understanding the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ, regarding rules they derived from these, is not disagreement at all but agreement, because what they all refer to is one, the sound and established origin from God. From this is the Prophet's ﷺ rejection of ʿUmar, Ubayy, and others, may God be pleased with them, when each of them objected to the one who differed with him in recitation, and he said: "This Qur'an was revealed in seven modes, so do not dispute." [p. 447] There is no difference whether each of the two matters is based on the Prophet ﷺ by transmission or by independent reasoning, because it is in effect a consensus, due to the unity of its source. And God is the Granter of success.

It is also possible that the pronoun in "between them" refers to them and to their worshipped objects, for among them there is no worshipped object, silent or speaking, except that it cries out by the tongue of its state, even if the tongue of its speech does not speak, that it is subdued, owned, a worshipper, not a worshipped. So they, along with those they worship, are in the utmost disagreement. [p. 448] Since it is an evident matter that a religion is not sound unless it is arranged in an order free from defect, and since a crooked religion calls to division and announces by itself its own abandonment and distance, the situation calls for amazement at anyone who adheres to it, let alone one who persists in it, let alone one who does not pay heed when warned, let alone one who fights in its defense. He answered one who seemed to say: What is the cause of their attachment to this error, which necessarily results in disagreement, actually or potentially? He said, emphasizing it, as a refutation of one who denies what this report contains, even though to some blind people other than this appears, from liars and disbelievers, [p. 449] adorned deeds and subtle thoughts, which are thought to be guidance but are really a trap:

﴿Surely God﴾, that is, the King, the Powerful, the Dominant, the Wise. Since the original form would be "He does not guide them," and He intended generality and the attaching of the judgment to a description, in order to repel from it, He said ﴿does not guide﴾, that is, He does not create guidance in the heart of ﴿him who﴾, that is, whose inner self ﴿is a liar﴾, that is, one who commits lying, deeply engrossed in it, until his lying led him to say about the King of kings that something draws near to Him without His permission, and to submit to it by worship, which is the ultimate in exaltation. Worship is not befitting except for the One who bestows the utmost blessing, yet he directed it to one who possesses neither harm nor benefit. He did not express the lying in an intensive form, because those whom the context concerns did not commit lying except in their claim that they bring them near.

Since whoever disbelieved at a certain time in history has multiplied his disbelief, owing to the abundance of the proofs for the Oneness (al-wahdaniyya) and the favours God has bestowed upon him, and since those whose context this is have disbelieved by designating their partners (shurakā') as fit for worship (ta'hīl), by actually worshipping them, and by claiming that they bring them near (to God) — He says ﴿kaffār﴾ (ungrateful disbeliever), in the intensive form (ṣīghat al-mubālagha).

It is better to say that the intensiveness (al-mubālagha) serves to convey that the one whom He does not guide is only the one upon whom He — glory be to Him — has sealed death in that state. Al-Qushayrī said: the indication is a warning to whoever presumes upon a station not his own and claims something he is not truthful about. God never guides him to what would set him right and give him direction; and his punishment is that He deprives him of that very thing he laid claim to with his assertion, before he has actually attained it through its existence and his tasting of it.

When He, glorified is He, had informed of the judgment among them, and that, together with its containing a threat, was sufficient to negate a partner and adequate in that respect, since the one judged cannot be a counterpart to the Judge, no doubt remained in any of this except regarding the claim of sonship. He said, negating it by way of resumption (istinaf), in answer to one who asks: "What, then, is the state of one who takes a son?" Al-Qushayri said: The impossible is mentioned by way of remoteness, as if to say what its ruling would be: ﴿If God had wished to take﴾; that is, He who encompasses all attributes of perfection; ﴿to take﴾; that is, to assume (yatakallaf), as is your habit; and it is not permissible by reason that God would be one who assumes; ﴿a son﴾; that is, as whoever claimed this has claimed. Since a son is only desired to be a chosen one, and God is capable of all things, He turned away from saying "He would have taken" to His saying: ﴿He would have chosen﴾; that is, He would have selected by way of adoption; ﴿from what He creates﴾; that is, what He brings into being more swiftly than a glance; and He expressed it with the particle most commonly used for what does not reason, indicating that He is capable of making the least of things the most noble, by way of repetition and continuity, as the use of the present tense indicates. So He said: ﴿whatever He wills﴾; that is, from what would stand in the place of a son, for one who cannot create other than this needs no recourse to a means of producing a son.

Since He is pleased only with the most perfect of offspring, who are sons, yet He did not will that, and so it did not occur, this is the utmost that could be conceived by reason: that He would create a noble creature and call it a son, as an indication of the intensity of His honoring it and His ennobling of it, or bring it near in the utmost nearness, as He did with the angels and with Jesus, peace be upon them. That became a cause of your error concerning them, until you claimed they were sons, then you claimed they were daughters, so you were liars in two respects. This is the furthest extent of possibility. As for whether begetting (tawallud) is permissible for Him, no; rather it is something reason rules out, because begetting occurs only for one in need, and the God cannot be conceived by reason to be in need at all.

Ibn Burjan said, in substance: Begetting as commonly understood is of two kinds. One is a son ascribed to his father by sonship, by birth, and by kinship; this has no existence in the exalted Being, no possibility of attainment in what is possible, and no admissibility in action in any way. The other is a son in the sense of adoption and taking, which the Arabs and other nations used to practice until the Qur'an abrogated it. So it is not far-fetched that this expression was permissible in the books before us. But when the disease overwhelmed them, and they deviated from the right intention, which is chosen selection, toward the sonship of birth, God misled them, blinded their sight, closed the path of worship from that, revealed the meaning of selection, made manifest the meaning of guardianship (wilayah), and abrogated that by this, because this admits no confusion. All of this is to demonstrate the perfection of this community and its exaltedness in every matter.

Since the attribution of a son to Him is like the attribution of a partner, or worse, and both are negated by the proof already mentioned, through their acknowledgment that His judgment, glorified is He, is binding in everything, as witnessed by existence and by the evidences establishing that He has no need of anything at all, let alone a son, He declared Himself free of what befits His majesty of transcendence in this station, and said: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾; that is, to Him belongs complete transcendence above every deficiency. Then He established the proof of this transcendence, which requires His uniqueness, and said: ﴿He is﴾; that is, the Doer of this deed and the Speaker of these words, outwardly and inwardly; ﴿God﴾; that is, the One who unites all attributes of perfection. Then He mentioned attributes which serve as the reason for this, saying: ﴿the One﴾; that is, the One who is not divisible at all and has no like, so He has no consort and no son, for if any of that were so, He would not be unique, nor would He have any genus, nor any resemblance in any respect. ﴿The Subduer﴾; that is, the One who possesses this quality, so everything is under His subjugation, their gods and others, by way of repetition and continuity. Thus it is established beyond doubt that He has no need of anything at all, and making what one has no need of, and no motive drives one toward, is folly from which the rational person is exalted. How then could it be attributed to One who possesses all perfection?!

al-Biqa'i's commentary (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 39, verse 5:

When he established these attributes, which negate that He has a partner or a son and affirm for Him absolute perfection, He indicated them by His saying: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth﴾. That is, He originated them from non-existence. ﴿With truth﴾: that is, a creation united with a established matter, which is not imagination or magic, in a manner that has no deficiency in any respect, no disparity, and no flaw, such that anyone could say it contradicts wisdom. Since this is among the clearest indications of the two attributes of Oneness and Dominance, along with the completeness of power and the perfection of command, He then mentioned, after the creation of the two horizons, the alternation of the two lights (al-malawayn). The takwir (إدارَةُ الشَّيْءِ عَلى الشَّيْءِ بِسُرْعَةٍ, the rapid turning of one thing around another so as to encircle it, rise above it, overcome it and cover it) indicates the attribute of dominance more than the iyla' (inserting one into the other). So He said, explaining the time of the creation of the two lights: ﴿He wraps the night over the day﴾. That is, He created them, meaning He shaped them while He wraps, folds and turns, covering with speed, height and dominance, a repeated, continuous and ongoing wrapping until their appointed term. ﴿The night over the day﴾: by covering it with it so that it leaves no trace of it. Because of the greatness of this work, He repeated the agent and said: ﴿And He wraps the day﴾, rising in its wrapping and covering, ﴿over the night﴾, so that it removes it in the same way. This includes an increase in each of them corresponding to what the other loses, because when one departs and the other comes in its place, it is as if the coming one wraps around the departing one and clothes it, just as clothing is wrapped around the one who wears it. Or it likens the departing one, in its disappearance, to the coming one as a visible thing around which is wrapped what hides it from the sight of gazes. Or, since each of them returns upon the other in successive returns, this is likened to successive turbans (akwar), one upon another, so that what is beneath them is concealed.

Since darkness preceded light, and the night is only darkness which is preceded by light at the rising of the sun, He, glory be to Him, arranged this order according to the sequence of creation. For this reason He mentioned the sign of the day first. He said, expressing it in the past tense, by His creating the two signs subjected (musakhkharatayn) to a known course for each of them, which it does not transgress, and a defined limit which it does not overstep: ﴿And He subjected﴾: that is, He made submissive, compelled, dominated, and obligated for what He wills, without any benefit to the subjected. ﴿The sun﴾: that is, the one which erases what was of darkness, so that it brings about the designation of day. ﴿And the moon﴾: that is, the sign of the night.

Since He informed of their subjugation, He explained the matter in which He directs them, saying, clarifying this subjection: ﴿Each﴾: that is, of the two; ﴿runs﴾: that is, by Our decree, which cannot be averted. This is a sign of the variation of the states of the servant, because his creation is comprehensive, so he varies in contraction and expansion, in union and separation, in taking and returning, in sobriety and intoxication, in the stars of reason, the moons of knowledge, the suns of recognition, the day of Oneness, the night of doubt and denial, the day of union, the nights of estrangement and separation; and in the manner of their variation, their increase and their decrease. This was said by al-Qushayri.

Since the purpose of the surah is might (al-'izza), whose center is victory, and the context is that of dominance, and since the decree is for a cause from which the effect does not deviate, it indicates dominance more than mentioning the end alone without its cause. He said: ﴿For a term appointed﴾: that is, to the end of the cycle and the cessation of motion. Since His dominance is established by this, He said, calling out, as a shot into the hearts of the deniers: ﴿Unquestionably He is﴾: that is, He alone is ﴿the Mighty﴾. Since perhaps a captious person might say: "Then why does He not seize those who oppose Him?" and since the attribute of dominance and might may cause the disobedient to despair and so keep them back from turning to Him, He said, explaining the reason for the delay and seeking to win their hearts: ﴿the Forgiving﴾: that is, the One who has the attribute of covering sins repeatedly, so He erases the sins of whomever He wills, both their trace and their substance, by His forgiveness, and seizes whomever He wills by His might.

When the creation of living beings was more indicative of God's oneness and dominion, through what He set them apart from inanimate things by life, which one cannot be freed from before one's term, and through what they have of compulsory matters from which there is no escape, and of voluntary matters which are, outwardly, left to His will; and when the most wondrous of His creations was man, through the power of speech he has, He said, indicating what was indicated by the creation of the two horizons, and turning the speech to address the whole species, signaling their fitness for address and their ascent to the heights of causes, without a conjunction, signaling that each of their creation and the creation of what came before them is independently indicative of what the passage is brought for: ﴿He created you﴾, that is, O people, you who claim divinity for other than Him, ﴿from a single soul﴾, which is Adam, peace be upon him.

When our bringing them into being from it came after the female was split from it, He said, conjoining it to what is implied: "He made from it its mate," indicating by the word "made" that the male is its cause and its source, and alerting by the particle of delay to the dominion to which the context points, with delay in time, the effect being postponed from its cause that necessitates it until the time of His will, because its being brought into being from him was after a period of his being brought into being. The principle in causes is that effects follow them without delay, and also a delay in rank: that this, being extremely contrary to its origin, is among the most wondrous of wonders. ﴿Then﴾, that is, after a time. He used the word "made" because it is sufficient to negate partnership, which is the style of this passage, and to show that He created Adam, peace be upon him, only so that he would be a cause for what arises from him of offspring, so that there would follow from that the manifestation of what belongs to Him (p. 456), glorified be He, of attributes of perfection. So He said: ﴿and made from it﴾, that is, from that soul, ﴿its mate﴾, that is, and He transported you after your creation from him to her; then He brought you forth from her into external existence. It is also permissible, and it is the better, that the meaning be, since the context is about the comprehensiveness of knowledge, which is implied by the sending down of the Book and what followed it: He decreed your creation in the state you are in, of number, colours, and all forms, when He created Adam, by preparing him so that you would issue from him, so you add nothing to what He has decreed, nor do you diminish; and that his mate would issue from him, and that was before Eve was created from him; then He brought her into being, so the issuing from her was an issuing from him, and all is from him. For this reason the hadith has come, in the Musnad of Ahmad ibn Mani', from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Allah created Adam on the day He created him, and struck his right shoulder, and brought forth offspring white like ants, and struck his left shoulder, and brought forth offspring black like coals. He said to the one in his right hand: 'To Paradise, and I do not mind.' And He said to the one in his left: 'To the Fire, and I do not mind.'"

When the diversification of living beings into different kinds was more indicative of power, which is the source of dominion, and He, glorified be He, is described as exalted, and most of the cattle are stronger than man, their being subjected to him and made submissive to him was a bringing down from their strength (p. 457) and a making weak of their might. He said, indicating that act and making by the word "sending down": ﴿And He sent down for you﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿of the cattle﴾, that is, camels in both their kinds, and cattle likewise, and sheep and goats. Since the Bukhti (Bactrian camels) and the buffaloes were not among the Arabs, He did not mention them, and restricted Himself to what they had, and said: ﴿eight pairs﴾, that is, of each kind two mates, male and female. "Zawj" (pair) is a name for one which has another with it, whose benefit is not complete except with it. If you consider this expression together with the expression about the creation of man, you will understand that the cattle were created, each male and female of them separately, not that one of them is from its companion; and that is more indicative of the absoluteness of disposal and its diversification than if He had made their creation like that of the son of Adam.

When their formation in their stages was a wonder, He said, resuming, as an explanation of what was summarized before: ﴿He creates you﴾, that is, He decrees your bringing into being and that of the cattle, in the state you are in of mixtures of elements, ﴿in the wombs of your mothers﴾. Since the shaping of creation inside the womb, where no creature's hand or sight can reach, is in question, He said, indicating His greatness and His perfect power and dominion: ﴿a creation﴾, and it indicated His forming it thing after thing, by the affirmation of the particle: ﴿after a creation﴾, that is, through the transitions of stages and the alternations of phases. Since the living being is not recognized for what it is except in the fourth stage (p. 458), and ignorance is darkness: He said: ﴿in three darknesses﴾, the darkness of the drop, then of the clot, then of the lump of flesh. When it becomes bones clothed with flesh, it is known whether it is male or female, and the darknesses of ignorance leave it, and it becomes another creation. It was said: the darkness of the belly, the womb, and the placenta; this was transmitted from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and Ibn Abi al-Dunya attributed it in his book "al-Qana'a" to Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him.

When perfection of greatness and dominion was established for Him, glorified be He, He said, resuming what the preceding discourse produced, magnifying by the particle of distance and the plural mim: ﴿That is﴾, that is, the One of lofty ranks, by your testimony, O creatures, all of you, some of you by the tongue of speech, and some of you by the speaking of their state, whose acts are all that has been mentioned from the beginning of the surah to here. When He indicated His greatness by the particle of distance, He gave information about the demonstrative name, and said: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One comprising all attributes of perfection. He alerted to their ignorance, in what they know of His lordship, by their practice of association, the practice of one ignorant of it, and said, describing Him: ﴿your Lord﴾, that is, the Owner and the Cherisher of you by creation and provision. Since the cherisher may not be a king, He said, as a result of what preceded: ﴿to Him﴾, that is, alone, ﴿belongs the dominion﴾. Since the one specially holding dominion may not be a god, He said, affirming for Him divinity, according to what oneness requires of it, and it is (p. 459) in the position of a result of a result: ﴿There is no god but He﴾.

When this context has undertaken the necessity of sincerity in turning to Him and turning away from what is other than Him, because all is under His domination and His prohibition and command encompass all, He made the following statement its consequence: ﴿How then are you turned away﴾, that is, how, and by what means, ﴿are you turned away?﴾, that is, compelled away from sincerity to Him, to associating with Him, by some diverting force, however great it may be. By using the passive form, despite this, He indicated that they are compelled in doing what they are engaged in, because they follow sheer destruction, leaving aside the proofs in which there is no concealment in any part; and it is known that no one leaves the proof in the thirsty wastelands, which if he leaves he perishes, except under compulsion. And that people were prepared for the path of guidance by what they were created upon of the best form, by soundness of natural disposition and rectitude of intellects. He alluded to this because they disdain being attributed to compulsion, and doing anything without choice, owing to the pride they have, and their loftiness of aspirations and greatness.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 7:

When the proofs became manifest and the arguments dazzled, he explained what is due upon those who veiled them with obstinacy, and what is for those who repented and returned through remembrance. So He said, beginning anew (mustaʾnafan) with what is the outcome (natijah) of what preceded, making known to them His blessing upon them, that He has not been worshipped for something that specifically benefits Him in gain or harm, but rather it is solely for their own welfare, beginning with what is of warding off corruptions: ﴿If you disbelieve﴾ (p-460), i.e., you conceal the proofs and persist in turning away from Him through associating others with Him; ﴿then indeed Allah﴾, because He is comprehensive of the attributes of perfection, ﴿is Free of need from you﴾, i.e., your disbelief does not harm Him, nor does your obedience benefit Him. As for you, there is no independence from Him for you in any way, and He will certainly judge between you; so you have harmed only yourselves. ﴿And He does not approve for His servants﴾ disbelief, for you — this was the original wording, as shown by what precedes it and follows it — and He only manifested it so that it would be general, and to remind them of what they find within themselves: that none of them would approve for his servants that their tribute be paid to another without his permission. So He said: ﴿for His servants﴾, i.e., those whom He alone brought into existence and nurtured, ﴿disbelief﴾, by turning toward other than Him; and you do not approve of that for your servants, although your ownership of them is in the utmost weakness. The meaning of non-approval is that He does not act as one who approves, by permitting it and affirming it, or by rewarding its doer and praising him; rather He acts as one who is displeased, by forbidding it, censuring it, and punishing its perpetrator. ﴿And if you are grateful﴾, i.e., through worship and sincerity in it, ﴿He approves it for you﴾, i.e., He approves the gratitude, which His act indicates, ﴿for you﴾, i.e., the approval befitting His sacred presence — glorified is He — by allowing you to persist in it, or by commanding you to it and rewarding you for its performance; and both aspects are by His will. The variation of the readers in its final ha' indicates the levels of gratitude — and Allah knows best. So the full vowel (al-wasl) is for those who reach the ultimate end according to their differing levels in attaining it, the elision (al-ikhtilas) is for the intermediate ones, and the quiescence (al-iskan) is for one who is in the first rank of it.

When this is in the context of judgment and subjugation, and it was the custom of the dominant rulers to impose upon some people the burden of others and to hold them to account for their transgressions, so that elevation over all might be orderly for them, because their knowledge does not encompass every opponent of their command, He explained that He — glorified is He — is other than that. So He said: ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾, whatever bearer it may be; ﴿but the burden of every soul is upon itself﴾, not extending beyond it; it is recorded against it for the duration of its existence in the abode of action. The sin that is written upon a person for abandoning enjoining good and forbidding evil is not the burden of another; rather it is the burden of his own self. The burden of the doer is upon the deed, and the burden of the silent one is upon the omission, because of what was obligatory upon him of commanding and forbidding. ﴿Then to your Lord﴾, i.e., alone, not to anyone whom you have associated with Him, ﴿is your return﴾, i.e., by resurrection after death, to the abode of recompense. And since recompense follows knowledge, He said, expressing it by it: ﴿Then He will inform you﴾, i.e., there results from the resurrection that He will inform you with a mighty informing, ﴿of what you used to do﴾, i.e., of what was in your nature to do, whether you actually did it or not; then He will recompense you for it if He wills.

And since the intent — as He indicated by "used to" (kuntum) — is the informing of all deeds that exist actually or potentially, the reasoning with His words is fitting: ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing﴾, i.e., of perfect knowledge, ﴿of the contents of the breasts﴾, i.e., of their possessors, from thoughts and resolutions; and this is what the companionship indicates: everything that has not come forth outwardly is, with respect to what has come forth, better known to Him.

(p-٤٦٢) When He (glory be to Him) mentioned that He alone possesses the dominion, and followed it with what pleases Him and what angers Him, He established the proof of that exclusive possession, though it is clearer than the sun, by an evidence that every person finds within himself. He did so in a manner in which He censured them for the contradiction, which is the gravest of censures and the most repugnant. He said: ﴿And when﴾. Here, and Allah knows best, it is a circumstantial clause (ḥāliyyah, a clause describing the state of the subject) from the wāw of "tuṣrafūn" (you are turned away). The original would have been "massakum" (touched you), but He generalised it, and by turning from direct address to the third person He pointed to the attribute that causes forgetfulness. So He said: ﴿touches the human being﴾, meaning this species, which is intimate with its own self, whether believer or unbeliever. ﴿Harm﴾, whatever harm it may be, from any direction it expects, as indicated by the adverbial phrase (ẓarf) in agreement with the purpose of the surah, together with the warning in the verse before it. ﴿He calls upon his Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to him, whose reminder of your heedlessness has preceded in His saying: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾ [Az-Zumar: 6], mentioning the attribute of His beneficence. ﴿Turning in repentance﴾, that is, returning greatly, ﴿to Him﴾ with his inner self, sincere in that, knowing by necessity found in his own soul that no one else will suffice him in his affair. This is because the harm has removed from him his desires and his shares of pleasure, and he turns away from what he used to claim of partners, his state of being making plain that He has no partner, glory be to Him, as is the truth. Thus in the state of hardship the truth and the belief coincide.

(p-٤٦٣) Since the human being, by the nature in which he was created of anxiety and despair, when he is in harm deems it utterly unlikely that it will be lifted from him, because he is confined to particulars and limited to clinging to means, He pointed to that, together with an indication of the promise of bringing about relief. So He said: ﴿Then﴾, that is, after his having deemed it extremely unlikely. And since ease is certain, and it is more than hardship, He expressed it with the particle of certainty. He said, drawing attention by the expression "khawwala" (to bestow) that His giving is an initial bounty from Him, for which no one deserves anything, because "takhwīl" (bestowal) is not a reward but an initiation: ﴿when He bestows upon him﴾, that is, gives him a gift firmly established from the outset, and makes him able to take good care of it, capable of managing its upkeep well, ﴿a favour from Him﴾, and enables him in it. ﴿He forgets﴾, that is, despite his supplication, to give thanks for the beneficence. So the period of his being bestowed upon became the time of his forgetting. Thus it is known that his welfare lies in hardship. ﴿What﴾, that is, the matter which ﴿he used to call upon﴾ his Lord, in sincerity, ﴿to Him﴾, for its removal, ﴿from that harm which was﴾. He informed of the closeness of the two times, of forgetting and of turning in repentance, by affirming the preposition, so He said: ﴿from before﴾, that is, before the state of bestowal. ﴿And He appoints﴾, in addition to ingratitude through forgetting the favour, ﴿for Allah﴾, that is, the One having no equal, as witnessed by the innate nature, the intellect and revelation, ﴿equals﴾, that is, because he ascribes to Him rivals, thereby placing them in the position of one who is able to oppose and contend. It is known from the expression of forgetting that he knows his Lord, and for that reason he called upon Him in the removal of his harm. And that he made his knowledge at the time of being favoured into ignorance, so he became like one who does not know, among the other dumb animals.

(p-٤٦٤) Since this is in the utmost degree of error, because, although it is a mistake, it necessitates cutting off the beneficence and the non-answering of the removal of harm a second time; and since they used to claim that they were the most intelligent of people; and since this error was most evident, and the intelligent person does not do anything except for a cause, He glorified them, in mockery of them, as though they had not gone astray with this manifest error without intending it. So He said, pointing to all of that: ﴿so that he may lead astray﴾, that is, by himself, if the yā' is vowelled with a fatḥah, and lead others astray, if it is vowelled with a ḍammah, ﴿from His way﴾, that is, the path leading to His good pleasure, which brings about success through His beneficence.

Since it is known, established, and certain, fixed in the primordial natures (al-fiṭar al-ūlā, the innate disposition, fiṭrah) and continuing in what follows, that the sovereign does not leave one who disobeys him without punishment; and since it has been established by the consensus (ijmā', the agreement of the scholars) at the time of necessity that one does not turn to anyone other than Allah; and since whoever turns to another after Allah has delivered him from his harm and lavished upon him His favours is an unbeliever beyond doubt in the judgement of any person of intellect; and since those who are in this condition in this abode are the people of great blessings and of pure enjoyment free from troubles, it is known that they must necessarily be punished in the abode of permanence. So He (exalted be He), explaining that this enjoyment is only the cause of this ingratitude, as a gradual lure (istidrāj), together with the turning away that announces wrath, said:

(p-٤٦٥) ﴿Say﴾, that is, O most beloved of Our creatures to Us, the one deserving to be addressed directly, to this one who has been judged to be an unbeliever, threatening him with what will be cut off from him of the pleasant life in this world, from the outpouring from the most holy presence, and what his affair will come to of the greatest punishment: ﴿Enjoy yourself﴾, that is, in this world, which, together with its being transient, and everything in it, is overflowing toward Allah. Therefore it is among the things that incur hatred, except for one who spends it in obedience to Allah.

When He mentioned His granting him enjoyment of the base, He mentioned its base cause, to magnify the rewards of the believers for their turning away from unbelief, despite their knowledge that it is among the causes of such enjoyment, and to make clear to others of lofty resolve. So He said: ﴿with your disbelief﴾. Then He pointed to the brevity of the time of this world and what is in it, compared with the Hereafter, so He said: ﴿a little﴾. Then He gave the reason for that: that if the most blessed of the people of this world were dipped once into His punishment, he would say, "I have never seen any blessing at all." So He said, emphasising it, because of their denial of the Fire and to repel what had settled in their souls, that their being blessed in this world is only due to their nearness to Allah and His love for them, and that this would connect with the blessings of the Hereafter, supposing it exists: ﴿Indeed, you﴾. This command here is intended as a rebuke. Its implied meaning is: if you enjoy yourself in this manner, you will be ﴿among the companions of the Fire﴾, that is, those who were created for nothing but it: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind (p-٤٦٦) who have hearts with which they do not understand﴾ [Al-A'raf: 179].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 9:

When "*am*" (or, is it that) is definitively indicated, in the reading of the one who doubles the letter, by assimilating (*idghām*, the merging of one letter into the next) one of the two *mīm*s into the other, the implied sense, as an explanation of the state of the believers after the state of the polytheists, is: "Is this one who calls upon God once, and [then] another who makes rivals to Him [at other times], more upright in his path and sounder in his saying?" ﴿Is he who﴾. The implied sense in the reading of Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Hamzah, with the lightened pronunciation, is: "Is one who is of this quality better, or that disbeliever who forgets the one who has been good to him?" The implied sense as an interrogative rather than an exclamation strengthens the denial of equality between the one who knows, whose knowledge moves him to devotion, and the one who does not truly know, or does not know in a metaphorical sense, because he does not benefit from his knowledge. ﴿devoutly obedient﴾, that is, sincere in his worship of God (exalted be He) constantly; ﴿during the hours of the night﴾, that is, all of its hours.

Since the context is sincerity, and sincerity is the nearest means of drawing near to God, because it is the stripping away of all other things, and prostration is the most fitting of acts for this state, and for this reason it is the closest approach of the servant to his Lord, because it belongs exclusively to God (exalted be He), He says: ﴿prostrating﴾, that is, and bowing; and He indicates his firmness in the two qualities by conjunction, so He says: ﴿and standing﴾, that is, and sitting. He expresses it by the noun form to draw attention to the continuity of his sincerity in both his prostration and his standing. The verse is an instance of *iḥtibāk* (a rhetorical device in which one term is mentioned and its counterpart omitted, the omitted one being understood from the mentioned one). He mentions prostration as an indication of bowing, and standing as an indication of sitting. The secret in what is mentioned and what is left out is that prostration indicates worship, and the pairing of standing with it indicates that it is standing [in worship] from Him, so it is worship; and this is together with the announcement that these two are the greatest of the pillars, so it is a recommendation to lengthen them over the other two pillars, because sitting is only for the ease of rest, while bowing is intended to dedicate the limbs to worship, since it is not customarily possible for it to be for anything else. As for prostration, the possibility of falling is conceivable in it, and standing and sitting are among the things customary. So when He joined bowing to them, they became purely for submission before the King, the All-Knowing, the Mighty, the Merciful.

Since man is the locus of slackness, heedlessness and forgetfulness, and this is in the place of forgiveness, and his rectification is not possible except by fear of the Judge, the King of Judgement, He said, giving the reason or beginning a new statement as an answer to one who seems to say: "Why does he tire himself with this fatigue and exert himself with this toil?": ﴿He fears the Hereafter﴾, that is, the punishment of God therein; so he is constantly renewing this [fear] whenever he forgets it. And when He mentioned fear, He followed it with its companion, which is not valid without it, so He said: ﴿and hopes for the mercy of his Lord﴾, that is, the One who never ceases to turn in His bounty.

Since what moves one to fear, hope and action is only beneficial knowledge, and knowledge that does not benefit is like ignorance, or ignorance is better, the answer to the preceding interrogation was: "They are not equal," because the sincere one is a knower and the polytheist is ignorant. So He commanded him to answer with His saying: ﴿Say﴾, that is, they are not equal, because what moves one to sincerity is knowledge, and what moves one to polytheism is ignorance and lack of intellect. Then, reject the one who doubts that, so say to him (p-468): ﴿Are they equal?﴾, that is, in rank; ﴿those who know﴾, that is, who act in accordance with the requirement of knowledge, so their knowledge led them to monotheism and sincerity in religion; ﴿and those who do not know﴾, so their deeds do not accord with the requirement of knowledge, either from ignorance or from turning away from what knowledge requires, so they became as if they had no knowledge, because it brings them no benefit. For if they reflected even briefly, while stripping their souls of desire, they would return to the fact that no one at all is pleased that his servant should oppose his command, and to the fact that knowledge is applied only to one who acts. The saying of Ibn Hisham in the *Sīrah* guides to this: "They love to be praised for what they did not do," that people say, "They are scholars," while they are not people of knowledge, and [such knowledge] did not lead them to guidance or truth.

Since the axis of rectitude is remembrance, and the axis of remembrance, by which righteousness and corruption come about, is the heart, because it is the seat of intellect, which is the instrument of knowledge; and since a heart that does not move one toward righteousness is nothing, indeed nothingness is better than it, He said: ﴿Only those remember﴾, that is, a great remembrance, by what the articulation of the *tā'* (in the verb) makes understood. So it is known that the benefactor does not accept being good to one who eats of his bounty and worships another; ﴿people of understanding﴾, that is, the pure intellects and the luminous hearts. They are the ones described at the end of *Āl ʿImrān* by His saying (exalted be He): ﴿Those who remember God standing and sitting and upon their sides﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:191] to (p-469) its end. How excellent is the expression here by *lubb* (kernel, pith, essence), which is the essence of a thing! Because the context is sincerity. Al-Razi said in *al-Lawāmiʿ*: Imam Muhammad ibn ʿAli al-Tirmidhi said: God (exalted be He) created things subjected to the son of Adam, and created the son of Adam for service, and placed in him His lights, so that service to God (exalted be He) might come forth from his inner being through need. So the son of Adam is commanded to know God (exalted be He) and His commands, according to what he was created for; and service and devotion by your heart before Him, inclining, standing upright, true, hastening, racing, driving your vehicle in all your affairs with love for Him. The knowledge of service is the knowledge of the two carpets: the carpet of power and the carpet of servitude. When you contemplate the carpet of power with full intellect, which is that you know yourself and your composition, of spirit and body, and you contemplate the carpet of servitude with complete shrewdness, you perceive His governance in servitude, and the inner meaning of His command and prohibition, and the causes of prohibition and permission. God spread the carpet of lordship from the gate of power, and spread the carpet of servitude from the gate of greatness. Then the last of His creation, glorified be He, was this human being, for whom He spread these two carpets, and in whom He gathered the two worlds, and increased above what is in them the acceptance of the command by choice and willingly. Everything He gave you, He gave you only so that you might manifest it through your limbs and employ it for what it was created for; for if He had not given you, He would not have asked it of you. Zakat is not demanded from one who has no wealth, nor is prayer standing demanded from one who has no leg.

(p-470) Since it has been established that the one who is obedient (al-qanit) is best, and since those who oppose him are many, and since the greatest motive for obedience (al-qunut) is taqwa (God-consciousness), and since the multitude of opponents is the greatest shaker of resolve, and since man, by reason of his deficiency, is most in need of being made firm, and since firmness that comes from one of one's own kind and comforting that comes from one of one's own likeness are more soothing to the heart and more expansive to the breast, He commanded the most perfect of creation and the most gentle of them in kindness to make them firm, so He said: ﴿Say﴾. And since firmness does not take root amid the multitude of opponents and the successive shocks and perils unless it comes from the King, He attributed that to Himself, glory be to Him, so that the Creator and those nearest to Him among creatures would be gathered around it, so He said: ﴿O My servants﴾, rather than saying "O servants of God" for example, as a reminder to them and to calm their hearts, given what is known, that the implied words are "God says"; and as an honoring of them by attributing them to Himself with a pronoun that indicates tenderness and great special closeness; and as an informing of them that He is present and never absent from them in any way. ﴿Who have believed﴾, meaning: who have brought this reality into being, even at its lowest degree.

Since kindness may sometimes embolden one toward the benefactor, He, glory be to Him, pointed to the soundness of the saying of the knowers: "Sit upon the carpet, and beware of overfamiliarity (al-inbisat)." He also alerted, by turning the speech away from the mode of direct address, to a description indicating that the intelligent person is one for whom kindness obligates reverence and exaltation, and whose tenderness and nearness produce in himself humility, lowliness, fear and brokenness, lest he suffer what is least of it, namely the cutting off of kindness. So He said: ﴿Fear your Lord﴾, meaning: make between yourselves and the anger of the One who is kind to you a shield, by ascending through the degrees of His obedience, sincere to Him, just as He created you for yourselves and not for any purpose of His, so that your faith may take root and your goodness may grow. This is the clearest proof that faith may exist together with the absence of taqwa.

Since He guided them, by the name that looks toward kindness, to say: "What will we have if we do it?", He answered them, giving the reason: ﴿For those who do good﴾, meaning: for you. But He made apparent the description that indicates the cause of their reward, to arouse eagerness for more of it from Him. And since action benefits only in the abode of obligation, He said: ﴿in this﴾, using the demonstrative to add precision, ﴿world﴾, meaning: the lowly, the defiled, in which life is not purified except by sanctification through worshipping the Creator and adorning oneself with His attributes. ﴿Good﴾, meaning: great in this world through victory and support, along with the multitude of opponents, and in the Hereafter through reward. It is also permissible that the meaning of "they did good" is "they performed goodness," and it is known that this is in this world; then what follows would be a subject and predicate, but it becomes specific to the reward of this world; so the first reading is preferable.

Since it may happen to a person in a land that someone prevents him from doing good and drives him to disobedience, He, glory be to Him, urged emigration to where that obstacle is removed, alerting that such a thing is not an excuse for negligence, as it has been said:

"And if a dwelling turns harsh on you, then move on."

So He said: ﴿And God's earth﴾, meaning: He to whom belongs all sovereignty and all-encompassing greatness, ﴿is spacious﴾; and His existence, by His knowledge and power, is in every land equally. So whoever is bound to one place of it is weak in resolve and feeble in certainty, and there is no excuse for one who falls short in goodness by not emigrating.

Since patience upon leaving one's homeland, especially if there are family and kin there, is very severe, He mentioned what awaits the one who is patient in that, for whoever longs to ask about it. So He said: ﴿Only the patient will be given their due﴾, meaning: the great full recompense, ﴿the patient ones﴾, meaning: patient upon what souls dislike in opposing desire and following the commands of the Most High King, including emigration and other things. ﴿Their reward without reckoning﴾, meaning: in such abundance that it is not possible in the usual way to count it. That is because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, and every deed can be counted and limited, except patience, which is constant with every breath, and it is one of the inner meanings, whose measure in its strength and weakness, its severity and gentleness, no creature perceives; because although it is hidden, its measure varies and its effects grow according to the aspirations in their height and lowness, their loftiness and descent. It is also permissible that the meaning is that whoever's patience is perfected, by what the particle of perfection (lam al-kamal) indicates, will have no reckoning upon him, in accordance with what al-Bazzar and Ibn Hibban related in his Sahih (authentic collection) from Abu Hurayra, may God be pleased with him, who said: "A woman came to the Messenger of God ﷺ, afflicted by a lamam (an affliction), and she said: 'O Messenger of God, pray to God for me.' He said: 'If you wish, I will pray to God and He will heal you; and if you wish, you may be patient and there is no reckoning upon you.' She said: 'Rather, I will be patient, and there is no reckoning upon me.'"

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 11:

Since the eyes are fixed on the command, to see whether the one who gives it acts upon what he commands, and are bound to the leader so that they may follow his example; and since the greatest of the patient is the one who struggles against his own self until he purifies its deeds from impurities, guards them from personal interests and obstacles, and protects them from slackness and preoccupations; He commanded him with what would make them eager for striving and would reveal to them the sweetness of patience, by saying: ﴿Say﴾. And since the leader, because of his nearness to the King, is such that it is thought that he is indulged in much of what is imposed upon others, He emphasized his statement: ﴿Indeed I have been commanded﴾; and He constructed the verb in the passive form, to magnify the command, indicating that it is decided and has passed, such that no mixture remains in it; and He placed in the position of the subject, as a sign that it is the core, to urge adherence to it, His statement: ﴿that I worship Allah﴾; that is, the One before whose grasp and exaltedness and greatness all creation is equal, because He is independent of everything; ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾; that is, the worship for which reward is hoped from Him.

The chief, when he goes ahead to something, arouses souls toward it and makes it incumbent upon them to devote themselves to it. So He said: ﴿And I have been commanded﴾, i.e., the command has come to me and been settled upon me with great commands beyond what you have been commanded, which you cannot bear, ﴿that I should be﴾, i.e., for the sake of being, ﴿the first﴾, i.e., the greatest, ﴿of the Muslims﴾, i.e., those who submit, in rank, who win the prize of precedence in every respect in obeying the commands of God, for there is no success except by complying with His commands. Or [it means] the earliest of them in my time. So the aspect of this act is not the aspect of the first [meaning]. Therefore He conjoined it with it (with ʿaṭf, the conjunction *ʿaṭf*), because it is for securing the prize of precedence, while the first [meaning] is for absolute sincerity (*ikhlāṣ*) in worship.

Since what He commanded him to do implies that it should be accompanied by both encouragement and warning; and since it might be thought that the leader does not fear the King, because of matters hoped for from him or feared; and since repeating the command to convey it to those commanded had a greater effect on their hearts and made their souls more attentive, He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿Say﴾; i.e., to your community. And He emphasized, because of what occurs to minds, that the leader does not fear, his saying: ﴿Indeed I fear﴾; i.e., even though He has assured me of the forgiveness of what came before and what came after, out of sincerity in His exaltation and magnification, and in fulfilling what is due from the servant to his Master, to whom belongs all greatness and majesty. And since the attribute of goodness may embolden one toward disobedience, He made clear that this happens only from lack of recognition, so He said: ﴿If I disobey my Lord﴾; i.e., the One who has been good to me, who has nurtured me with every beauty, so that I abandon sincerity toward Him; ﴿the punishment of a great day﴾. And if the day is great, how then will His punishment be?!

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 14:

When He had explained what He commanded him, and informed him that He fears opposing His command in this respect, thereby indicating that he is complying with what he was commanded, the Exalted commanded him to state this explicitly, because explicit statement has a distinction that is not hidden. So He said: ﴿Say: "Allah"﴾; i.e., alone, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection; ﴿I worship﴾, singling Him out for this, and not turning at all toward worship of anyone other than Him, ever; ﴿sincere to Him﴾, alone; ﴿in my religion﴾; i.e., in compliance with what I have been commanded, so I do not sully it with any admixture at all; neither seeking a garden, nor fearing a fire, for He has forgiven me what came before and what came after. Thus my worship becomes for the sake of His Face, and for His being deserving of worship exclusively, out of longing for Him, love for Him, and shame before Him. As for desire for what is with Him, the Exalted, and fear of His punishments, which in sum mean the cutting off of kindness, which for the ignorant is the least of what is feared, then my fear is only for the sake of giving the station its due of the humility of servanthood and the might of lordship.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 15:

When it became known from this the utmost of obedience through the utmost of desire and awe, and they know that he (ﷺ) was the strongest of them in heart, the purest of them in intellect, the boldest of them in soul, the most truthful of them, and the most courageous of them in kinsfolk and party, the fear of others was by way of a fortiori. So on this basis He threatened them with the greatest threat, by His saying: ﴿So worship﴾, meaning: you, O those who call upon Him in time of adversity and turn away from Him in time of ease, ﴿what you will﴾, meaning: of inanimate things or others. He alerted to the lowliness of the rank of everything in relation to Him, Glorified is He, as a rebuke to whoever turns to other than Him, by His saying: ﴿besides Him﴾, for the worship of what is beside Him leads to the severing of His favour, and there is no favour except His favour; so when it is severed, every evil occurs, and in that is the whole of loss.

When they claimed intelligence and did what no intelligent person would do, He commanded him to say to them what alerts them to their stupidity, by what they will come to of their wretchedness. So He said: (p-476) ﴿Say: Indeed the losers﴾, meaning: those whose loss is the (true) loss, because it is the ultimate in ruin; ﴿who have lost themselves﴾, meaning: by their entering the Fire, which is the source of destruction, due to their worshipping other than Allah of everything that necessitates transgression. And since the dearest thing to a person after himself is his family, those through whom his honour is, He said: ﴿and their families﴾, meaning: for if they were like them, their state in loss is like their state, and none of them can console his companion in any way, for each of them has a matter that occupies him; and if they were saved, there would be no gathering among them.

And since the outcome is the thing intended in itself, He said: ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾, because that day is the decisive judgement, in which what has passed cannot be remedied at all. And since in that is the utmost of terror, He repeated the description of their stupidity, as an alert to their firm rootedness in that attribute, by way of conclusion from what the preceding had conveyed; so He said — calling out, because it is more terrifying, emphasizing with the resumption, the particle of alerting, the pronoun of separation, the definiteness of the predicate, and its description: ﴿Unquestionably, that﴾, meaning: the great matter, far-reaching in rank in loss exceedingly; ﴿it is﴾, meaning: alone; ﴿the loss﴾ — he came with the form "fu'lān", which conveys absolute intensity; so how if it is built on the ḍamma, which is the heaviest of the vowels? And he increased in rebuking them for stupidity by His saying: ﴿the manifest﴾.

**(p. 477)** When this became known, that the one who calls out with it is clearly so in himself, by what is in it of ugliness, that no loss belongs to anyone but him, He specified it with His saying, in the manner of mocking them: ﴿For them﴾. The habit of the *lam* (the preposition *al-lam*, "for") when it accompanies a *majrur* (the object governed by a preposition), especially a pronoun, is to indicate that the one for whom it is intended is the one addressed. This is especially so with the mention of the canopies. He indicated their nearness to them by affirming the preposition (*al-jarr*, "from"), so He said: ﴿Above them are canopies﴾. When that led them to think there was relief, He removed that with His saying: ﴿of Fire﴾. That is more severe than if He had conveyed the evil to them from the start. Since remaining in one place, whatever it may be and in whatever state, contains some kind of relief through stillness, He made clear that they are suspended in the surges of agitation. The blaze lifts them up at times, and its reflection back onto them brings them down at other times, so there is no resting place for them at all. This is like a grain of pulses in water over fire, boiling up and down, never settling at the bottom of the pot at all. This is His saying: ﴿and beneath them﴾. Since the canopy, which is taken from shade, being beneath (them) is extremely strange, He repeated it and did not suffice with the first mention. He did not repeat the mention of the Fire, because it is understood to be below by a fortiori reasoning. So He said: ﴿canopies﴾.

Among what supports my understanding of the absence of a resting place is what al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih, from Samura ibn Jundub (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished a prayer, he would turn his face to us and say: 'Who among you saw a dream last night?' One day he asked us, and we said: 'No.' He said: 'But I saw two men come to me, take me by the hand, and bring me out to the holy land.'" He then related it at length, until he said: "We set off to a pit like an oven, narrow at the top and wide at the bottom, with a fire kindled beneath it. In it were men and women, naked. The blaze reaches them from beneath, so when it approaches them they rise up until they nearly come out, and when it dies down they sink back." He related it, and it is long and great. Then he interpreted them as fornicators.

Since this is a dreadful matter, and they neither fear it nor turn back from their error because of it, He mentioned its benefit, together with an increase in magnifying it, and said: ﴿That﴾, that is, this matter of great importance, ﴿with it Allah makes fearful﴾, that is, the Greatest King, whose attributes are overpowering might and majesty, ﴿His servants﴾, that is, those for whom there is little turning toward Him, so that they may increase in faith along with their faith, and so He protects them from it. When He had qualified them to be attributed to Him, and made them fear His forcefulness, He turned to them at the moment of preparing them to listen, alerting them that this is a fear of tenderness and gentle appeal, and said: ﴿O My servants, so fear Me﴾, that is, as a consequence of that, make between yourselves and what displeases Me a shield against what pleases Me, so that I may be pleased with you.

When he had mentioned the fate of those who worship the *taghut* (false deities), he joined to it their opposites, so that promise would be paired with threat and the encouragement (*targhib*) and the warning (*tarhib*) would be complete. He said: ﴿And those who avoid﴾. That is, they imposed this upon themselves, though the self inclines toward it through desire, together with Satan's adornment of it, as in the hadith: «The Fire is surrounded by desires.»

Since the general statement (*ijmal*) followed by the detailed explanation (*bayan*) has a great effect, He said: ﴿the *taghut*﴾. It is everything that is worshipped besides Allah. Its form is *fa'lut*, derived from *al-tughyan* (transgression), and it is an intensive form (*sigha mubalaghah*).
