There is another intensification in it, by making the essence itself identical with the meaning. It also indicates the opposite of those who follow it, by reversing the order of its letters.

Since He mentioned avoiding it in general, as encouragement toward it, He clarified the essence of what is to be avoided for its sake, along with a repulsion from it by its feminine form (*ta'nith*). The turning-back believers perceived this by Allah's strengthening them against it, so that they became males while they were females, the reverse of what had preceded concerning the disbelievers in *al-Baqarah*. So He said, replacing it with a *badal al-ishtimal* (inclusive apposition): ﴿to worship it﴾.

When He mentioned avoiding *shirk*, He followed it with adherence to *tawhid*, and said: ﴿and turn back﴾. That is, they returned with a great return, in which they removed any hesitation and made it a single turning, with no diversion in it, ﴿to Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, so there is no deviation from Him. ﴿For them is good news﴾ in this world, through the tongues of the messengers, and at death the angels will receive them. They have gained a profit with no loss attached, because they benefited from the words of Allah and so made their religion sincerely His. So give them good news, this is how the original would be; but He made it apparent for generality, and to attach the news to the attribute. So He said, making it a consequence of their deeds, turning the speech to the first-person singular for the honour of those who are given the good news and described thus: ﴿So give good news to My servants﴾, that is, those who qualified themselves by confining their resolve to Me, for their attribution to Me.

(p-480) [Al-Biqa'i:] ﴿Alladhina yastami'un﴾ (those who listen): that is, with all their hearts. ﴿Al-qawl﴾ (the word): that is, this type of speech from every speaker. They are not coarse or stubborn; when they turn toward something, they do not turn away from everything else without evidence. ﴿Fa-yattabi'una﴾ (so they follow): that is, with all their resolve, after examining it. ﴿Ahsanahu﴾ (the best of it): by what their intellects indicate to them, without deviating to any lowest desire. It clearly enters into this verse that the People of the Book are urged to follow this Great Qur'an, for all the books of God are good, and this Qur'an is the best of them in speech, meanings, and arrangement. No one who has even the slightest taste doubts this.

When He had described their conduct, this resulted in their praise. So He said, showing increased love for them and concern for their affair, by emphasis: ﴿Ula'ika﴾ (those): that is, specifically those of lofty aspiration and rank. ﴿Alladhina﴾ (who). Since among these chosen ones are those of very high rank and others, He brought the object forward, and said, transforming the style to the Greatest Name, indicating the greatness of their guidance: ﴿Hada-humu Allah﴾ (God has guided them), by what He has of attributes of perfection. Thus He, glory be to Him, made clear that there is no arrival to Him except through Him. This is unlike the verse of al-An'am, where He mentioned the prophets, peace be upon them, and said: "Those are the ones whom God guided," so He omitted the object, so that their guidance would be repeated, by necessity of making the governing verb apply to the relative pronoun, which in this verse returns the pronoun to it. He repeated the demonstrative to increase their honor, and said: ﴿Wa-ula'ika hum﴾ (and those are they): that is, specifically; ﴿Ulu al-albab﴾ (people of understanding): that is, those of intellects pure from any turbidity of cloudiness.

ولَمّا خَصَّ - سُبْحانَهُ - البِشارَةَ بِالمُحْسِنِينَ؛ عُلِمَ أنَّ غَيْرَهم قَدْ حُكِمَ بِشَقاوَتِهِ؛ (p-٤٨١)وكانَ ﷺ لِما جُبِلَ عَلَيْهِ مِن عَظِيمِ الرَّحْمَةِ؛ ومَزِيدِ الشَّفَقَةِ؛ جَدِيرًا بِالأسَفِ عَلى مَن أعْرَضَ؛ سَبَّبَ عَنْ أسَفِهِ عَلَيْهِمْ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿أفَمَن حَقَّ﴾؛ وأسْقَطَ تاءَ التَّأْنِيثِ (tā' al-ta'nīth, the feminine ending) الدّالَّةِ عَلى اللِّينِ (al-līn, leniency or softness)؛ تَأْكِيدًا لِلنَّهْيِ عَنِ الأسَفِ عَلَيْهِمْ؛ ﴿عَلَيْهِ كَلِمَةُ العَذابِ﴾؛ بِإبائِهِ؛ وتَوَلِّيهِ؛ فَكانَ لِذَلِكَ مُنْغَمِسًا في النّارِ؛ الَّتِي أبْرَمْنا القَضاءَ بِأنَّها جَزاءُ الفُجّارِ؛ لا يُمْكِنُ إنْقاذُهُ مِنها؛ أفَأنْتَ تُنْقِذُهُ مِن إعْراضِهِ الَّذِي غَمَسَهُ في النّارِ؟ ثُمَّ دَلَّ عَلى هَذا الَّذِي قَدَّرْتُهُ بِقَوْلِهِ - مُؤَكِّدًا بِإعادَةِ حَرْفِ الِاسْتِفْهامِ (ḥarf al-istifhām, the interrogative particle)؛ لِأجْلِ طُولِ الكَلامِ؛ ولِتَهْوِيلِ الأمْرِ؛ وتَفْخِيمِهِ؛ لِلنَّهْيِ عَنْ تَعْلِيقِ الهَمِّ بِهِمْ؛ لِما عِنْدَهُ ﷺ مِن جِبِلَّةِ العَطْفِ؛ والرِّقَّةِ عَلى عِبادِ اللَّهِ -: ﴿أفَأنْتَ تُنْقِذُ﴾؛ أيْ: تُخَلِّصُ؛ وتَمْنَعُ؛ وتُنْجِي؛ ووَضَعَ مَوْضِعَ ضَمِيرِهِ قَوْلَهُ - شَهادَةً عَلَيْهِ بِما هو مُسْتَحِقُّهُ؛ ولا يُمْكِنُ غَيْرَ اللَّهِ فَكُّهُ مِنهُ -: ﴿مَن في النّارِ﴾؛ مُتَمَكِّنًا فِيها؛ شَدِيدَ الِانْغِماسِ في طَبَقاتِها؛ والرُّسُوخِ؛ بِحَيْثُ إنَّها قَدْ أحاطَتْ بِهِ مِن كُلِّ جانِبٍ؛ وكانَ الأصْلُ: أنْتَ تُنْقِذُ مَن حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ العَذابُ؟ فَقَدَّمَ المَفْعُولَ وجَعَلَهُ عُمْدَةَ الكَلامِ؛ لِيَقْرَعَ السَّمْعَ؛ ويُتَرَقَّبَ الخَبَرُ عَنْهُ؛ ثُمَّ حَذَفَ خَبَرَهُ لِيَكُونَ أهْوَلَ؛ فَتَذْهَبَ النَّفْسُ فِيهِ كُلَّ مَذْهَبٍ؛ ثُمَّ أنْكَرَ أنْ يَكُونَ أعْلى الخَلْقِ يُنْقِذُهُ؛ فَغَيْرُهُ مِن بابِ الأوْلى؛ فَصارَ الكَلامُ بِذَلِكَ مِنَ الرَّوْنَقِ؛ والبَهْجَةِ؛ والهَوْلِ؛ والإرْهابِ؛ ما لا يَقْدِرُ البَشَرُ عَلى مِثْلِهِ.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 20:

When he had explained that whoever worships the rivals (al-andad) is doomed, because he has stepped outside the circle of reason through audacity and lack of deliberation, he explained what belongs to their opposites. He said, turning the speech away from the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam) to the attribute of Ihsan (beneficence), as an indication of the nobility of the God-fearing, with what they possess of soundness of judgment (asalat al-ra'y), which necessitated their fear, together with remembrance of the beneficence, so that it would indicate that their fear at the remembrance of retribution is more fitting: ﴿But those who fear their Lord﴾; that is, they made between themselves and the anger of the One who does good to them a shield (wiqayah) in every movement and stillness, so they did not do anything of that kind except with a consideration that guides them to His pleasure. ﴿For them are chambers﴾; that is, lofty upper rooms of Paradise, which they dwell in, corresponding to the canopies of the disbelievers. And since the chambers are in a settled place in which the eyes are comforted, He did not say "above them," as He said regarding the people of the Fire; and He said: ﴿above them are chambers﴾; that is, of great height. And since it might be thought that the second tier is the sky, because the ghurfah (chamber) is originally something high, and for this reason the seventh heaven was called "ghurfah," and that the chamber might be like the canopies of the Fire, having no settled place, He said, establishing the reality and in the singular, as is customary in describing a plural of multitude for that which has reason: ﴿built﴾. And since dwellings are not pleasant except with water, and flowing water is more noble and better, He said: ﴿beneath them flow rivers﴾; that is, beneath the chambers, from the lower tier and from the upper tier, without any difference between high and low, because the power is capable of more than that: ﴿the rivers﴾.

When he mentioned the Day of Resurrection and what occurs in it, he explained that it is a matter that must come to pass, by saying, turning the context back to the Greatest Name, which cannot be conceived of while keeping in mind the majesty it possesses, a failure to fulfil (ikhlaf): ﴿The promise of God﴾; emphasising the content of the sentence by the form of the verbal noun (masdar) indicating the act, which governs it and whose implied verb is obligatory to omit, and by its being attached to the Greatest Name, which gathers all the attributes. Then he followed that with an explanation of what follows from His being the one who makes the promise, by saying, as a conclusion: ﴿God does not fail﴾; that is, the King, who has no partner who could prevent Him from anything He wills. And since keeping watch over the time and place of a promise is only for the sake of safeguarding it, and it is more emphatic than keeping watch over oneself, he expressed it with the form "mif'al," saying: ﴿the appointment﴾; because there is no cause at all that would move Him to fail.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 21:

When He - glorified is He - had informed of His power over resurrection, He indicated it by means of something whose like is repeatedly witnessed; and He singled out the Chosen Prophet (ﷺ) with the address, to urge reflection upon this proof and to alert to its greatness. So He said - by way of supposition -: ﴿Have you not seen﴾; that is: from what indicates to you His power - glorified is He - over restoring what has crumbled, been torn apart, become dry and scattered: ﴿that Allah﴾; that is: He to whom belongs every attribute of perfection; ﴿sends down water from the sky﴾; that is: the sky in which water cannot be held except by a overpowering power that compels it to that; ﴿and drives it as springs into the earth﴾; that is: into the depths of the soil, as gushing springs; ﴿so He compelled it to rise after He had hidden it in the depths of the earth with abundant flow and downpour, after He had constrained it to be restrained on high, then compelled it to descend in a known measure, in a arranged manner and an apportioned command. Ash-Sha'bi and ad-Dahhak said: every water in the earth comes from the sky; it descends to the rock, then the springs and wells are apportioned from it.

Since the bringing forth of vegetation is delayed after the descent of rain, He expressed it with ﴿then﴿ (thumma); and in it there is also an alert to the magnitude of the matter that follows, that it is the locus of witness. So He said: ﴿Then He brings forth﴾; that is: Allah; ﴿thereby﴾; that is: by the water; ﴿crops﴾; and since variation in the effect with unity of the cause is more wondrous in craftsmanship and more indicative of marvelous power, He said: ﴿of varying colours﴾; that is: in kinds, qualities, natures, tastes and other respects, while the water is one, which He gathered from the depths of the earth after it was crushed therein and became dust.

Since stopping after strong growth indicates subjugation and the force of command, He said, indicating that exceeding the limit is not praiseworthy in anything, for it returns to its possessor with loss: ﴿Then it dries up﴾; and He increased the magnification of this meaning, to urge reflection upon it, by attributing it to the best of creation (ﷺ), so He said: ﴿so you see it﴾; that is: so, as a consequence of its drying, which is the intensity of its swelling in its growth after completion, by the appointing of cessation: that you see it ﴿yellowed﴾; beginning to dry after that blossom, splendour and freshness. And since the context is to show complete power, He expressed it with making, attributing it to Him - glorified is He - unlike the verse of al-Hadid, in which He expressed it with being, because the context there is that the worldly life is non-existence; so He said: ﴿Then He makes it debris﴾; that is: broken, crumbled, decayed.

When this wondrous pattern was complete, which indicates without doubt to everyone who sees it that its Doer is able to restore, after annihilation, whatever He wills, just as He was able to bring into existence from non-existence and to grant existence to all that was not - He said, by way of emphasis, to alert that their denial is extreme foolishness and stubbornness: ﴿Indeed in that﴾; that is: in this arrangement in this manner; ﴿is a reminder﴾; that is: a great and clear reminder of resurrection and what follows it; for the plant is like the human: it is water, then it is formed into a human being, then it comes forth as an infant, then it becomes a youth, then a man of middle age, then an old man, then decrepit, then dust crumbled in the earth; then He gathers it and brings it forth as the water brought forth the plant; ﴿for those of understanding﴾; that is: the very pure intellects, as He alerted to by the specific address at the beginning of this section to the one upon whom this Book was sent down; as for others, and those who did not follow him in excellence, they are like the beasts of cattle.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 22:

Since what he established through this (the verse) is a matter that the listener would consider apparent, and since it was fitting that some who stop at the outward meanings would deny that it is specific to the people of intellect (ulu al-albab), he gave a consequence for that denial in His saying: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam...?﴾. That is, the One who has complete power and all-encompassing knowledge. ﴿Opened to Islam﴾: that is, to submission to the proof. So his heart was soft, and he submitted to faith and was guided to the inner reality of this proof. ﴿So he is﴾: that is, as a consequence of the submission of his outward and inner being to the caller, he was ﴿upon a light﴾: that is, a great clarity, with a Book by which he takes, by which he gives, and to which he returns in every matter. It has risen above him, so he is as one who rides it, directing it wherever he wills. He increased the explanation of the greatness of his guidance by turning the speech to the locus of beneficence (p-486), saying: ﴿from his Lord﴾: that is, the One who is beneficent to him by His beneficence in his submission. So there is good news for him. ﴿He is upon a straight path.﴾ Like one whose breast is made narrow and constricted, so his heart is hard, so he is stumbling in darkness. ﴿Woe to him!﴾ This was the original form, but it was said instead: ﴿Woe to those whose hearts are hardened﴾: that is, because of the narrowness of their breasts. He increased the explanation of what they were afflicted with of great hardness by turning the speech to the Name that indicates all the Most Beautiful Names and the Sublime Attributes, saying: ﴿from the remembrance of Allah﴾. For whoever's hardness begins with what hearts find tranquility in and skins soften to, from praise of the One who combines all attributes of perfection, is harder than stone.

Since whoever is marked with this disgrace is the greatest of people in loss of bargain, his description produced His saying (exalted is He): ﴿Those are in clear error﴾: that is, the far-removed and hateful ones; ﴿clear﴾ in itself, its matter made manifest to everyone. So the verse is of the type of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which something is omitted at each of two places, the opposite of each being indicated by the other): first it mentioned the expansion and the light, indicating the omission of its opposite second; and second it mentioned the woe for the hardened and the error, indicating the omission of its opposite first.

Al-Bayhaqi related in al-Shu'ab, and al-Baghawi through the path of al-Tha'labi, and al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi through another route, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse. He said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, how is the expansion of their breasts?" He said: "When the light enters the heart, it expands and widens" (p-487). We said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the sign of that?" He said: "Turning in repentance to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before death descends."

Ustadh Abu al-Qasim al-Qushayri said: The light that comes from Him (exalted is He) is the light of the lawa'ih (luminous illuminations), through stars of knowledge; then the light of the lawami' (flashing lights), through the clarity of understanding; then the light of the muhadara (presence), through the increments of certainty; then the light of the mukashafa (unveiling), through the manifestation of the Attributes; then the light of the mushahada (witnessing), through the appearance of the Essence; then the lights of the samadiyya (the state of being the Eternal Refuge), through the realities of tawhid (divine oneness). At that point there is no finding, no seeking, no nearness, and no distance. Not at all; rather, He is Allah, the One, the Subduer. This is as it has been said: The believer, by the strength of his intellect, necessitates his independence in his knowledge until it appears. From it comes the completeness of his firm grip on the brightness of his insight. Then, when a flash of the authority of the gnostic knowledges appears to him, those lights become moonlit. When the lights of tawhid appear, they consume that whole collection. When the dawn became clear, its light absorbed the lights of those stars with its own light.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 23:**

Since it is extremely unlikely that a heart would harden in the face of the remembrance of God, God explained this and depicted it in the greatest of remembrances. For it was "a guidance and a healing for those who believe, while for those who do not believe there is deafness in their ears and blindness in their eyes." So He said, exalting the One who sent it down by making the Greatest Name the subject and building the sentence upon it: ﴿God﴾, that is, the Doer (al-Fa''al) of whatever He wills, who possesses all the aspects of greatness and encompasses all the attributes of perfection, ﴿has sent down﴾, that is, gradually, for instruction and to answer every doubt, ﴿the best of speech﴾ and the greatest of remembrances. Had He not been the One who sent it down, it would not have been the best, and no one would have been able, even for a single day, to produce anything like it. He substituted for "the best" the phrase ﴿a Book﴾, that is, one that gathers every good, ﴿consistent﴾ (mutashabihan), that is, in its miraculous eloquence and its beautiful admonition, with no discrepancy in it at all, in wording or in meaning, even though it was revealed in installments over more than twenty years. As for human speech, discrepancy is unavoidable in it, even if a long time is spent refining it, whether its time of composition is unified or not, and variation among what differs over time is greater. He did not say "mushtabihan" (ambiguous), lest it be thought that all of it is unclear in its indication, and that is not something to be praised.

Since it is divided into surahs, verses and sections, He described it with the plural in His words ﴿repeated (mathani)﴾. Mathani is the plural of mathna, a form of maf'al derived from tathniyah, in the sense of repetition, that is, its stories, admonitions, rulings and wisdoms are repeated, varying in their modes of expression according to aspects of wisdom, and differing in the manner of clarifying their indications, with no difference at all in the underlying meaning. It is never tiresome through its repetition, its recurrent recitation, its contemplation, or its consideration. Moreover, everything in it comes in pairs of a thing and its opposite: the believer and the disbelieving, the obedient and the disobedient, general mercy and special mercy, Paradise and Hellfire, bliss and wretchedness, misguidance and guidance, prosperity and adversity, glad tidings and warnings. Thus whenever a reward is stated explicitly for any of these, its opposite is also alluded to, so it is mentioned twice, encouraging or deterring twice. It is also possible that the underlying construction is "its repetitions being consistent (mutashabihatan mathaniyah)," in which case the accusative is a specification (tamyiz). The benefit of repetition is that souls are most averse to words of admonition and advice; if they are not repeated to them, returning to the beginning again and again, they do not take root in the soul and do not do their work. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) used to repeat his words three times or more.

Since repetition causes tedium, He mentioned that among the distinguishing features of this Book is that it delights with repetition and grows sweeter, even if it is recited during the hours of the night and the edges of the day. So He said ﴿shiver (taqsha''irru)﴾, that is, it quivers, gathers, and contracts with intense contraction, from al-qash', which is the dry hide. The letter (the ''ayn/ta' augmentation, i.e., the extra letter) was added to increase the meaning, and the letter of repetition was chosen to indicate intensification in it. That it is the letter of development (tatwir) is even more fitting. ﴿From it, the skins﴾, that is, the outer surfaces of the bodies, ﴿of those who fear﴾, that is, who fear intensely and experience a pleasure that produces reverence and awe, and that is the cause of it. He increased their praise by saying that they fear the Benevolent One, so when the attributes of majesty are mentioned they fear even more. Therefore he turned the speech to the description of benevolence, saying ﴿their Lord﴾, that is, the One who nurtures them and is benevolent to them, because their hearts are stirred. Al-Tabarani narrated from al-''Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the skin of a servant shivers from the fear of Allah, his sins fall away." It is also reported from Ibn ''Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that he passed by a man from the people of Iraq who had collapsed. He said, "What is the matter with this one?" It was said, "When the Qur'an is recited to him and he hears the remembrance of Allah, he collapses." Ibn ''Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) said, "We fear Allah and we do not collapse! Indeed, Satan enters into the inside of one of them. This was not the practice of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

﴿Then softens﴾, that is, extends and becomes soft and at ease. He mentioned first what explicitly states the shivering, which necessarily implies dryness, and delayed the hearts, distancing them from what might suggest dryness and thus imply hardness. So He said ﴿their skins﴾, because they return after a while to hope, however firm their hardness may be, ﴿and their hearts﴾. Mentioning them is to indicate the renewed softness of the hearts along with the skins, which points to the shivering of the hearts together with them from the intensity of fear, since fear occurs only in the heart. The secret of omitting explicit mention of that was to keep it free from any mention that might suggest hardness.

Since the heart is extremely turbulent and changeable, He indicated its being preserved by His all-penetrating command and His dazzling greatness, by the transitive use of ﴿to﴾ (ila), so that the meaning is: calm and tranquil ﴿to the remembrance of Allah﴾, that is, the Lord of majesty and generosity. The basis of His remembrance is hope, because His mercy precedes His wrath. He made the pronoun explicit in place of the implicit reference to "the best of speech," lest it be thought that the pronoun refers to the Lord, which would become a doubt for the Unitarians (ittihadiyya) or others among the people of innovation. He did not say "to the speech" or "to the Book," for example, but turned to what is known to be His remembrance, glorified is He, so as to make it more magnificent in its majesty. He further increased its grandeur by turning the speech away from the description that requires benevolence to the name that encompasses majesty and generosity.

Since what was mentioned of these effects is wondrous, He indicated its greatness by saying, by way of inference, ﴿That﴾, that is, this great, strange matter of the speech sent down, and of contraction and expansion, ﴿is the guidance of Allah﴾, that is, of the One from whom nothing is withheld, ﴿by which He guides whom He wills.﴾ Whomever Allah guides, no one can misguide, and whomever He misguides, no one can guide. Thus their skins are not affected because of the hardness of their hearts, so it is guidance for some and misguidance for others. ﴿And whomever Allah misguides﴾, that is, the Supreme King, encompassing everything, misguides him with a firmly established misguidance in his heart, by what the grammatical construction implies, so that the temporary misguidance is removed, ﴿then he has no guide﴾, because no one can repel His command or revoke His judgment, since He is the One in His dominion, and He has no partner. The verse is an instance of ihtibak (a rhetorical figure in which elements are omitted from each part and each part indicates the omitted counterpart of the other). It first mentions the unrestricted scope of His command in guidance, as an indication that its counterpart in misguidance is omitted, and then the closing of the door of guidance to whomever He misguides, as an indication that its counterpart is omitted regarding whomever He has guided. This verse is a decisive refutation of the Qadariyya (who deny divine predestination).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 24:

When he had completed the denunciation of those who made equals (with God), he explained who had had his breast expanded (for Islam) and who had a constricted breast, and what followed each of them, and he concluded that the first is guided and the second is astray. He began to explain what belongs to each of the two, in a somewhat scattered arrangement, also in the style of denunciation. He said, indicating that misguidance is the cause of punishment and guidance is the cause of bliss, and omitting here the one given bliss, whose bliss was caused by the softness of his heart, just as he omitted the hard-hearted one in the verse of al-Sharh (94), whose hardness caused him punishment, so that the two verses correspond and the two expressions balance: ﴿Is then he...﴾. He used the singular with the word "man" (who), lest it be thought that the great faces (are meant). So he said: ﴿...who shields﴾, and he indicated that his hand, with which it is customary for a person to shield himself from fears, is shackled, by his saying: ﴿with his face﴾, which used to protect him from fears and guard him against them, by making it (and it is the noblest of his limbs) a shield with which he shields others from his body; ﴿from the evil of the punishment﴾, that is, its severity and its adversity, because he followed his own self in its desires until his heart hardened and his mind was corrupted; ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾, because he will be thrown into the Fire headfirst, and he will be bound, having no limb at all with which to ward off his face; there will be on his neck a rock of sulphur like a great mountain, and he will be dragged in the Fire on his face. (Is he then) like one who is safe from punishment? For he receives bliss with his heart and his body.

Since absolute rebuke and reproach is (grammatically) "inclined", he built the verb in the passive, saying: ﴿And it will be said﴾ to him, (the original form being so); but he made it general, and attached the judgment to it, and used the plural as a warning that their multitude did not avail them anything: (p-493) so he said: ﴿to the wrongdoers﴾, that is, those who abandoned the path of guidance, followed desire, went astray and led others astray; ﴿Taste what﴾, that is, the recompense of what; ﴿you used to earn﴾, that is, what you considered a gain and fruit of your deeds and conduct. It was also said to the people of bliss: "Be content of soul and cool of eye, as a reward for what you used to do." So the verse is of the (rhetorical device of) ihtibak: he mentioned the interrogative first, as an indication of the omission of its complement second, and what is said to the wrongdoer second, as an indication of what is said to the just first.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 25:

When He had mentioned what has been prepared for them of the Hereafter, and they, during the period of their disbelief, were like dumb animals that look only at the immediate particulars before them, He warned them by what they were doing in this world. He said, by way of a fresh statement (istint'af) in answer to one who asks: "Are they then punished in this world?": ﴿Those before them denied, so the punishment came upon them﴾; and He indicated the closeness of the time of those punished to their own time by introducing the preposition (al-jarr), so He said: ﴿from before them﴾; that is, like Saba' (Sheba) and the people of Tubba' (the Tubba' kings of Yemen), and their likes. ﴿So the punishment came to them﴾; and their affair was easy for Us. And He indicated that their caution did not avail them, by His saying: ﴿from where﴾; that is, from a direction; ﴿they did not perceive﴾; that a punishment would come from it. He made its coming to them from their place of safety, so that this would be more painful for the one punished, and more evident of (His) power, for with Him (exalted is He) it is equal whether the punishment comes from a direction that is expected, or from a direction from which no evil at all is expected to come, let alone that by which they were seized. Rather, from it nothing is expected but good.

(p-494) When He had made clear their folly and extreme stupidity in hastening on the punishment mockingly, He consequently rebuked those who did not take warning from their condition, saying: ﴿So Allah made them taste disgrace﴾; i.e., He Who has no one to turn back His command; ﴿disgrace﴾; i.e., the humiliation resulting from exposure; and ﴿the great punishment﴾ for what they intended of disgracing the Messengers by denying them; ﴿in the life of this world﴾; i.e., the hasty and base life.

Since awaiting relief is something that consoles, he said, informing that their punishment is lasting, by way of ascent to what is more severe, and emphasizing it because of their denial of it: ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is surely greater﴾; i.e., that to which they passed by death and to which they will return by resurrection; ﴿greater﴾ than the punishment with which He destroyed them in this world, and more disgraceful. So the verse is of ihtibak (the rhetorical device of omission): He mentioned disgrace first, as a proof of its being intended second, and "greater" second, as a proof of "great" first. Its secret is the aggravation of the matter against them by combining disgrace and punishment, for what they did to His Messengers, peace and blessings be upon them, unlike what comes in "Fussilat" (Surah 41), since its context is the challenge to Oneness (tawhid). Oneness, because of the abundance of its proofs, its distance from doubts, the greatness of the One characterized by it, and the fact that nothing affects Him, the mere punishment is sufficient to deter the disbeliever who denies it.

Since whoever knows that his act brings about a penalty refrains from it, and they do not refrain nor take warning, he said: ﴿If only they knew﴾; i.e., if they had any knowledge at all, they would have known that it is greater, so they would have taken warning and believed; but they have no knowledge whatsoever. Rather, they are like cattle; nay, they are more astray in way, because particular perceptions do not benefit them as they benefit the rest of the animals. For the sheep sees the wolf and flees from it, perceiving that there is enmity between them, by what Allah placed in the wolf's nature of eating the likes of it; but these people see what befell the likes of them of punishment, due to their denial of the Messengers, yet they do not flee from it toward belief.

When He, glory be to Him, mentioned the condition of the earlier peoples as an admonition to the Arabs, it was as if it had been said (turning the speech to the manifestation of majesty, to remind them of the favor contained in forbearance, because the condition of such people calls for hastening the punishment and promptly unleashing wrath): "We have set forth for you their condition as a parable for your condition, so that you may take heed by it, for parables convey hidden meanings and make them seem as though they were perceived by the senses and witnessed." Then He joined to it His words, emphasizing their denial that the Qur'an contains a sufficient clarification, and their claim that it is merely poetry, soothsaying, and sorcery: ﴿And We have certainly set forth﴾, by virtue of the majesty We possess. Since this was within the context of distinguishing between the god-fearing and others, from the beginning of the surah, when He said: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient⦆ [Az-Zumar: 9], until He concluded with His words: ﴿Then is one who shields with his face⦆ [Az-Zumar: 24], and founded all of that upon the origination of creation from a single soul, the concern in this context was with the addressees more so; so He put forward His words ﴿for mankind⦆, meaning: in general, because the message of your Messenger is general.

Since the one who seeks to make difficulties is abundant, He identified the one spoken of by the demonstrative, which is the most definite of the definite forms, and made it something used to express nearness, as an indication that when the Messenger ﷺ brought it, it stripped away hearts and filled them, so that nothing else is present in them, and even if the obstinate one says otherwise, his speech is falsehood, slander, sin, and transgression. So He said: ﴿in this Qur'an⦆, meaning: the one that comprises every knowledge. And since His words, glory be to Him, cannot be exhausted, and His wonders cannot be counted or bounded, and this was within the context of marveling at their hesitation, He said: ﴿of every kind of parable⦆, meaning: a parable whose striking is sufficient for clarification, to establish the conclusive proof. Then He explained the purpose of the striking by His words: ﴿so that they may remember⦆, meaning: so that their condition after the striking of it becomes the condition of one whose remembrance is hoped for by what has been set forth for him, of what he knows in the cosmos, in himself or in the horizons, a clear and manifest remembrance, by what the manifestation guides to, so that he may be admonished by those parables delivered in the finest speech, arranged with what suits them of forms and figures of exposition and of the clearest proof.

When this was at its utmost in nobility, that nobility was further emphasized by a qualifying circumstantial phrase (ḥāl) that points to the intensity of their obstinacy. This is called *muwaṭṭi'a* (a "preparatory" qualifier), because the true circumstantial phrase is what follows it, namely His saying: ﴿a Qur'an﴾; that is, the thing struck as a parable is a Qur'an comprising everything that is needed. It is also permissible for the accusative to be one of praise: ﴿in Arabic﴾, proceeding according to the rules of their own language in its composition, in its breadth and clarity, and in the fact that a single word in it admits many meanings. How much more so when it is combined with other words and becomes speech?

Since a thing may be straight in actuality while being crooked in potential, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿without any crookedness﴾; that is, it is not ascribed to any kind of crookedness, and crookedness is not part of its nature. Thus it is not valid for it to be crooked at all, in any part of its arrangement or in its meaning, whether by contradiction or otherwise, as in the verse of *al-Kahf* where it is the same. In the use of *'iwaj* (crookedness), which is specific to meanings, there is a clarification that the attribute belongs to it in actual reality. Therefore it is more eloquent than *ghayra mu'waj* (not crooked), because the latter may admit the meaning of its people [i.e., those who are called crooked] in a metaphorical sense.

Since reminding by admonition, because it is more eloquent in exhortation, is necessarily a driving force for the intelligent person toward the fear that causes salvation, He said: ﴿so that they may be mindful of God﴾; that is, so that their state after the remembrance arising from the reminder would be the state of one for whom it is hoped that he will place between himself and the anger of God a protective barrier.

[p. 497]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 29:

When He, glorified is He, had established the clear proof of the great disparity between the one who is devoutly obedient (qanit) during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, calling upon Allah while sincere to Him in religion, and the one who calls upon others as equals to Allah; and had concluded with the striking of parables; and since parables are clearest in what is intended of states, He said, drawing attention to their greatness, by turning the speech away from the manifestation of greatness to the Greatest Name, the one that comprises all attributes of perfection: ﴿Allah sets forth﴾; that is, the Greatest King, the one singular in attributes of perfection; ﴿a parable﴾ for these two men; even though no person of intellect doubts that the polytheist cannot approach the one who is sincere, let alone that the polytheist would be greater, as the polytheists claim. And since the male is stronger than the female and more knowledgeable of the places of benefit and harm; and since his being mature is greater for his strength and firmer for his resolve, so that he is more protective of himself against shame and more effective in repelling injustice from his side and more defensive of his sanctuary; He said, explaining the parable and pointing to the rebuke of the disbelievers and their contentment for themselves with what they would not accept for their own selves, even the lowest of slaves: ﴿a man in whom﴾; that is, exclusively. And since their objects of worship, being among the created things, are many in their likenesses and counterparts, He expressed them with the plural of multiplicity, saying: ﴿partners﴾; outwardly among the idols, and inwardly among desires and appetites. He described the partners by His saying: ﴿quarrelling﴾; that is, disagreeing, difficult, pulling against one another, with bad character and narrowness of it, and the ugliness of partnership; so none of them is content with fairness, and he cannot please them at all. ﴿And a man belonging wholly﴾, that is, free of dispute, ﴿to one man﴾, so there is no partnership for anyone else in him, and no connection at all; so he is more worthy of being able to please him, with his ease from the pulling of partners. This is according to the reading of al-Makki and al-Basri; and according to the reading of the rest, with the alif omitted and the lam fathah, it is a description by the verbal noun, for emphasis.

When the matter became entirely clear in it, He said: ﴿Are the two equal?﴾; that is, the two men, one of them being equal to the other in any respect whatsoever, even with utmost effort and care? And since equality was vague, He said: ﴿in description﴾; that is, in terms of the parable; meaning, are their parable equal, i.e., does one single parable encompass them, such that they would be equal? It is a specification (tamyiz) transferred in origin from the subject. The answer to this rhetorical question of denial is certainly: no, they are not equal. Rather, the parable of the man who is wholly at peace is in the utmost excellence, and so is what he represents, namely the devoutly obedient, sincere one; and the parable of the man in whom disputing has occurred is in the utmost ugliness, and so is what he represents, namely the one who calls upon equals.

Since by this parable struck for the two men the lowness of the one who shares (partners) was known, namely the one who calls upon equals, and the loftiness of the one at peace, namely the devoutly obedient, there became evident, without doubt, the worthlessness of those who share, and the majesty of the Singular One, who is Allah. So He certainly produced His saying: ﴿All praise﴾; that is, the encompassing of attributes of perfection, ﴿is for Allah﴾, to whom there is no equal, which everyone knows, because of the manifestness of what He has of the evident signs; so it is not valid that He should have a partner. ﴿But most of them﴾; that is, of the people, ﴿do not know﴾, because they act in ways that do not befit this knowledge, so they associate others with Him, whether openly or secretly. It is also permissible to say: all perfection belongs to Him, so those who turn to other than Him do not turn at all as those with knowledge; rather they have no knowledge at all, and they are the ones with open shirk. As for the people of hidden shirk, they, though they have some knowledge, it is not complete.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 30:

Since the one who is sound (al-salim) is an example for him (ﷺ) and his followers, and the other is an example for the opponents, and since He (Glorified is He) had established their ignorance, and the ignorant person is possessive of his zeal, his refusal of the truth to which he is summoned, and his partisanship:

"The ignorant are enemies of the people of knowledge."

So for this reason, reflecting on their affair, and on what it leads to, namely withdrawing from the followers and attacking them with harm, especially since they are more numerous than the people of knowledge, leads to regret and severe anxiety. Thus it was a matter of which one would say: "So what should he do?" In reality, only one who thought the affliction would last forever should have been troubled. (Exalted is He) said, consoling him, comforting him, and reassuring him, in a context of emphasis (ta'kid, emphasis), as an alert that whoever is anxious has a state that calls for denying that the emphasis is cut off: ﴿Indeed you﴾. He singled out (ﷺ), because when the address is to the head, it is more effective for his followers. So every place where the address is to the followers, but (ﷺ) is singled out for the address to the exclusion of them, then they are in reality the ones addressed, in a more eloquent manner.

Since a possible thing (mumkin) has of itself nothing but non-existence, He said: ﴿dead﴾, meaning now, because this is a necessary attribute, unlike "dying" (ma'it). The meaning is: be like the dead before the washer, for you will soon be at rest from what you suffer from their hostilities, and you will return to your Lord to reward you for your obedience to Him. ﴿And indeed they﴾, meaning all the servants, your followers and others, ﴿are dying﴾, so what they are engaged in of contention and of ease and plenty will come to an end.

When the complete healing comes only through exacting vengeance and the humbling of the wrongdoer, He said, indicating by the particle of delay the duration of the barzakh (the intermediate state between death and resurrection), emphasizing because of their denial of resurrection, let alone retaliation (qisas), and addressing them directly after the third person: ﴿Then indeed you﴾; that is, O servants, all of you, for every person is accountable for himself and for others (p-501) whether he upheld God's right regarding them, or you and they, by way of giving precedence to the addressee, even though it is one person, because of His greatness, over those who are absent. He strengthened the meaning with His words ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾, presenting it as something beyond dispute, and made clear that that state differs from this state because the causes have ceased. With His words, turning the speech to the attribute of nurturing, which entitles Him to bestow favor on the obedient and justice on the disobedient: ﴿before your Lord﴾; that is, the One who nurtures you through creation and provision. Therefore it is not fitting in wisdom that He leave you so that some of you transgress against others without reckoning, as is observed. Even the least intelligent of you does not accept this among his slaves whom God has given him as property in a weak ownership, or whom he has placed in authority over them in a shaky authority. How then of one above him? How then of the wise? ﴿You will dispute﴾; that is, you will press hard in contention, so that He may take the hand of the oppressed, avenge him against the oppressor, and recompense each for what he did. As for evil, a bad deed is met with its like, and no one is wronged even by the weight of an atom or less. As for good, a good deed is multiplied tenfold, and beyond that, by what no one but Him knows. Therefore it is never fitting for the oppressed to imagine that his distress will last forever and that his hand will not be taken, so that he falls short in works, inclines toward some fear and dread. Rather, he should rejoice in what multiplies his reward, and be pleased with what eases his reckoning, and occupy himself with what saves his soul on the Day of Meeting, when people will be in two groups, and not occupy himself with what is not (p-502) part of the purification of the abode of turbidity from its troubles, and the bottom of defilement from its filth and impurities, for permanence in it is impossible in any state of affairs.

Al-Qushayri said: He (ﷺ) announced his own death, and announced to the Muslims that they too would die. So they freed themselves from their mourning, and in custom there is no condolence after three days. Whoever has not freed himself from mourning for his own self, and from the various kinds of his grief and anxieties, has no share in this discourse. When a heart is emptied of the discourse of its own self, and of existence in its entirety, then at that time it finds good from its Lord. This discourse is only after their passing away from themselves.

One of them recited, meaning in the language of the state according to what we have presented:

"I wrote to you on a night after my death,
and I did not know that after my death I would be writing."

End of quotation. It is well known that when they cause their souls to die, their spirits come to life, their breasts are expanded, the powers of their hearts are revived, their knowledge widens, their understanding is illuminated, and the realities of matters are disclosed to them. So they speak from direct witnessing: "People are asleep; when they die, they awaken."

When He - glory be to Him - informed them that they had set up rivals to God, and made known that they were liars in this, they were disbelievers, concealers of the truth, and that He does not guide one who is a liar and a great disbeliever. He also informed them that there must be a contest between Him - glory be to Him - and the one who calls them to account before Him, because in wisdom it is not permissible to leave them neglected, as is established in the intellects, present in the primordial natures, and known through observation of their conditions. So He bestows favour upon the oppressed and takes vengeance on the oppressor. The liar in even the smallest matters is an oppressor, and more oppressive than him is the one who lies against the great, and the most oppressive of oppressors is the one who lies against God. He - exalted is He - said, as a consequence of what preceded: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who lies against God and denies the truth when it has come to him?﴾ That is, "more unjust than them", which is what the original structure would be. But He said ﴿than one who lies﴾ to generalise and to attach the judgement to the attribute, so that he disbelieves by concealing the established truth and displaying what has no reality.

Since lying is extremely ugly in itself, how much more so when it is directed at the great, as already mentioned? How much more so when they are kings? How much more so when it is directed at the King of kings? He turned the speech to the manifest form of the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam, the Greatest Name of God) to draw attention to this, saying ﴿against God﴾. That is, the One whose is the majesty as His cloak and greatness as His garment; whoever disputes with Him in either of these two, He breaks him. So in his lie he claims that He - glory be to Him - has rivals, partners and children.

Since the occurrence of the Reckoning on the Day of Resurrection is true, because it is bound to occur, occurring in a manner that matches the report about it, and because it is known that nothing else is fitting in wisdom, and it is known that the least of creatures would not be content to leave his servants neglected, how much more so the Creator? So the report about it is true, because certain knowledge has come about that it matches that reality. He said ﴿and denies the truth﴾, that is, he brings about denial of everything that informs him, ﴿the truth﴾, that is, the report that God is one and that He will raise the creatures for recompense, each of these two matching the reality, by the evidences that point to this which are observed, ﴿when it has come to him﴾, that is, without hesitation and without examining any proof, as is the habit of the obstinate. ﴿Those are the disbelievers.﴾ For them is what will harm them of the punishment of Hell. ﴿That is the recompense of the evildoers.﴾

Since it has been established, as clear as the sun, that it is not befitting in the intellect of any sensible person to leave creation neglected, and the Day of Religion is therefore certain, and since the meaning of this interrogative of denial (al-istifham al-inkari, the rhetorical question expressing denial) is the negation of what it governs, its translation is: "There is no one more lying than them." It was the usage of the language, in applying this negation to the form ﴿af'al﴾ (the elative pattern, meaning "more...", as in akthar, "more lying"), to affirm the meaning of the ﴿af'al﴾, so the meaning is that they are the most lying of creatures. Thus the implied reading is: "Is not this liar who denies a sensible person who fears that God, who created him, will call him to account? Is not God, who is characterised by all the attributes of perfection, calling His servants to account, just as each of the creatures calls to account whoever is under his hand? Does He not imprison the oppressor among them in the house of His vengeance, just as the least of rulers does? Is not the house of His vengeance Hell, which those who enter it meet with scowling and frowning?" He connected to this his saying: ﴿Is there not in Hell a dwelling﴾, that is, the Fire, which those who enter it meet with frowning and scowling, just as they met the truth and its people; ﴿a dwelling﴾, that is, a prepared place of abode for remaining in it, as an obligation upon them? That is what the original structure would be. But He said, generalising and giving the cause through the attribute, making clear that lying is disbelief, that is, concealment of the truth and display of what has no reality, and denying the truth is likewise: ﴿for the disbelievers﴾, that is, those who concealed their lying, clothing it in the garments of truth, and concealed the truth that they denied. [p. 505] That is the recompense of the evildoers, because they are not God-fearing. Thus He - glory be to Him - established this premise as evidence for all those premises.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 33:

When He, glorified be He, mentioned the wrongdoers who lie, He mentioned their opposites, those who dispute with them before their Lord, and they are the good-doers who speak the truth. So He said: ﴿And he who﴾; that is, the group who ﴿brought the truth﴾; that is, the report that corresponds to reality, so he ﴿affirmed Allah's (word)﴾. Its definiteness (ta'rif) indicates its perfection, and it points out that bringing it is their habit; they do not intentionally tell a lie. ﴿And confirmed it﴾; that is, every truth he heard and for which evidence was established. He is not, by his stubbornness, an enemy of what he does not know; rather, he rejects everything he has not heard. So who is more just than him? Because he affirmed Allah's (word) and confirmed the truth when it came to him and persevered in it. Perhaps the pronoun was made singular to indicate the scarcity of those described with this quality of truthfulness. This group is the Messengers and their followers, and for this reason piety is restricted to them. So He said, indicating with the plural their greatness though they are few: ﴿Those are﴾; that is, those of lofty rank; ﴿they are﴾; that is, exclusively; ﴿the God-fearing (al-muttaqun)﴾, those who shunned wrongdoing. So there is no path for Hell over them, nor is there for them therein any abode or resting place; rather, the Garden is their abode. Is there not in the Garden an abode for the God-fearing? The verse is an instance of ihtibak (interlocking ellipsis): He first mentioned the abode in Hell (p-506), as evidence for the omission of its opposite second; and piety second, as evidence for the omission of its opposite first. Its secret is that He mentioned the most painful of what the criminal has of disbelief and evil recompense, and the most pleasing of what the Muslim has, namely the restriction of piety to him, the mention of his most beloved reward, and an indication of his firm rootedness in good-doing. There is another ihtibak in the verses: He mentioned lying and denial first, as evidence for truthfulness and confirmation second; and piety and its recompense and what follows it second, as evidence for its opposite first. Its secret is that He mentioned, in the portion concerning the evildoer, the most painful form of lying and denial, in its most ugly settings, especially among the Arabs; and the most pleasing, in the portion concerning the good-doer, of uprightness of nature and good recompense.

When He praised them for their piety, He said, answering the question of what their reward would be, turning the speech to the description of excellence (iḥsān) to make known the greatness of His honouring them: ﴿For them is whatever they wish, with their Lord﴾. That is: His will for them renews itself whenever they wish it; ﴿with their Lord﴾, that is, the One who is good to them and gentle with them in this world and in the Hereafter, because they submitted to Him in the first life regarding what He willed, so He submits to them in the next life regarding what they wish. Since this is the greatest of rewards, He praised it in a manner that clarified its cause and made its generality obligatory, so He said: ﴿That﴾, that is, the great reward, ﴿is the recompense of the doers of good (muḥsinūn)﴾, that is, of everyone who is characterised by iḥsān, just as they were characterised by it through taqwā (piety). So Allah, glory be to Him, loves him as He loved them, and he becomes the hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. (p-507)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 35:

Since the intelligent person is one who gives priority in every matter to what is most important and then to what is next in importance, and so distinguishes between the two goods and follows the better, and between the two evils and avoids the worse, the doer of good (muhsin) is one who places his greatest sins before his eyes and works to demolish them. For this reason He gave the cause of the good-doing in His saying: ﴿so that He may expiate﴾, meaning, He may cover over with a great covering, as if He had said: "...the good-doers who did good for this purpose." It is also permissible that the causal clause relates to the reward. He expressed it with the Greatest Name, ﴿Allah﴾, drawing attention away from the attribute of good-doing, indicating the great effort in the deed, and announcing that He does not grant forgiveness to whomever He wills except through absolute freedom of action. So He said: ﴿Allah﴾, meaning the One whose majesty and beauty the good-doer has set before his eyes, so that he is absorbed in His attributes, seeking His pleasure, and worships Him as if he sees Him. By their acknowledgment of error and their intention to expiate, which was established by the fact that their deed weighed on them, He said: ﴿the worst of what they did﴾, the deed, ﴿which they committed﴾, and they repented of it through remorse, abandonment, and resolve not to return to it. It is known that when the greater sin is erased, the lesser is erased with it, because good deeds remove evil deeds. How excellent is the insight and sincerity of the people of insight, both in public and in private!

When He informed of purification from the filth of evil deeds, He followed it with information about illumination by the lights of good, so He said: ﴿and reward them with their reward﴾ (p-508), meaning, that which He graciously promised them.

Since He (exalted be He) increases righteous deeds and nurtures them, He added the preposition in the reward, to inform that He makes all righteous deeds like the best of them, so He said: ﴿with the best﴾. Since the aim of this surah is more specific than the aim of surah "al-Nahl," and since "alladhi" and "man" are less ambiguous than "ma," He said: ﴿of what﴾, meaning, the deed which, and it is like the first, of the type of the attribution of a thing to that of which it is a part, like "a silver ring." He indicated their constancy in good by expressing it with the verb "kana" (was) and the present tense, so He said: ﴿they used to do﴾, renewing it time after time, because it is in their natures, and they are deeply engaged in practising it. Whoever in this world is a good-doer at some time, worshipping Allah as if he sees Him, will in the Hereafter see Him at every moment. Al-Qushayri said: "Then it is necessary that for the best of deeds there be the best of rewards, and the best of rewards is the vision (of Allah), so it must be continuous. This is a strong inference."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 36:

When it was understood from His saying, ﴿And he who denies the truth when it comes to him﴾ [al-Zumar: 32], that the polytheists were denying him, and it is in the nature of human beings to be concerned with such matters, especially when the denier is numerous and powerful; and it was established that He, glory be to Him, is the Just Judge between the disputants and others, in this world and the Hereafter; and it became binding on every listener to affirm the Hereafter; and He gave glad tidings to the good-doers and warned the evildoers; and it was known that they were threatening him with their gods just as they threatened him with their God; His saying was most fitting in every way, affirming sufficiency to the utmost degree of affirmation and denying its negation in the utmost degree of denial (p-509): ﴿Is not Allah sufficient?﴾ That is: the one who gathers all the attributes of greatness, described with the descriptions of perfection of majesty and beauty. He emphasized the intended meaning by the addition of the particle (bi, "with") to the word "sufficient", because of their firm conviction that they would prevail. So He said: ﴿for His servant?﴾ He realized the subject through the idafah (genitive construction) in His saying ﴿His servant﴾, that is, the one devoted to Him, who has not associated anything with Him at all, as has already been mentioned in the parable, against those who denied him and intended him harm; so He will help him against them, until He makes His religion manifest and raises his affair, and suffices him from needing anyone else or inclining to anything other than Him, by believing that there is something in His hand that is independent. This does not contradict striving in the means, while holding the belief that they are in the hand of Allah; if He wills, He ties the effects to them, and if He wills, He renders them barren. Rather, striving is more perfect, because the arrangement of means is by the decree of the Wise; so abandoning them contradicts the placement of wisdom. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Ja'far read ﴿ʿibādahu﴾ (his servants) in the plural, meaning the Messenger and his followers.

And since the answer is certainly "Yes, indeed; He suffices whom He wills, while the idols, likened to quarrelling partners, cannot suffice anyone who relies on them," He built upon that a wondrous state of their condition. So He said, marveling at them and mocking them: ﴿And they threaten you﴾; that is, the worshippers of idols, who know that Allah suffices whom He wills, and that the idols have no sufficiency in any way, while the situation is that they threaten you. And since fear is of one who has choice, and if he is rational it is stronger because of his opposition, and it was obvious by necessity that they have no choice, let alone reason (p-510), He said, mocking them, by using the expression used for rational males, because they treat them in worship and other things as if they were rational, although they acknowledge that they have no reason; thus they became a laughingstock and a byword among people: ﴿with those [besides Him]﴾; and He made clear their lowliness by His saying ﴿besides Him﴾, namely their objects of worship, astray from the right path. So they say: "We fear that our gods will afflict you with madness," just as 'Ad said to Hud, peace be upon him: "We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil." The reference to them with the feminine form will come later, as an increase in their reproach.

And since it is a clear truth, as plain as the sun, that what they said is not said by any rational person, and the implicit meaning was: "Allah has misguided them as a humiliation to them, and guided you as an honour to you," He made clear that He, glory be to Him, compelled them to that, so that their misguidance by Him would be a sign, just as His guidance of whomever He guided is a sign. So He said, lightening for him (ﷺ) the burden of his soul's grief over them, and refuting the Qadariyyah: ﴿And whomever Allah misguides﴾; that is, He to whom the whole command belongs, so His command is not turned back; ﴿then he has no guide﴾, because it is He who misguided him; ﴿from among [men]﴾; that is, so lower your grief over them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 37:

﴿And whomever Allah guides, there is no misleader for him﴾; i.e., the One whom nothing ever overpowers; ﴿And whomever Allah guides, there is no misleader for him﴾; so He, glorified is He, guides whomever He wills among them, if He wills.

Since no doubt remained, nor any trace of uncertainty, that the One who guides and misleads is Allah alone, and that He made one single thing a cause for the misguidance of one people, so that their misguidance would outwardly be a reason for retribution, and a guidance for others, so that their guidance would be a cause for blessing, He reached the height of beauty in His saying: ﴿Is not Allah⁠ ⁠Mighty⁠ ⁠and⁠ ⁠Vengeful?⁠﴾; i.e., the One in whose hand is everything; ﴿Mighty⁠﴾; i.e., overpowering in what He wills, in misguiding a people who claim that they have reached the pinnacle of perfection of intellect because of what He guided others through; ﴿Vengeful⁠﴾; i.e., He possesses this attribute, so whoever wills retribution from Him, He empowers against him whatever He wills of that which grieves him and humiliates him, just as when He wills, He blinds him from the brightest of lights and misguides him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 38:

When it became known from these proofs that He, glory be to Him, is the One who disposes of meanings, through His disposal of hearts in guidance and misguidance, and the sense was: "If you put them to this rejecting question, they will surely say, 'Yes'" (ʿaṭafa ʿalayhi), He connected to it the explanation that He is the Creator of essences, just as He is the Owner of meanings and attributes. So He said, undermining their religion by their acknowledgment of two principles, the complete power of His and the complete incapacity of their objects of worship: ﴿And if you ask them﴾, that is, if you say to whichever of them you wish, individually or collectively: ﴿Who created the heavens﴾, that is, with all their vastness, greatness and height; ﴿and the earth﴾, with all its wonders and the benefits it contains; ﴿they will surely say﴾, after having frightened you with their partners, who are themselves part of the creation of the One who sent you, concerning your situation: "﴿Allah﴾", that is, alone, the One who has no namesake and no confusion in any respect in His affair; and shame at contradiction does not prevent them from this, nor does fear of incoherence through conflict.

Since this is perplexing, because it is clear, and they must neither accept nor turn away, it was as if it were said: "So what should I do?" He said: ﴿Say﴾, causing as a consequence of their acknowledgment to Him, glory be to Him, of the entire matter, His saying, establishing the branch after their affirmation of the root, and rebuking them by frightening them with one who has no command of binding or loosing: ﴿Have you considered﴾. Since the sincere questioner should draw the opponent's attention to the point of the matter so that he may awaken from his heedlessness and return from his error, He expressed their objects of worship with the particle for non-rational things, after having previously expressed them with the particle for rational males, as a clarification of their error. So He said, expressing the first object of "raʾayta" (have you considered), and the second being the interrogative clause: ﴿what you invoke﴾, that is, invoking in worship; and He established their distance from being a source of fear by ascribing divinity to them in His saying: ﴿besides Allah﴾, that is, the One who is possessed of majesty and honour; so there is nothing but that it is beneath Him and under His dominion. And since well-being is more frequent than affliction, He indicated it with the particle of doubt, and drew attention to the increase of His greatness, glory be to Him, by repeating the Greatest Name, so He said: ﴿If Allah wills harm for me﴾, that is, the One whose command none can repel. And since averting corruptions takes precedence, He said: ﴿harm﴾, that is, if I obey you in inclining towards them out of fear of them. He went to great lengths in warning them, out of sincere advice to them, so that they might return from the outward appearance of their error, by what was mentioned of their baseness and lowliness, expressed with the feminine, after their lowliness in lacking reason, together with their meanness, and after the mockery of them by expressing them with the particle for rational males. So He said: (p-513) ﴿Can they﴾, that is, these idols which you worship, ﴿be removers﴾ ("kāshifāt"), that is, of it from me, while you acknowledge that they have no creation and that they are created by Allah (Exalted); ﴿of His harm﴾, that is, which has befallen me with it, any kind of removal, so that I might hope from them at the time of my distress; ﴿or if He wills mercy for me﴾, in return for my obedience to Him in His unity and in abandoning what is other than Him of His servants; ﴿can they be withholders﴾ ("mumsikāt"), that is, from me, ﴿of His mercy﴾ (the text reads "rahmatahu"), that is, because of my disobedience to them, any kind of withholding, so that I might obey you out of fear of them. This is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, with tanwīn and the active participle functioning with the object in the accusative, which is the original form of the active participle; and the rest read it with the genitive construction, and there is no benefit other than lightening; and it may be imagined from it that the idols are specifically of this meaning, well known.

Since it is known that they fall silent at this question, because they know the necessary contradiction if they answer falsely, and the invalidity of their religion if they answer truthfully, and since the answer to this is decisively: "No" (lā), whether they speak or remain silent, it becomes clear that there is no disposer in any respect except Allah. Thus the conclusion is His saying: ﴿Say﴾, when you have silenced them: ﴿Sufficient for me is﴾, that is, my sufficiency is ﴿Allah﴾, whom I have singled out for worship, because to Him belongs the entire command, against what they frighten me with and against other than that; ﴿upon Him alone﴾, because to Him belongs all perfection; ﴿let those who would rely [upon Him] rely﴾, that is, those who wish that their affair should prevail over every affair. He commanded him to say it, to make known that their state at this question is the very evident contradiction. (p-514)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 39:

When they persisted with these decisive proofs, these crushing evidences, and these shining demonstrations, which cannot be repelled in any way, they were like cattle, who perceive only particulars at the moment they occur. So he said, admonishing them while also appealing to their sympathy: ﴿Say: O my people﴾; that is: O my kinsfolk, whom I hope for in times of distress, and in whom there is sufficiency for undertaking what they attempt. ﴿Work﴾; that is: act, performing deeds founded upon knowledge; ﴿according to your station﴾; that is: your condition in which you have been established and to which you have clung rigidly, because it is a natural disposition for you, of existence and capability, so that you may perceive the realities of affairs and then move from your base states to lofty stations. Thus it is as if he is pointing out that they are like dumb animals, having no choice; and he is alluding to action, whose foundation is knowledge, and to the station whose place is rigidity, that their deeds contain nothing founded upon knowledge, but are mere chance, with no weight or value. Then he answered whoever among them might say to him: "So what will you do?" with his words: ﴿Indeed, I am working﴾; relying on God's sufficiency for me; I have no regard for anything other than Him, and I fear none but Him; I have no station to which I bind myself in rigidity, rather I stand upon whatever comes from God: if He moves me, I move; and if He commands me otherwise, I comply; and I am awaiting every moment for increase. Then he gave a reason for the words of whoever among them might say: "And what might it come to?" with his saying, signifying that he is confident of his matter, since the one who informed him of it is God: ﴿Then you will know﴾; that is: by a promise that admits no failure.

(p-515) ﴿Whoever will receive﴾, i.e., from us and from you, ﴿a punishment that will disgrace him﴾, by removing from him everything with which he could have found sweetness; ﴿and there will descend upon him﴾, i.e., it will be due at its time, from "ḥalla ʿalayhi al-ḥaqq yaḥillu" (with kasra): i.e., it became obligatory; and "al-dayn" (the debt) became due (ḥāll) when its term arrived; ﴿a lasting punishment﴾, because he remains in his state and persists in his misguidance.

And whoever Allah grants victory, He will elevate him, and transfer him to a great bliss, because of his advancement through the stages of perfection by the commands of the One of Majesty and Beauty. They already knew this in the story of the mockers, and then in the battle of "Badr," for whoever Allah destroyed among them, his destruction became the first of his punishment; and it transferred him with it to the punishment of the barzakh (intermediate state), then the punishment of the Fire. So there is no escape for him from punishment, and no hope for a good return.

When these brides of meanings were unveiled, captivating minds, and the swords of those structures shone forth from the oft-repeated verses, severing necks, and He concluded them with what He concluded with, of the piercing kind of warning, there necessarily followed His saying, explaining the reason for bringing about what He had threatened them with and confirming what they held of denial regarding the content of this report: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down﴾. That is, with what We possess of dazzling greatness and effective command.

Since the intermediary of the King was hidden, He did not repeat it, so He dropped the particle of ultimate purpose, to convey that it is in reality without intermediary, after He had established His intermediary at the beginning of the surah. So He said, joined with the command to worship, indicating the beginning of the state. When firm establishment was achieved, and the Book became his (ﷺ) disposition, and its manifestation in him became a guide for others, He alerted to this by the particle of elevation, and said: ﴿to you﴾. That is, specifically, (p-516) not upon others from the people of this time, because you are, in Our sight, the one purely for Us, apart from the people of the two cities and apart from all the people of the earth. Nothing other than Us has a share in you. ﴿the Book﴾, comprising every good, because it is at the utmost perfection, by what the definite article indicates. ﴿for mankind﴾, in general, because your message is general. ﴿in truth﴾, accompanied by it. No creature can divert any meaning of its meanings from its intended aim, nor any word of its words from its path and limit. Rather, it is inimitable in its meanings, whether present or absent, and in its composition, its words, the names of its surahs, its verses, and all its features. Therefore there must be the occurrence of what it contains of promise and threat.

Since knowledge of this entailed the obligation to hasten to submit to it, for the success of both abodes, His saying (exalted is He) was very fitting, as consolation for him (ﷺ), given the great compassion he had for them, and as a threat to them: ﴿So whoever is guided﴾. That is, obeys the guide. ﴿it is for his own self﴾. That is, his guidance benefits himself specifically. He has nothing in it except the reward of being the cause. ﴿And whoever goes astray﴾. That is, error has come from him by opposing the call of innate nature, then the call of the message, with knowledge and deliberate intent, or by neglecting reflection and laxity. Since it may perhaps occur to someone that the caller would bear, after clarification, a share of the sin of the one who goes astray, and since the context is a threat to those who go astray, He increased the emphasis and said: ﴿then he only goes astray to its harm﴾. That is, you bear none of his error, so let not your soul go to waste in regret over them.

Since the context guided to the implied meaning: "So you are not over them a compeller, to force them (p-517) to guidance," He linked to it His saying: ﴿And you are not﴾. That is, in this state. And for greater care in negating compulsion, He placed the particle of elevation first, and said: ﴿over them a guardian﴾, so that you would protect them from error. For the message to them is for establishing the proof, not because the Messenger has the power to guide them, nor because the sender is incapable of that.

When the agent (wakil) in a matter cannot properly act for another unless he is able to do it by some means, and their being guarded upon guidance and away from misguidance can only be entrusted to one who is present, who does not absent himself, who is not seized by sleep, and whom death does not reach, then no created being's agency over it is valid. It is as if it were said: "If their affairs were entrusted to you, they would be lost during your sleep and at your death." So He indicated this by what conveys its meaning, and He added to it benefits that are known through reflection, namely the comparison of guidance to life and wakefulness, and of misguidance to death and sleep. Just as none can cause death or sleep except Allah, so none can grant guidance or cause misguidance except Allah. Whoever understands this subtle point understands the secret of Allah's power, and whoever understands the secret in it finds calamities easy to bear, so this is a consolation to him (ﷺ).

He turned the speech to the expression by the Greatest Name (al-Ism al-A'zam), because the situation requires it, and He attributed the taking of souls (tawaffi) to Himself, glorified is He, because the passage is explaining that no other is fit for agency at all. So He said: ﴿Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses all perfections, and to whom no path of deficiency leads. ﴿Takes the souls﴾ which have died at the completion of (p. 518) their terms, i.e., He acts in their taking as one who exerts himself in that, by seizing them in full, leaving nothing of them in any part of the body. He expressed the plural of abundance with the plural of paucity (jam' al-qilla), indicating that they, although they exceed counting, are like a single soul. Perhaps He did not make it singular lest it be thought that unity is meant in its literal sense. ﴿At the time of their death﴾, i.e., His preventing them from acting in their bodies in this worldly life, being contained in their death, confined in it, enclosed by it. He conjoined to "the souls" the phrase ﴿and those that have not died﴾, i.e., and He takes the souls which ﴿have not died﴾ because their terms have not ended, at the time of their sleep, being ﴿in their sleep﴾, by preventing them from acting through sense and perception for as long as sleep exists, enclosed in it, with none of them in the body in the state of wakefulness. So what unites both is the absence of perception, awareness and action. And if it had been said "by their death and by their sleep," it would not have conveyed that each of death and taking (wafah) is a distinct sign from the other.

Since sleep is temporary, its being joined with death shows us that death is also temporary, and inevitably so, because the agent of each of them is one. Therefore He made the following a consequence of that: ﴿Then He keeps back﴾, i.e., as a consequence of the two takings, He keeps back with Himself ﴿those upon whom He has decreed﴾, i.e., He completed, judged and decided with a fixed, settled decision. The reading in the passive voice (qira'at al-bina' lil-maf'ul) clarifies this meaning by adding ease and facility. ﴿Death upon them﴾, enclosed in their death, unable to direct their bodies as long as death surrounds them, just as the sleeper is likewise while sleep surrounds her. ﴿And He releases the others﴾, i.e., those whose death He delayed and made enclosed in sleep, because their term, which He set for them, has not ended, so that the sleep passes away and He awakens them to direct their bodies. He makes that keeping back for the dead and the release for the sleeper, ﴿until a named term﴾, for the resurrection of the dead and the death of the sleeper, which none but Him knows. So when that term comes, He causes the sleeper to die and raises the dead. It has become clear from the estimation to which the context certainly points that the soul which sleeps is the one that dies, and it is the spirit (ruh). Ibn al-Salah said in his fatawa: "This is closer to the apparent meaning of the Book and the Sunnah." End of quote.

al-Tabarani narrated in al-Awsat, (al-Haythami said: its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih), from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The spirits of the living and the dead meet, and they ask one another. Then Allah keeps back the spirits of the dead and releases the spirits of the living to their bodies." al-Bukhari narrated from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: «When one of you goes to his bed, let him say: "In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side.
