O Allah, if You take my soul, have mercy on it; and if You release it, guard it with what You guard Your righteous servants."» It has also become clear that the verse contains ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which one element of a parallel pair is mentioned and its counterpart omitted): He mentioned "the time" first, as evidence for the omitted like of it in sleep second, and "sleep" second, as evidence for the omitted death first.

When this has been completed in this elevated style and firm composition, he drew attention to its greatness and the secrets within it, by saying, emphatically, as a rebuke to those who ascribe it to fables and other falsehoods: ﴿Indeed, in that﴾, i.e., in this great matter, of taking and sleep, in this manner and this expression (p. 520), ﴿are signs﴾, i.e., evidence that none but Him can give life and preserve, and that He is able to resurrect and to do everything else He wills; ﴿for a people﴾, i.e., people possessing strength in handling affairs. Since this matter requires nothing more than stripping the soul of distractions and reflecting, He said: ﴿who reflect﴾, i.e., upon the greatness of this arrangement, so that by it the greatness of Allah may be known. This is because the soul is a spiritual substance, and in its attachment to the body it has three states. The first is that the light of the soul falls upon the body both outwardly and inwardly, and that is life with wakefulness. The second is that the light of the soul is cut off from the body outwardly but not inwardly, and that is by sleep. The third is that this is cut off both outwardly and inwardly, and that is by death. So death and sleep are of one genus, except that death is a complete cutting-off and sleep is an incomplete cutting-off. None can bring one thing into existence in two kinds, then place both in one thing in succession, and separate each of them from the other, except He, glorified is He. And whoever is able to end the lesser death by a limit He set for it, is able to end the greater one by the same means.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 43:

When he (al-Biqa'i) had drawn this conclusion, which is necessary, by way of saying something like, as a warning to them: "Do they not know that nothing can stand in His place, that nothing happens except by His leave, and that no one can come near to the power over any of His acts? How then could anyone approach His rank, let alone be like Him? So would they then turn back from their error?" He balanced this with His saying: ﴿Or have they taken﴾; that is, they burdened themselves, after the proofs had become clear to them, by taking ﴿besides Allah﴾, that is, the One who has no equal and no one close to Him, ﴿intercessors﴾; that is, to bring them near to Him in nearness, ﴿in this world and in the Hereafter﴾, assuming that such intercession exists, even though the evidences of witnessing (al-adilla al-shuhudiyya) are present with them, showing that no one intercedes except with one who can be equal to him in some respect. For this reason he drew attention to the meaning by His saying, turning away from them to indicate their lack of understanding: ﴿Say: "Even though?"﴾; that is, would they take them for that purpose, even though ﴿they own nothing﴾; that is, this attribute does not newly arise in them; ﴿and do not understand﴾, as is observed from the condition of your idols.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 44:

When He had negated the capacity of their idols for this matter, He indicated its negation from anything other than Him by restricting the matter to Him alone. So He said: ﴿Say: To Allah belongs all intercession﴾; that is, the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, alone; ﴿all intercession﴾; that is, this entire category; so no one other than Him possesses any part of it. Rather, He grants permission, if He wills, concerning what He desires of it, to whomever He wills of His servants. And since all that is other than Him is His possession, and since it is established that what is owned cannot confer upon anything the ownership of which its master possesses, because two ownerships do not converge upon one thing from one aspect, He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾; that is, He alone; ﴿the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾; that is, those which you do not witness of His dominion other than these two; and intercession is part of their dominion. And since what is owned may be a weak possession that sometimes overcomes its owner, confronts him, and thereby becomes qualified to intercede with him, He negated this with respect to Him, glorified is He, by His saying, indicating the greatness of dominance by the particle of delay: ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾; that is, not to anyone else; ﴿you will be returned﴾; meaningfully in this world, by His executing all His command upon you; and sensibly and manifestly, and meaningfully, in the Hereafter.

When He had shown that their intercessors are not worthy of intercession, and that the whole matter belongs to Him alone, and concluded that there is no escape from returning to Him, which requires that all aspirations be turned toward Him and all resolves be directed to Him, and because none is to be feared but Him and none is to be hoped in but Him, He mentioned one of their states, saying: ﴿And when﴾, meaning: the situation is what we have mentioned. ﴿Allah is mentioned﴾, and He repeated the Greatest Name rather than using a pronoun, to magnify His matter and to increase the ugliness of their state, saying: ﴿Allah﴾, meaning: the One than whom there is no greater, and to whom no matter belongs but Him. ﴿Alone﴾, meaning: apart from their intercessors, whose lack of any intercession for them has become clear. ﴿Their hearts shrink﴾, meaning: they recoil in aversion, fear, and arrogance, along with the darkening of the face and the constriction of the heart. This is how the original would have been, but instead He said: ﴿the hearts of those who do not believe﴾, meaning: those who do not renew belief ﴿in the Hereafter﴾. This clarifies that what drives them to this is their neglect of the belief in what the verse concluded with, namely the return to Him, which He perfected and made manifest: the return of the Hereafter. ﴿And when those besides Him are mentioned﴾, and He rebuked them for their contentment with the lesser, saying: ﴿besides Him﴾, meaning: the idols. He emphasized the extreme extent of their ignorance in following falsehood and their obstinacy upon it, without pausing to reflect on any evidence, or to hear "He said" or "It was said," by His saying: ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾, meaning: with their inner selves, which overflow upon their outward appearance, ﴿they rejoice﴾, meaning: they hasten to seek joy, to bring it about, and to renew it in a manner of constancy in all of that, whether Allah is mentioned along with them or not. So the rejoicing at that time is only in regard to the rivals. Shrinking and rejoicing are opposites, because shrinking is the heart being filled with grief and rage, so its effect appears, which is the contraction of the surface of the face, whereas rejoicing is the heart being filled with delight, so that its effect appears, which is expansion and brightness in the face. This was said by al-Zamakhshari. The governing element of the first "idha" is the same as that of the sudden-occurrence "idha" (fuja'iyyah), meaning: they suddenly rejoice at the time of this mention. He expressed the first with a verb and the second with a nominal sentence, so as to convey their blame for shrinking in any degree, even in its least state, and for the constancy of rejoicing, as a condemnation of disbelief in general and of persisting in it, while opening the door to repentance.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 46:

When he (Allah) negated the capacity of agency over people in guidance and in misguidance for anyone other than Him, and indicated this by His dominion and His possession, and informed of their deliberate pursuit of falsehood, that produced the obligation of seeking refuge in Him, turning away from all else, and confining resolve to Him. So He said (p-524), informing of this and teaching what is to be said when one opposes the caller by following desire: ﴿Say﴾; that is: O you to whom the Book was revealed, for none other than him understands Our true understanding; turning in desire to your Lord that He may grant you victory over them in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿O Allah﴾; that is: O Allah. This is pure vocative address. It is also used in two other ways, which Ibn al-Khashshab al-Mawsili (Ibn al-Khashshab) mentioned in his book "al-Nihayah Sharh al-Kifayah." One of them is that it is mentioned to establish the answer in the mind of the questioner, as when "the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Dimam ibn Tha'labah (may Allah be pleased with him) when he said: 'Did Allah command you to pray the five prayers?' He said: 'O Allah, yes,'" up to the end of what he said to him. He was pleased that when the one questioned invokes Allah in his answer, his invoking Him makes the questioner more inclined to believe him, because it weighs more heavily on his heart, provided he does not set himself up to invoke Allah and was not in the position of doing so, and he is one who considers the use of falsehood lawful. The second is that it indicates rarity and the infrequency of what is mentioned, like the saying of authors: "such-and-such will not happen, except if such-and-such occurs"; as if he sought Allah's forgiveness for his certainty, or does not close the door on the possibility that other than what he mentioned may happen. So he said: "O Allah, forgive me, for it is possible that such-and-such may occur." End of quotation. Then, according to Sibawayh, it is a substitute (badal); according to others, it is an adjective (sifah). So He said: ﴿Originator﴾; that is: the Creator from non-existence; ﴿of the heavens﴾; that is: all of them; ﴿and the earth﴾; that is: its kind. And since power is not complete except with complete knowledge, He said: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾; that is: what cannot be known to creatures and what can be.

Since none other than Him, glory be to Him, is able to do that, the restriction in His saying ﴿You﴾ is fitting; that is: You alone; ﴿will judge between Your servants﴾; that is: between me, them, and others, in this world and the Hereafter; there is no escape from that, and nothing other than it is valid in wisdom; just as everyone judges between his servants and those under his command, and in his opinion nothing other than that is permissible; ﴿concerning that about which they used to differ﴾; that is: constantly, according to what their natural dispositions, with which You created them, demand. As for other than You, He does not know all that they do, so he is not able to judge between them. As for what they are deeply immersed in differing about, he does not judge between them regarding it, because it is either what they were prepared for by their sound natural dispositions and upright intellects, in agreement upon which it is the truth; or what differing about arises for them not by deliberate intention, or by an unstable intention, and this is among what good deeds erase. Thus it is known that the placing of the adverbial phrase first is only for restriction, not for the sake of the verse-ending (fasilah).

Al-Biqa'i, *Nazm al-Durar*, on Surah 39, verse 47:

Since the implied sense is: "So He punishes the wrongdoers; for had they known this, they would not have claimed for Him, glorified be He, a son, nor partners whom they take as intercessors to draw them near to Him, on account of His majesty, His transcendence above what they have ascribed to Him, and His perfection," He joined to it, to magnify the matter, His saying: ﴿And if indeed﴾. The original form would have been "for them," but He said, to generalise and to attach the judgment to the description (*ta'liq bil-wasf*): ﴿for those who did wrong﴾, meaning, those who fell into wrongdoing in any matter, however small. ﴿Whatever is on the earth﴾. Since the matter is great, He emphasised it with His saying: ﴿all of it﴾, and increased its magnitude with His saying: ﴿and the like of it﴾, and said: ﴿with it﴾, so as to convey the whole as a single unit (*badal al-kull jumlatan*), not piece by piece. ﴿They would offer it as ransom﴾, meaning, they would strive to seek to ransom ﴿themselves therewith﴾ ﴿from the evil of the punishment﴾. He specified the time, to magnify it and to add to its terror, saying: ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say to the least punished of the people of the Fire: 'If you had everything that is on the earth, would you have ransomed yourself with it?' He will say: 'Yes.' He will say: 'I desired from you something easier than this, while you were in the loins of Adam, peace be upon him: that you should not associate anything with Me. But you refused, except to associate [others] with Me.'"

His saying "I desired" (*aradtu*) means: I acted toward you in the manner of one who desires, and this is the meaning of His saying in another narration: "I had indeed asked you."

Since the implied sense is: "Even if they possessed that and ransomed themselves with it, it would not be accepted from them, nor would it benefit them; and because that time is the time of recompense, not the time of action, whereas today is the time of action, not the time of recompense, so if they spent even the least thing in it, rightly, it would be accepted from them," He joined to it, from its root and not from its consequence, His saying, magnifying the matter by turning the speech to the Greatest Name: ﴿And there will appear to them﴾, meaning, it will become manifest in complete clarity, ﴿on that Day﴾, ﴿from Allah﴾, meaning, the Supreme King. He made its matter terrible by leaving it unspecified, so that it would stand in contrast to: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾ [al-Sajdah: 17]. So He said: ﴿what they had not reckoned﴾, meaning, in accordance with their innate natures and the heedlessness and negligence upon which they were created, ﴿they had not reckoned﴾, meaning, it was not in their dispositions to deliberately reckon it, and their minds would not have conceived of the punishment in this way. And when it was not thus, it was harder upon the soul and more startling to the heart.

[Translation]

﴿And there will appear to them﴾: that is, it will become manifest in a complete manifestation, as though it were in the open, with nothing to prevent it. ﴿the evil deeds of what﴾: and since this is in the context of ransom, and a person in ransoming himself gives up desirable and precious things, He here expressed it with "earning" (kasb), whose connotation includes the essence and the extract, which is the secret of a thing; so it is more specific than "work" ('amal). For this reason al-Ash'ari (al-Ash'ari) made it the criterion of reward, and said, explaining that the pure essence of their work is dropped, so how about other than it?! This is in contrast to what is in al-Jathiyah. ﴿They earned﴾: that is, the thing which they did with desire, striving in it, because they thought it beneficial, and that it was the most special of their deeds, the most sublime, and the most useful. ﴿And there will surround﴾: that is, it will encompass them by way of necessity and harm; ﴿them what﴾: that is, the recompense of the thing ﴿they used to﴾: that is, constantly, as though they were created upon it; ﴿mock﴾: that is, they seek and bring about mockery and derision of it, of the Fire and of everything they were being threatened with.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 49:

When he had informed them of the manifestation of this to them, he gave the reason for it: that they were doing what was not normally expected of them, namely repaying good with evil, while they were deserving of its opposite (p-528). So He said: ﴿Then﴾; that is, this happened to them because when ﴿harm touches man﴾, but He told about the kind to which they belong by what is impressed upon it, so He said: ﴿harm touches man﴾; whatever harm it was, from a direction he anticipates, as was mentioned in the one at the beginning of the surah. It is permissible that it be a consequence of the report of their ransoming themselves with what they are able to give, and that it be a consequence of their aversion to the Oneness of God, as a marvel at their state in reversing matters and at their misguidance. What was mentioned in the verse at the beginning of the surah about the secret of its being with the waw has preceded. He turned the speech to the place of manifestation of greatness, indicating that most people are not hoped to acknowledge the truth or submit to the people of goodness except when they are touched by harms. So He said: ﴿called upon Us﴾, knowing Our greatness, rather than His gods, despite his aversion to mentioning Us and his delight in mentioning them.

Since that harm was great, the deliverance from it was distant, from the aspect that there is no stratagem for any creature in repelling it, He pointed to its greatness and the length of its time by the particle of delay. So He said, reproaching him for forgetting the harm despite its greatness in itself and despite the length of its time: ﴿Then when We bestow upon him﴾; that is, We give him, upon Our greatness, bestowing favors upon him, benevolently taking charge of his affair, and making him fit for his condition, worthy of managing it, without any deed he did, fulfilling his good opinion of Us, and We perfected our upbringing of him and our care for him, despite his neglect of Our right (p-529); ﴿a blessing from Us﴾, in which no one other than Us has any share of obligation; and had it not been for Our greatness, it would not have been. ﴿He says﴾, forgetting what he was in of harm, though its duration had lengthened, restricting it to himself, not adorned with what We had alerted him to adorn himself with of Our goodness toward him and Our turning toward him when he submitted: ﴿Only I have been given it﴾, referring back to its pronoun to glorify it, and he built the verb into the passive to indicate that he has no regard for recognizing who the Giver is, thanking Him; his regard is only for the greatness of the blessing and the greatness of himself, and that it is according to some measure: ﴿Only I have been given it﴾; that is, this favor bestowed upon me, which is great and mighty, because I am great, so I am given according to my measure. And "mā" is the superfluous restrictive particle that stops "inna", to indicate restriction; it is permissible that it be a relative, the subject of "inna", and its predicate is His saying: ﴿on﴾; that is, a bestowing exalted, firmly established ﴿on knowledge﴾; that is, great knowledge, and diligence from me, by way of earning, striving, and the ways of seeking and cunning; so that was a cause of its coming to me; or: knowledge from God of his deserving it.

Since the estimate was: "It is not so, nor is it a blessing," He said, indicating the ill omen of that bestowal and its worthlessness, because it is one of the causes of his misguidance, with the feminine (p-530): ﴿Nay, it is﴾; that is, the gift and the blessing; ﴿a trial﴾, to test him: whether he will give thanks or disbelieve, so that the proof may be established against him; if it leads him to the Fire, it was a gradual leading on. He made the pronoun feminine to belittle it in relation to His power, glory be to Him and exalted; and because it led to delusion, after he had first made its pronoun masculine, glorifying it, to make thanking it obligatory.

Since among those tried there are those who become alert, and they are the fewer, He said, gathering, to alert to the intention of the genus, and that his first expression with the singular pronoun is an indication that most people are, in that wretched character, as if they were one soul: ﴿But most of them﴾; that is, most of these who utter this speech; ﴿do not know﴾; that is, no knowledge is renewed for them at all, because they were stamped with coarseness, ignorance, and dullness. So if, when they call upon Us while they are in Hell, We answer them and bestow Our blessing upon them, and they attribute it to other than Us, as they used to do in the world, it would be the same.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 50:

Since the disbelievers of Quraysh were the primary intended target of this with a great intention, although it is comprehensive in its generality of including others of the earlier and later peoples, He said, clarifying that: ﴿Indeed, those before them had already said it﴾; that is, their statement: ﴿"It was given to me only because of knowledge"﴾ [az-Zumar: 49], ﴿those who came before them﴾; that is, from among those who were stronger than them in power and greater in number, as Qarun said, and whoever was pleased with his condition and so wished for his wealth. ﴿But what they used to earn did not avail them﴾; that is, those past ones, ﴿what they used to earn﴾ (p-531) by what their natures required; ﴿they earn﴾; that is, they continually renew their earning of it, of wealth and status, even if it filled the plain and the mountain.

﴿Fa-asābahum﴾ (so it befell them): that is, a severe affliction, as indicated by the masculine form of the verb; that is, it resulted from their not being enriched that there befell them ﴿the evil consequences of what they earned﴾: that is, the calamity of that, and whatever harm results from its effects. ﴿And those who wronged﴾: that is, those who put things in other than their proper places; ﴿from among these﴾: that is, from among your people, who do not reflect upon the Qur'an, for if they had reflected upon its verses, they would have known; but blindness has preceded them. ﴿Will befall them﴾: that is, an extremely severe affliction, by a promise that admits of no breach, as it befell those before them; ﴿the evil consequences of what they earned﴾: that is, what they did with desire and delight, thinking it would benefit them; ﴿and they will not escape﴾: even if they thought that their wealth was a fortress for them, and they performed, out of insolence and exultation in it, the deeds of one who thinks that no misfortune will reach him in this world, and that he will not be raised to the terrors We have prepared for him in the Hereafter. Indeed, that befell them: the first of what befell them was what time revealed of the battle of "Badr"; then what followed it, to an endless extent.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 52:

(p-532) Since it is established that the one who harms and the one who benefits is none other than Allah, who gives to whom He wills, withholds from whom He wills, and takes away and abases whom He wills after having raised him up, the implied construction is: "Have they not known that what those before them amassed did not avert the command of Allah?" Then He joined to it His saying, ﴿Have they not...﴾ [﴿أولم﴾]. Since the context is negating knowledge from most of them, and since the purpose of the surah is to demonstrate that He is true to His promise, and bare knowledge suffices for this, He expressed it with knowledge ('ilm), unlike what came before in "al-Rum" (Surah al-Rum), where He said, ﴿Have they not seen?﴾ [﴿يعلموا﴾]. That is, through the experiences they witnessed in their lifetimes. He also turned the speech to the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam, the Name of Allah) in order to magnify the situation and to remove confusion and obstinacy with the utmost clarity of explanation: ﴿that Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses majesty and beauty, ﴿extends provision﴾, that is, He alone extends it in its fullest measure, ﴿to whom He wills,﴾ even if that person has no stratagem or strength, ﴿and restricts it﴾, that is, constricts it, along with hardship, by a compelling decree, upon one who is among the most skilled of people in stratagems and the most powerful in dominions. It is well known that were it not for the fact that all of this comes from Him alone, no one among those who possess physical strength and firm mastery of knowledge would be poor at all.

Since this is a matter that no one denies, He treated it as accepted and said, ﴿Indeed in that﴾, that is, in this great matter, and He emphasized it because their actions are the actions of one who denies that there is a lesson in it, ﴿are signs for a people﴾, possessing strength and lofty resolves, ﴿who believe﴾, that is, they have been prepared so that faith may come into existence in them, so they renew their affirmation at every moment with continuous renewal, that all affairs are from Allah. Thus they fear Him, hope in Him, thank Him, and do not disbelieve Him. As for others, the Word has become due against them, by the work of the Fire that has been prepared for them, so faith is not possible for them. Therefore there are no signs in this for them, because those signs will not benefit them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 53:

(p-533) When He, glorified is He, had given warning in this surah, especially in these verses, so that the warning grew long, and He had filled it with threats, with a frightening and abundant great warning and threat, and concluded it with exhortation to faith and to sound reflection in recognition (of Him), and the abundance of threats had perhaps caused despair, repulsion, and estrangement, and had prevented tenderness and driven people away, He, exalted is He, said, seeking to win hearts, gently and kindly toward those who had fled from His door, being gracious, combining the two tones of affection, speaking in the manner of one bestowing favor, through the tongue of the Prophet of mercy, turning the speech from the third person to direct address after the style of absence, saying: ﴿Say﴾ — that is: O most noble of creation and most merciful of them toward the servants. He departed from what "Say" would require, from the absent form to the sense of direct address, to increase the appeal to tenderness, and He increased in gentleness by mentioning servanthood and by the attribution to His own pronoun, free of any formality, so He said: ﴿O﴾ — that is: your Lord, who is good to you, says: O ﴿My servants﴾. So He sweetened their hearts after those bitternesses with the sweetness of attribution to His presence, bringing them near to His door. When He attributed (them to Himself), the obedient hoped that they were the ones intended, so they raised their heads, while the disobedient lowered theirs and said: "Who are we, that He should direct this speech toward us?" Then He, exalted is He, consoling them, said: ﴿Who have transgressed﴾ — that is: they exceeded the limit in placing things other than in their proper places, until heavy burdens became theirs, ﴿against themselves﴾, so they pushed them away from the divine presences and cast them down into satanic lowliness. Thus the situation was reversed: those who had lowered their heads were lifted up, and their humiliation was removed, while those who had raised their heads were brought low, and their assault was removed. This is what al-Qushayri said. The restriction of transgression implies that transgression against another is not forgiven except by exiting that other's claim. ﴿Do not despair﴾ — that is: let your hope be cut off, and you despair and refrain. He magnified the hope by turning speech away from direct address to the third person, and by attributing mercy to the Greatest Name, which comprises all attributes of majesty and generosity, so He said: ﴿of the mercy of Allah﴾ — that is: the generosity of the One encompassing every attribute of perfection, so that this despair will not prevent you from repentance, which is the gate of mercy. And because of the greatness of the station, He attributed (mercy) to the Greatest Name. Then He gave the reason for that by His saying, as an emphasis, because they thought that the abundance of threats prevented forgiveness and made punishment by retribution certain; and He repeated the Greatest Name, to magnify the matter and to emphasize, by what it contains of the meaning of encompassing and totality, to intend generality, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾ — that is: the One combining all the qualities of beauty, majesty, and generosity. Just as He is characterized by retribution, He is characterized by pardon and forgiveness. ﴿forgives﴾, if He wills, ﴿the sins﴾. Since the definite article "the" conveyed comprehensiveness, He emphasized it, saying: ﴿all of them﴾, and He does not mind. Yet it had already been stated by Him that He forgives polytheism only through repentance from it, while He forgives other than it if He wills, with repentance, and if He wills, without repentance; and no one can prevent Him from any of that.

Since such a thing is not known among people, rather if a king of the kings of the world wished to pardon the people of crimes, his soldiers would rise against him, his authority would dissolve, and his limit would be breached, (p-535) He gave this reason with what is specific to Himself, so He said, emphasizing the improbability of that by analogy with what they are accustomed to: ﴿Indeed, He is He﴾ — that is: alone; ﴿the Forgiving﴾ — that is: the one of far-reaching forgiveness, such that He erases sins whatever He wills, in essence and in trace, so He does not punish and does not rebuke; ﴿the Merciful﴾ — that is: the One who bestows honor after forgiveness. No one at all can raise any kind of objection against Him, nor direct any criticism toward Him.

Now, when the implied sense was: "Desist from your sins, for they cut you off from good and keep you far from perfection," he followed it with an appeal (istiʿṭāf), indicating that the forgiveness mentioned earlier comes only if He, glory be to Him, wills to bestow favor, with repentance or without repentance: ﴿And turn back (in repentance)﴾; that is, return with your whole selves, entrust your needs, lean your affairs upon Him, and make your path ﴿to﴾; and he turned the speech to the attribute of beneficence to increase the appeal, saying: ﴿your Lord﴾; that is, the One from whom you have seen no beneficence except that it is from Him; ﴿and submit to Him﴾; that is, bring about the submission of all that He has granted you as possession, of substances and meanings, disclaiming them for His sake, for if He willed, He would strip them from you. So when you do not possess them with complete ownership, then count yourselves as lent to Him, not owning it nor having power over it; as though what you held as your own original possession had never been.

Since that was difficult, because restraining oneself from what the soul is close to attaining of its desire is most bitter, he said, threatening them, and indicating by the particle of beginning (p-536) his contentment with them when they carry out what he has affirmed in the brief span of time, because no one can truly measure God with His due measure by devoting all of time to obedience, even though the ambiguity of the appointed term urges the sensible person to devote himself entirely to it: ﴿before the punishment comes upon you﴾; that is, while you are humbled; ﴿the punishment﴾; that is, the one that cuts off all sweetness and makes every bitterness and hardship swallowed. And since a person may fear harm in pursuing what gives him pleasure and tries to avert it, he said, magnifying this punishment and indicating with the particle of delay that it cannot be averted even if the span is long: ﴿then you will not be helped﴾; that is, no kind of help will ever come to you again.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 55:

When He had commanded seeing all matters as from Allah, and surrendering all leadership (of one's affairs) to Him, He commanded what is higher than that, which is striving (mujahadah) by putting the self to death (qatl al-nafs). So He said: ﴿And follow﴾; that is: treat your selves and oblige them to follow ﴿the best of what has been sent down﴾ ﴿to you﴾ ﴿from your Lord﴾, [following it] on the path of justice, and [then] of excellence (ihsan), which is higher than pardon, and which is above retaliation; by following this Qur'an, which is the best of what has been revealed from the books of Allah, and by following the best of what is in it. So you join the one who cut you off, give to the one who deprived you, and do good to the one who wronged you. This is regarding the rights of creation; and its like regarding the worship of the Creator is that you be ﴿as if you see Him﴾, which is higher than the awareness ﴿that He sees you﴾, which is higher than performing it while heedless of that.

Since this was difficult for the self, He encouraged it by His saying, displaying the attribute of ihsan in place of the pronoun: ﴿from your Lord﴾; that is: the One who never ceases to do good to you while you oppose Him with great sins. And since among selves there are those that are like beasts, which do not submit except by striking, He said, also alerting to the reason for His gentleness, by affirming the preposition: ﴿before there comes upon you﴾; that is: in your state of inability to defend yourselves, ﴿the punishment﴾; that is: the matter which removes what you find pleasant and sweet in this world or in the Hereafter.

Since seizing [someone] while unaware is harder on the selves, He said: ﴿suddenly﴾. And since a person may sense a thing once and then forget it, so it takes him by surprise, He negated that by His saying: ﴿while you do not perceive﴾; that is: you have no awareness of its coming, neither at the time of its coming nor before it, in any way whatsoever, due to the extreme of your heedlessness; so that it is the most dreadful thing for the self, because of how strongly it contradicts what is settled within it, and it has become accustomed to the opposite of it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 39, verse 56:

When a person is faced with the onset of loss, he has words and states that he would reckon with if he imagined them before they overtook him. So he would have distanced himself from the causes of loss. He gave as the reason for turning to following (the truth) the utmost effort and contention, and so He said: ﴿lest⦆; that is, out of dislike that ﴿a soul should say⦆. Since what leads a person into deficiency is only his desires and appetites, which oppose his intellect, He expressed it with His words ﴿a soul⦆; that is, when the punishment befalls it. Its being singular and indefinite is sufficient for the threat, because anyone may be the one intended.

﴿Alas for me!⦆ The *tahassur* (lamentation) is grief over what has passed and regret for it. He added the *alif* in place of the *ya'* (in *hasratā* for *hasratī*), as a magnification of it; that is, "O the length of my grief!", because what contained my well-being has been uncovered from me and has moved far from me, so there is no way for me to reach it to make up for what has passed from it. This is at the uncovering of its states and the arrival of its terrors and horrors. Abu Ja'far's reading, ﴿Alas for my⦆ *hasratāy* (with a double ending), indicates that this lamentation has exceeded its limit, through combining the *'iwad* (compensation), which is the *alif*, with the *mu'awwad 'anhu* (that which is compensated for), which is the *ya'*, and by *hall al-masdar* (resolving the verbal noun into a full clause), because what it is resolved into is clearer in attribution, more emphatic, more indicative of the intended meaning, and greater. So He said: ﴿over what I neglected⦆; that is, by what I wasted, so that its order slipped from me and its joining and cohesion became impossible.

Since everyone's right is that he be near to himself, physically or in meaning, as if he were beside himself, and since the side (*janb*) is the support of a thing, yet a person may neglect it because it is turned away from direct confrontation and observation, neglecting it indicates attributing to the neglecter a heedlessness toward his companion, and that is a matter that is not forgiven. He said: ﴿in the side of⦆, and He turned the speech toward the Greatest Name, to increase the awe, with His words ﴿Allah⦆; that is, the right of the Greatest King, who is not neglected nor treated lightly.

Since the one who is harmed, punished and overpowered exaggerates in confession, hoping for acceptance and turning away (of the punishment), He said, emphasising and with great insistence on announcing the abandonment of what his state was requiring and what his speech declares, that he is in the right and in earnest: ﴿and indeed⦆; that is, while the case is that I ﴿was⦆; that is, that was in my nature, ﴿among the mockers⦆; that is, the scoffers, the arrogant, those who place themselves in a position other than their proper station. That is because disobedience did not suffice for me until I was mocking the people of obedience. That is, he says this, perhaps he will be relieved from it and pardoned for it, in the manner of those who plead tenderly at times of hardship, hoping they will return to the best of habits.

Since the soul, when it falls into a predicament, leaves no possibility unexplored until it clings to its hems, grasps at its ropes, and tries its every means, it (the soul) said, relating its lie, where only truth avails: ﴿Or [lest] it say﴾; that is, at the descent of what it has no power to withstand; ﴿"If only Allah"﴾; and it stated the Name explicitly rather than using a pronoun, to magnify it and to take pleasure in mentioning the noble Name; so it said: ﴿"Allah"﴾; that is, the One who possesses complete power and all-encompassing knowledge; ﴿"had guided me"﴾; that is, by making the path clear; ﴿"I would have been"﴾; that is, constantly, with the constancy of something imprinted upon, ﴿"among the God-fearing (al-muttaqin)"﴾; that is, those who do not undertake any act for which no proof has guided them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 58:

When he had mentioned her state in acknowledging falsehood, and then her resort to lies and calumny (p-540), he followed it with the wish that yields nothing but loss, saying: ﴿Or [lest] she say﴾; that is, that excessive soul [that neglected its duty]; ﴿when she sees the punishment﴾; that is, which has fallen upon her, whether as mercy or as vengeance; ﴿"If only﴾; that is, "Would that" ﴿I had a return﴾; that is, a return to the abode of action, so that I might secure [my salvation] through it; ﴿so that I would be﴾; that is, so that as a consequence of my returning to it I would be ﴿among the doers of good﴾; that is, those who act with the goodness to which the Qur'an calls. This parsing, namely its being conjoined to the answer [the "lau" clause], is more fitting with the rest of the verses that belong to the same string.

When He, glory be to Him, had warned about what befalls the one who is seized (on the Day of Judgment) of evil conditions and dreadful terrors, and the meaning of what preceded of his lying and his wishing was that: "No clear proof came to me, and I had no time in which I could be able to act," He said, refuting him: ﴿Yes indeed﴾; that is, both of these matters were in fact yours. ﴿My signs came to you﴾; and He turned the speech to the first person, while stripping the pronoun of the appearance of majesty, because of what preceded of the requirements of calling that to mind, to inform (the listener) of the extremity of His anger, after turning (the address) to remind the soul being addressed, which indicates that it acted in disobedience like strong, hardened people: through denial and arrogance, while having, outwardly, the ability to reflect upon the signs, to seek clarification of the proofs, and to walk the paths of guidance. This comes after its feminine form (of the word for soul, nafs) indicated its weakness in bearing punishment and the overcoming of deficiencies over it. So He said: ﴿My signs﴾, despite their greatness in clarity, a clarity such that no clarity is like it, at a time when you were able to act with the heart, the tongue, and the limbs. (p-541) ﴿So you denied them﴾; with audacity toward God, and a lack of concern for the consequences. ﴿And you were arrogant﴾; that is, you regarded yourself as too great to accept them. ﴿And you were﴾; that is, a state as though it were your innate nature, due to the intensity of your immersion in it and your eagerness for it. ﴿Among the disbelievers﴾; that is, those deeply immersed in concealing what had appeared of the lights of guidance, by denying out of arrogance. There was no barrier for you to good conduct except that; it was not the absence of clarity, nor the absence of time suitable for action.

When he had deliberately lied at the moment of the punishment, in the absence of clarification and at a time when repentance is still accepted, (Exalted is He) said, warning against his state and the state of those like him, and turning the speech toward one who would not fully grasp it except for Him, as consolation for him and an increase in the warning to others: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection﴾; that is, the Day for which it is not fitting in wisdom to leave (the reckoning) aside; ﴿you will see﴾; that is, O beholder; ﴿those who lied﴾. He increased the condemnation of their state in their audacity by turning the speech to the Greatest Name, saying: ﴿against God﴾; that is, the One possessing all attributes of perfection, by describing Him with what does not befit Him, while He is exalted above it, such as that He does what is not befitting of wisdom, through imposing obligations without clarification, and through creating creatures that attack one another without a reckoning that establishes justice between the wrongdoer and the wronged, or by attributing to Him a partner, or the like. Ibn al-Jawzi said: al-Hasan said, "They are those who say: if we wish we will do, and if we wish we will not do." End of quote. It seems he meant the Mu'tazilah (a rationalist theological school), who withdrew from his assembly and innovated their doctrine that they create their own actions. It also includes everyone who speaks about religion in ignorance, and everyone who lies while knowing he is lying, in whatever matter it may be, for insofar as his act is the act of one who supposes that God does not know his lie or is not able to requite it, it is as if he lied against God. ﴿You see them with your eyes, their faces blackened﴾; (this is) a subject and predicate, and it is the state of the relative pronoun; that is, their blackness is established, of increasing ugliness and great disgrace, by making that a sign upon them, so that whoever sees them may recognize them by what they lied about in the world, for they were not ashamed of the shameful lie. Is that not a deterrent from lying in general? So how much more from lying against God, whose prison is Hell? So how much more for those who were arrogant toward Him? ﴿Is there not in Hell﴾; that is, the one that greets whoever is cast into it with scowling and frowning; ﴿an abode﴾; that is, a dwelling; ﴿for the arrogant﴾; those who were arrogant toward following the command of God.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 61:

When He mentioned the state of those whom He made wretched, He followed it with the state of those whom He made happy. So He said, linking one sentence to another sentence (and not linking it to "you see," which is the object placed for the Day of Resurrection), to indicate that this is His treatment of them in both abodes, and to indicate the abundance of deliverance, given the abundance of the terrors, an abundance that exceeds counting: ﴿And Allah will deliver﴾, that is, absolute deliverance, for some of those who had taqwa (fear of God), by what the reading of Ya'qub indicates with the lightened form (yunajjī); and a great deliverance for some of them, by what the reading of the rest indicates with the intensified form (yunajjī with tashdid). He stated the Name explicitly and did not use a pronoun, in addition to magnifying their state and calming their hearts: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, He acts, with what He has of attributes of perfection, in their deliverance, acting as one who is most thorough in that. ﴿Those who had taqwa﴾, that is, those who exerted themselves to the utmost in guarding their souls from His wrath. Just as He protected them in this world from transgressions, He shields them there from punishments. ﴿With their mafaza﴾, that is, because they considered themselves to be in a distant, frightening desert (mafaza), so they halted there from every deed except with a guide, lest they walk without a guide and perish. Their taqwa led them to al-fawz (success), which is attaining the aim, and its time and place, the place for which the mafaza was named by way of optimism (tafa'ul). For this reason, Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, interpreted the mafaza as good deeds, because they are the cause of success. It was also read in the plural, taking into account the types of the verbal noun. All of that is through Allah's care for them in both abodes. So each person's mafaza in the Hereafter is according to the measure of his mafaza through acts of obedience in this world.

When it was as though it were said: What did He do regarding their deliverance? He said, mentioning the result of the deliverance: ﴿No harm will touch them﴾, that is, this kind of harm; so they will not fear. ﴿Nor will they grieve﴾, that is, no grief over something lost will reach their inner selves, because nothing whatsoever will be lost to them.

When the feared thing and the grieved-over thing both encompass everything in existence, and none can ward them off except the Originator (al-Mubdi'), the Self-Subsisting (al-Qayyum), He said, either as a new sentence or as a reason, making the Greatest Name (al-Ism al-A'zam) explicit to magnify the station: ﴿Allah﴾; that is, the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge (p-544), who saved them. ﴿Is the Creator of all things﴾; so nothing comes into being at all except by His creation. He does not create what they fear from Him, and no grief befalls them over it. Since this indicates comprehensive power, it must be accompanied by complete knowledge. He said: ﴿And He is﴾; He expressed it with the particle of elevation (ʿalā), because it is one of its finest uses, ﴿over all things﴾; that is, with dominance and supremacy, ﴿a Disposer of affairs﴾; that is, a Guardian of everything He wills concerning it, ﴿Self-Subsisting﴾; no weakness reaches His court, nor any heedlessness.

When the two horizons were the treasuries of all created beings, and only the one who holds the keys can dispose of treasuries, He said, indicating that He is their trustee: ﴿To Him belong the keys (*maqalid*)﴾. That is, to Him alone. The singular of *maqalid* is *miqlad*, like *miftah* (key), and also *miqlid*, like *qindil* (lamp). They mean the keys and the comprehensive, powerful affairs. The word is a metaphor for complete control over ﴿the heavens﴾, meaning all of them in number, ﴿and the earth﴾, meaning its kind. Their treasuries and affairs, and their keys that encompass everything in them, belong to Him. Thus nothing can exist in them, nothing in them can be disposed of, and no one in them can act, except by His permission. So there is no wonder in His delivering those who were mindful of God.

Since the implied sense was: "Those who believed in God and accepted His signs, they are the successful," He joined to it another statement, which the context of threat required: ﴿And those who disbelieved﴾. That is, they covered over the evidences that had become clear to them, and they denied that all affairs are in His hand. ﴿In the signs of God﴾, that is, the One for whom there is no manifest reality other than these signs. For (p-545) nothing exists except His Essence, glorified is He, which is unseen and which created beings cannot grasp; His acts, which are the most manifest of things; and His attributes, which are unseen from one aspect and witnessed from another. ﴿They﴾, the distant and the hateful, ﴿are﴾, exclusively, ﴿the losers﴾. For they lost their souls and everything connected to them in terms of benefit, because their disbelief is the ugliest disbelief, inasmuch as it relates to the most manifest of things.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 64:

When these proofs stood out, as you see, like banners, and the darkness of the night was dispelled, and the ignorant ones had called him (ﷺ) – as the exegetes said at the beginning of surah "Sad" – to cease from their gods, and their acquiescence in them would be worship of them, there resulted from that his (ﷺ) being commanded to confront them with what would split them apart, by His saying: ﴿Say﴾. And since the station of jealousy (ghayrah) requires the effacement of others, and when the other is effaced, all its accidents follow it, He placed first the object "other" (ghayr) of "I worship" – the object, according to the estimation of "an" (that) – of "you command" – so He said: ﴿Is it other than Allah﴾; that is: the Most Great King, who does not allow corruption at all. And since placing the denunciation before their act made it more effective, and postponing what preceded in the speech for its denunciation made it more awe-inspiring, and since prolonging the voice is more emphatic in the meaning of the speech, more frightening, more terrifying and more dreadful, he said – turning the speech to address them, because that is more intimidating to them and more severe in their distress: ﴿you command me﴾ – with idgham (assimilation), which requires prolongation, in the recitation of most of the reciters. Perhaps the idgham is an indication that they tried to tempt him (ﷺ) regarding the matter of their gods, by way of deception and trickery. And since he had established the denunciation to prove the others, he completed the establishment of mentioning the governing element in "ghayr" – he said, deleting "an" (the verbal particle, "that"), so that its clause falls within the scope of the denunciation: ﴿I worship﴾. It is in the nominative case, because "an", when it was deleted, its governing effect was cancelled, and its rule was not observed either, so that it could be said that the accusative of "ghayr" with it is impermissible, because the complement of a relative clause may not precede the relative.

And since worship of other than Allah is the most ignorant of ignorance, and ignorance is the place of every downfall, he said: ﴿O you ignorant ones﴾; that is: those deeply immersed in ignorance. It is advancing in matters that are obscure without knowledge; so said al-Harali in surah "al-Baqarah".

When fronting (*al-taqdim*, placing a word before its usual position) indicates exclusivity (*al-ikhtisas*), and they had not called upon Him for exclusivity but only for averting harm, which entails associating partners with Him, he made clear that it is an exclusivity, in that God is free of need of everything, so He does not accept any deed in which there is association. Whenever even the slightest association occurs, that whole deed belongs to the one who was associated. So the sense, as an explanation of the reason for His command to say to them what has preceded, rebuking them, is: "Say so-and-so; for it has indeed been revealed to you and to those before you: the obligation of monotheism (*tawhid*)." Then He joined to it His words, emphasizing them because of what is firmly established in souls, that whoever works for someone else's sake is accepted or not, whether it is on the basis of partnership or not: ﴿And indeed﴾. Since the one revealed was known to him ﷺ, He made the verb passive in His words ﴿it was revealed﴾. Since generalization is more likely to secure acceptance, He said ﴿and to those who﴾. Since sending (prophethood) occurs only in some time and for some people, He said ﴿before you﴾. Since a judgment upon a group may be a judgment upon the collective with the condition of collectivity, He specified, to explain that, while it is a judgment upon the collective, it is also a judgment upon every individual. Also, addressing the leader is addressing his followers, because he is their exemplar.

Since what was revealed to them was that whoever associates (partners with God), his deed is nullified, whether he himself or another, the statement was correct in the singular, in the place of such a phrase as "Indeed, association nullifies deeds," and as a substitute for the subject. He turned away from that to what he mentioned, because it is greater in prohibition and more effective in deterring whoever among the community is fit for it. He also emphasized it, because the polytheists deny its meaning to the utmost degree: ﴿If﴾, that is: this wording was revealed to each one of you, which is: "By My might, if you associate ﴿[anything with God]﴾," that is: any of the things, in any part of your deed for God; and this is of the nature of supposing the impossible. He mentioned it in this way so that it would be more striking to the followers. The verb after *in* (*in*, the conditional particle) refers to the future; so he turned here from the expression in the imperfect, for conformity between the wording and the meaning, because the verse was brought to address the disbelievers indirectly, so the expression in the past tense was more fitting, to indicate by its wording that whoever commits association has indeed lost, and by its meaning that whoever commits it is likewise.

Since warning had been established, he answered the condition and the oath with His words: ﴿surely will be nullified﴾, that is: it will certainly be corrupted and certainly your deed will be voided, so that no trace of it remains from the side of the Almighty; for He was associated with in it; He is Self-sufficient and accepts only the sincere, since He has no need of anything. As for from the side of others, it is because they have no power over anything. Since the context is one of threat, and worship included what preceded association of deeds and what followed it, He did not restrict it by connection to death, being content with its restriction in the verse of *al-Baqarah*. He said: ﴿and you will surely be﴾, that is, for the sake of its nullification, ﴿among the losers﴾, for whoever loses all his deed, there is no doubt about his loss. The addressing of the leaders in this manner, although what is actually intended is their followers, is more deterring for the followers and more stirring to their hearts and ears.

Since the implied sense was definitively "So do not associate partners," He built upon it His saying: ﴿Rather, Allah﴾; that is, He alone, the One characterized by all attributes of perfection, because of this grave prohibition and this terrible warning; whatever worship you may have offered to anything at all; ﴿so worship﴾; that is, sincerely devoting worship to Him. He omitted the condition and compensated for it by placing the object first. Since His worship cannot possibly be offered except as gratitude for the blessings He has bestowed in abundance, past and future, and since thanking the Benefactor is obligatory, He drew attention to this with His saying: ﴿and be among the grateful﴾; that is, among the foremost in this attribute, because He made you the best of creation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 67:

Since the implied sense is: "How well did these people not esteem Him, nor did they honour Him when they called you to associate others with Allah, nor did they worship Him with the worship due to Him, since they associated partners with Him," he followed it with His words: ﴿And they did not measure Allah with His true measure﴾. He mentioned the Greatest Name in its most fitting place, saying: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the Greatest King; ﴿with His true measure﴾, that is, they did not magnify Him as He is due to be magnified. For even if time were entirely devoted to His worship and sincere obedience, such that no part of it was free of them, that would still not be His true measure. How much more so when some part of it is free of them? How much more so when others are set up as equal to Him?

Having mentioned the magnification of everything that is attributed to Him, he pointed to His evident power, which entails the grasping and folding up, through what is the state within the folding of this existence. He said, as a metaphor for greatness through this: ﴿while the earth﴾, that is, and the state being that it is; he placed it first because of their direct contact with it and their knowledge of its reality. Since what they perceive of it in terms of extent and size is sufficient for greatness, even if they do not perceive that it is seven, he emphasised it with what suits all its layers, as a reminder to the perceptive that it is seven, without explicitly stating it. He said: ﴿all together﴾. Since the least important and lightest thing for a human being is what he holds within his grasp, he gave the example of that in His saying, reporting about the subject, in the singular with a fatha on the qaf, because it is more apt for belittling great things in comparison with His sublime greatness: ﴿His grasp﴾ (p-550). Since in this world there are those who claim kingship, dominance, greatness and power, while in the Hereafter the matter is the opposite of this, because the means are cut off, He said: ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾. There is no grasp there, literally or figuratively; likewise the folding and the right hand. These are only an illustration and an imagining of the completeness of power. Since they knew that the heavens are seven, layered upon one another, through what they witness of the movement of the stars, He used the plural so that, together with "all together", it would be as an explicit statement covering all the earth as well, in His saying: ﴿and the heavens will be folded up﴾. Since the upper world is more noble, He honoured it when giving the example of the right hand, saying: ﴿in His right hand﴾. Since this is only an illustration through what we are accustomed to, and what is meant by it is the utmost in power, He declared His most holy self free from what may have been attributed to Him by the anthropomorphist (mujassim) and the one who likens (mushabbih). He said: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, that is: may His power be exalted above this kind of power, free of every trace of deficiency, and of what leads to deficiency, such as associating partners and corporealisation and what resembles them; ﴿and exalted is He﴾, with an exaltedness beyond comprehension; ﴿above what they associate﴾, that is: His exaltedness above that is the exaltedness of one who is pursued to the utmost, so He is at a degree of loftiness beyond which there is no further degree, for if He had a partner, that partner would contend with Him for this power, or some part of it, and so prevent Him from some of it. And these are the things they worship, which have no power over anything. Al-Bukhari related in his Sahih, in the Book of Tawhid, and others, from Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "A rabbi of the Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: On the Day of Resurrection Allah will place the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the water and the moist earth on one finger, and the creatures on one finger; then He will shake them and say: (I am the King)." I saw the Prophet ﷺ laughing until his molars showed, in wonder and in confirmation of his words. Then the Prophet ﷺ said: ﴿And they did not measure Allah with His true measure﴾, up to: ﴿they associate﴾. Al-Shaykhan related from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah will fold up the heavens on the Day of Resurrection, then He will take them in His right hand, then He will say: (I am the King; where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?), then He will fold up the earths, then take them in His left hand, then He will say: (I am the King; where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?)." And in al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Allah will grasp the earth on the Day of Resurrection and fold up the heaven with His right hand, then He will say: (I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?)."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 68 (part 1 of 2):

When he indicated the greatness of His station through some of what will happen on the Day of Resurrection, he followed it with what the strong cannot bear of the conditions of that Day, as another proof, saying, indicating His great power, might, and majesty, in the passive form: ﴿And the Horn will be blown﴾; that is, the trumpet (al-qarn), which gathers things together, brings them toward its sound, turns them away from their states, and overpowers them on that Day (p-552), after the resurrection of creation. It is the first blast after the Resurrection, which comes after the two blasts of death and resurrection mentioned in surah Ya-Sin. What is meant by it, and Allah knows best, is the casting of terror, fear, and dread into the hearts, to show greatness and to clothe Himself in pride and might, in the honor of the Day of Gathering. So the first thing that will surprise them on the Day of Judgment is what the strong cannot bear and what intellects and minds cannot endure, just as the last thing that surprised them in the Day of this world was of this kind, although the two differ in their effect. That one caused death, and this one causes unconsciousness, because there is no death after resurrection. It is the third of the blasts. ﴿Then all those in the heavens will swoon﴾; that is, will be stunned. Since the context calls for dread, and explicit mention is more terrifying, he repeated the subject by its wording, saying: ﴿and all those on earth﴾.

Since some of them will not swoon, and so that it may always be known that He is free to choose in every one of His acts, able, and overpowering, He made an exception, saying: ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾; that is, He to whom belong the sources of greatness and the bonds of might, who makes one thing a destruction for one group and not for another, and a swooning for one group and not another. He makes that which caused destruction a source of life, and that which caused unconsciousness a source of revival, even though with respect to them both are equal. This is to inform that the Agent who affects and acts is the one who wills, not the effect. It was said: those excepted are the martyrs; and it was said: others than them. ﴿Then it will be blown again﴾ (p-553), that is, a second blast of this kind, which is the fourth of the deadly blasts. Its swift effect is indicated by the suddenness in His saying: ﴿then behold, they will be standing﴾; that is, all of them standing; ﴿looking﴾; that is, directing their eyes, or awaiting what comes after that of the like of it, from the signs of greatness.

These two blasts are the ones meant in the hadith about the dispute between a Jew and a Muslim who slapped his face. At its end: "People will swoon on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to revive. Then behold, Musa (Moses) is grasping the side of the Throne, so I do not know whether he revived before me, or was recompensed with the swoon of Mount Tur." Al-Bukhari narrated it in the Book of Disputes in two places, in the Traditions of the Prophets in two places, in al-Riqaq, and in al-Tawhid. Muslim narrated it in al-Fada'il, Abu Dawud in al-Sunnah, and al-Nasa'i in al-Tafsir and al-Nu'ut. With a detailed examination of its narrations and a gathering of their wordings, it becomes known that what I have mentioned is what is meant. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated, in the Traditions of the Prophets, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "While a Jew was displaying his merchandise, and Bukhari said: his merchandise, he was offered for it something he disliked or did not accept. He said: No, by Him who chose Musa over mankind. A man from the Ansar heard him and slapped him, and Bukhari said: so he stood and slapped his face (p-554). He said: You say, by Him who chose Musa over mankind, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is among us?! So the Jew went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Abu al-Qasim, I have a covenant and a pact. And he said: So-and-so slapped my face. And Bukhari said: Why did so-and-so slap my face? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Why did you slap his face?' He said: O Messenger of Allah, he said: 'By Him who chose Musa over mankind,' while you are among us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry until anger was seen in his face, then he said: 'Do not prefer between the prophets of Allah, for the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and I will be the first to be raised.' In Muslim's narration: 'or among the first to be raised.' 'Then behold, Musa is holding the Throne, so I do not know whether he was counted among those who swooned at the Day of Tur, or was raised before me. I do not say that anyone is better than Yunus ibn Matta.'" In a narration of Bukhari in the commentary of surah al-Zumar: "'I am among the first to raise his head after the last blast, and behold, Musa is clinging to the Throne, so I do not know whether that was so, or after the blast.'" In a narration of Bukhari in the Disputes, al-Riqaq, and the Traditions of the Prophets, and it is also in Muslim, both said: "Two men quarreled, a man from the Muslims and a man from the Jews (in a narration of Muslim: a man from the Jews and a man from the Muslims). The Muslim said: 'By Him who chose Muhammad (ﷺ) over the worlds.'" Bukhari said in the Book of Tawhid and the Traditions of the Prophets: "in an oath he swore." "The Jew said: 'By Him who chose Musa over the worlds.'" Bukhari said: "So the Muslim became angry at that and slapped the face of the Jew." Muslim said, and likewise Bukhari in al-Tawhid, al-Khusumat, and the Traditions of the Prophets: "So the Muslim raised his hand at that and slapped the face of the Jew. The Jew went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and told him what had happened between him and the Muslim." Bukhari said in the Disputes: "So the Prophet (ﷺ) called the Muslim and asked him about it, and he informed him, then they agreed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Do not give me preference over Musa, for people will swoon'" (Bukhari said in al-Riqaq, al-Khusumat, the Traditions of the Prophets, and a copy in al-Tawhid: "on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be among the first to revive"). In another narration of his in the Disputes: "then I will swoon with them." In another narration of his in al-Riqaq, and another in al-Tawhid, and it is a narration of Muslim and Abu Dawud: "then I will be the first to revive, and behold, Musa is holding the side of the Throne" (Abu Dawud said: "at the side of the Throne"), "so I do not know whether he was among those who swooned and then revived before me, or whether he was among those whom Allah excepted." In another narration: "so I do not know whether he was among those who swooned and revived before me, or he was content with the swoon of Tur." In another narration of Bukhari in the Traditions of the Prophets: "so I do not know whether he was among those who swooned and revived, or among those whom Allah excepted." He did not mention "before me." Al-Tirmidhi narrated the hadith in the commentary of surah al-Zumar, and Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd (p-556). He said: "The Jew said" (Ibn Majah said: "a man from the Jews") "in the market of Madinah: 'By Him who chose Musa over mankind.' A man from the Ansar raised a hand and struck his face with it" (Ibn Majah said: "so he slapped him"). He said: "You say this while the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) is among us?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And the Horn will be blown." Ibn Majah said: "You say this while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is among us?" It was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Allah (the Exalted) said: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking﴾. I will be the first to raise his head, and behold, Musa is seizing" (Ibn Majah said: "and behold, I am with Musa, seizing") "one of the legs of the Throne, so I do not know whether he raised his head before me, or was among those whom Allah excepted. And whoever says, 'I am better than Yunus ibn Matta,' has lied." Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith" (good and sound). In a narration of Bukhari in al-Riqaq: "People will swoon when they swoon, and I will be the first to stand. Then behold, Musa is seizing the Throne, so I do not know whether he was among those who swooned." He said: It was narrated by Abu Sa'id (may Allah be pleased with him) from the Prophet (peace be upon him). And in Bukhari, in the Disputes, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting, a Jew came and said: 'O Abu al-Qasim, a man from your companions struck my face.' He said: 'Who?' He said: 'A man from the Ansar.' He said: 'Call him.' He said: 'Did you strike him?' He said: 'I heard him in the market swearing, by Him who chose Musa over mankind. I said: "Wicked one over Muhammad!" and anger seized me, so I struck his face.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Do not prefer between the prophets, for people will swoon on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first whom the earth splits open for' (in a narration in the Traditions of the Prophets: 'I will be the first to revive'), 'then behold, Musa is seizing one of the legs of the Throne, so I do not know whether he was among those who swooned, or was reckoned for his first swoon.'" In a narration in the Traditions of the Prophets: "I do not know whether he revived before me, or was reckoned for the swoon of Tur."

And Allah knows best. This is what I have seen of the wordings of the hadith in the Six Books. As for the meaning of "ṣaʿiqa" (swooned), it means: he cried out and died suddenly, or he was overcome by unconsciousness. In al-Qamus (the dictionary) it says: al-ṣāʿiqa is death, and every destructive punishment, and a cry of punishment. "Ṣaʿiqa," like "samiʿa," ṣaʿqan, may be vocalized as ṣaʿaqa; and ṣaʿqatan, and taṣʿāqan: he was overcome by unconsciousness. And al-ṣaʿaq, with a vowel on each letter: intensity of sound; and like kataf: one of intense voice. Abd al-Haqq said in al-Wa'i: al-Azhari said: "al-ṣāʿiqa" is a violent thunderclap from which a person swoons, meaning he is overcome by unconsciousness. It is said: "al-ṣāʿiqa struck them," meaning with the vowel; and "it struck them" (aṣ'aqathum) when it reached them, so they swooned and were struck. From it is the hadith of al-Hasan: "The one struck dead is awaited for three days, as long as they do not fear a stench from him," meaning the one who died suddenly. He said: "al-ṣāʿiqa" is a verbal noun that came in the form fāʿila. You say: "I heard the thunderclap of the thunder, and the bleating of the sheep." And His saying (p-558): ﴿And Musa fell down swooning﴾ [al-A'raf: 143], that is, overcome by unconsciousness. His words, glory be to Him, indicate this: ﴿When he recovered﴾ [al-A'raf: 143]. One says "recovered" only from illness and fainting, and "was raised" only from death. He said: The whole of the ṣāʿiqa is a sound together with fire. Abu Abd Allah, meaning al-Qazzaz, said: the ṣaʿq is that a person hears the sound of a violent crash, so his intellect swoons because of it. The derivation of "al-ṣāʿiqa" is from this; it was named "ṣāʿiqa" because of the intensity of its sound. You say: "He is a ṣaʿiq," meaning of intense sound; and likewise "he is ṣuʿāq." End.

Thus it becomes clear from this that *al-sa'q* (swooning, the loss of consciousness) is applied to sudden death and likewise to fainting (*ghashy*), and that recovery (*ifaqah*) occurs only after a swoon, not after death. It is therefore known that the *sa'qah* (the single stroke of swooning) in this verse is only a swoon, because the second one is followed by recovery. Moreover, it is established that no one dies in the *barzakh* (the intermediate realm between death and resurrection), so how could the prophets, peace be upon them, die there? The correct view is to interpret the *sa'qah* mentioned in the hadith as a swoon or something resembling it. This is supported by the possibility that the *sa'qah* of Sinai was a recompense for it. And if it is a swoon, then, if we say that it occurs through the blast of death (*nafkhat al-imatah*), it follows that neither the swoon nor its absence has any bearing on the doubt over whether Musa, peace be upon him, recovered before it or whether he never experienced a swoon at all. This is because what his striking the Throne (*batshuhu bil-'arsh*) refers to, while he is with his spirit and body, is the resurrection from death, not the recovery from a swoon, nor the absence of a swoon before the resurrection. What clarifies the matter and leaves no ambiguity is that this occurs after the resurrection, and then the blasts become four. The first is for the death of the living; the second is for the revival of all the dead. These two are the ones mentioned in Surah Ya-Sin. (p-559) That is why, when He mentioned them, He stated concerning them what admits of no other meaning: ﴿They await only a single Blast which will seize them while they are disputing﴾ [Ya-Sin: 49]; ﴿So they will not be able to make a bequest, nor will they return to their families﴾ [Ya-Sin: 50]; ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and at once they will rush from the graves to their Lord﴾ [Ya-Sin: 51]. The third is for their being startled after the resurrection by a terrible dread, as the situation requires, because that Day is a day of terrors, awe, dread, and the manifestation of greatness and majesty, so that all means are cut off. What the hadith indicates in its many narrations is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, the people will swoon on the Day of Resurrection." The Day of Resurrection is the name of the time whose beginning is the resurrection and whose end is the complete entry of each group into its abode and place of settlement. As for the swoon of death, it occurs in the abode of this world, and it is for putting to sleep, not for dwelling (*li'l-inamah la li'l-iqamah*). The sound narrations, which firmly state that the Prophet (ﷺ) will be the first whom the earth splits open for, weaken the interpretation of it as occurring before the resurrection. Al-Karmani also related a consensus (*ijma'*) on this. There is no merit in it except through the occurrence of the resurrection, not through the mere appearance of the body without a resurrection. So this firm assertion contradicts that doubt. If what is meant in the hadith is the swoon, then there is another blast for awakening from it. These two are what is meant in this surah, as in the narration of al-Tirmidhi, and in Surah al-Naml. That is why it is expressed as *al-faza'* (terror). This is supported by the expression in the narration of al-Bukhari, in the Book of Tafsir, as "the last blast" (*al-nafkhah al-akhirah*). The Prophet (ﷺ) was given *jawami' al-kalim* (concise, comprehensive speech), and his speech was condensed for him in abridgement. Had they been only two blasts, the expression "the last" would have fallen short of what the second conveys, despite the equality in the number of letters. This is not to be presumed of an eloquent speaker, so how of the most eloquent of creation, supported by the Holy Spirit (ﷺ)? So the shift from "the second" to "the last" indicates that they are four. Perhaps this is the meaning of: ﴿You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice﴾ [Ghafir: 11]. It was called *imatah* (causing to die) because of the intensity of the swoon caused by it, due to the magnitude of its matter. And the meaning of "the quaking of the Hour" which "will make the nursing mother forget" is consistent with this. It is also supported by the expression of rising from it as *ifaqah* (recovery), not *ba'th* (resurrection). Nothing troubles this except the narration of al-Bukhari in the chapter on disputes: "So I will be the first whom the earth splits open for; and behold, Musa..." to the end. Apparently its narrator erred, or related it by meaning, so it did not fulfil the purpose. The preponderant narrations are those of the ones who said: "So I will be the first to recover" (*fa-akunu awwala man yufiq*), by their number, and with the removal of the difficulty. This is what appeared to me in reflecting on the meaning and applying the verses and hadiths to it. Then I saw our shaykh, the hafiz of his age, Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn Hajar al-Kinani al-'Asqalani al-Misri, may God have mercy on him, relate in the Book of the Prophets from his commentary on al-Bukhari, from Qadi 'Iyad, what I had gathered to reconcile the narrations. He said: "'Iyad said: It is possible that what is meant is the *sa'qat fazi'* (swoon of terror) after the resurrection, when the heaven and earth split open," and he affirmed this. Then he related from Ibn Hazm the exact same thing I had said about the blasts, and he said the following text: "A supplement: Ibn Hazm claimed that the blasts on the Day of Resurrection are four. The first is the blast of death, in which whoever remains alive on the earth dies (p-561) ; the second is the blast of life, so every dead person rises; the third is the blast of terror and swooning, from which they recover as those who have fainted, and none dies from it; and the fourth is recovery from that swoon." Then our shaykh refuted him by saying that the swoons are four, but this does not necessitate that the blasts be more than two. That is because the first blast is blown into the Horn, so whoever is alive dies, and whoever is dead is swooned over. These are two swoons in the first blast. Then the second blast is blown, so whoever was swooned recovers, and whoever was dead lives. These are two in the second blast. This refutation is rejected for anyone who examines what I have said with even slight reflection. It also entails that the chosen servants of God would be in a worse state and greater terror than those upon whom the Hour will come, and they are the worst of God's servants. It is strange that he who refuted Ibn Hazm accepted this from 'Iyad. And God is the Granter of success.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 69:

When He mentioned their sustenance through life, which is the light of the body, He followed it with their sustenance through the light of the whole of creation: outwardly through sensory light, and inwardly through judgment according to the path of justice, which is the light of existence, both outward and inward in reality; just as injustice is darkness, so too [justice is light]. So He said: ﴿And the earth shines with the light of its Lord﴾; that is, it shines with a great radiance, inclining towards redness by it; ﴿the earth﴾; that is, the one brought into being for their gathering. The speech turned away from the Greatest Name to the attribute of beneficence, because of the predominance of mercy, especially on that Day, for no one enters Paradise except by it.
