So He said: ﴿with the light of its Lord﴾; that is, the One who nurtured it with beneficence towards it, by making it a place for justice and grace, so that nothing other than that exists in it at all. (p-562) That light, which is one thing, is seen by one people and not by others, just as the Trumpet was at one time for destruction and at another time for life.

Since knowledge is in reality the light, and the Book is the foundation of knowledge, and since that Day has a greatness that exceeds description, and therefore the disbelievers denied it, He used, in what happens on it by His permission, the passive form, following the manner of the speech of those who are capable, indicating its lowliness before Him and that it is subservient to His command, with no burden upon Him in any of that; and likewise the verbs after it, as an increase in depicting the greatness of the Day through the greatness of the affair in it. So He said: ﴿And the Book will be placed﴾; that is, the one sent down to every nation so that they might act by it.

Since the prophets are more general than the messengers, and the Prophet is one who is sent to command whoever is commanded to enjoin the good, and whom God wills good for may follow him; and their number was 124,000, which is very few relative to all people, He expressed them without the messengers, and with the plural of paucity, saying: ﴿And the prophets will be brought﴾; for bearing witness against their nations regarding the delivery of the message. And since the least number of witnesses is twice the number of those held accountable, He expressed it with the plural of abundance, saying: ﴿and the witnesses﴾; that is, those appointed over the accountable, who observed their deeds and so bore witness to them and recorded them; thus the foundations were established, the claims were formulated, and the proofs were set up according to them, (p-563) of obedience or disobedience; and the recompense befell according to that, so justice appeared as mercy towards the disbelievers, and grace became manifest as mercy towards the Muslims. ﴿And judgment will be passed between them﴾; that is, between the servants, for whose sake all of that was done. Since the context is manifestly about the generality of grace, both justice and grace, as the alert to it will come, He said: ﴿with truth﴾; by the actual rewards and punishments corresponding to what the report in the Books, upon the tongues of the messengers, had stated.

Since the intended meaning is the perfection of the truth, considering its generality over all persons and deeds, and since a possibility of some specification might occur to one, He removed that by His saying: ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾; that is, neither inwardly nor outwardly; that is, no injustice will ever newly befall them at any time at all; so they will not be increased in the recompense of an evil deed beyond its like, nor will they be diminished in the recompense of a good deed below ten-fold.

When this was the case, it may have been relative to what the ruling applies to, and it is not explicit that the ruling covers every deed. He stated it explicitly with His words, mentioning fulfilment (*al-wafa'*) and action, because the context requires that, by mentioning the Book and what is within its scope of the prophets, the martyrs, and the true judgment. All of this is most fitting to mention with action founded upon knowledge, and fulfilment, which is the greatest pillar of truth and the thread of knowledge. Knowledge and fulfilment are more suitable for making the deed itself the recompense, so that it is depicted in the fair forms it deserves if it is a reward, and in the ugly forms if it is a punishment. This also distinguishes it from the intellect founded upon desire and the strength of the motivating impulse: ﴿And every soul will be paid in full﴾. Since full payment in recompense is at the utmost degree of precision, and of exaggeration in fulfilment, and of conformity in form and meaning, He made the one paid in full the very deed itself, so He said: ﴿what it did﴾, that is, of the good deeds. For this reason He expressed it with *al-'amal* (action), which cannot occur except with knowledge. The closing phrase implied the implicit estimate: ﴿And God knows best what they do﴾. Since *al-shuhada'* (the witnesses) is intended to mean the establishing of rights according to what people customarily recognize, and this might suggest a deficiency in knowledge, He said: ﴿and He is most knowing﴾, that is, more than the doers and the witnesses against them, ﴿of what they do﴾, that is, of what is done by motivation from the self, whether or not it was accompanied by regard for knowledge. Thus the verse is an instance of *al-ihtibak* (the rhetorical device of elliptical balancing, where each of two mentioned items implies the omitted counterpart of the other): the mention of *"what it did"* first implies *"what it did"* second, and the mention of *"what they do"* second implies *"what they do"* first. Its secret is that what was mentioned is more suitable to the purpose of negating injustice in light of the ruling of promise with justice and bounty, because it includes recompense for everything built upon knowledge. As for what is desired, it is not mentioned that one is recompensed for it, but rather God knows it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 71:

When the predominant theme in these stations is warning, he (Allah) foregrounded in this fulfilment (of the account) the condition of the people of wrath. He said: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven⦆; that is, with an easy command from Us, after the reckoning has been established, driven with harsh driving; ﴿those who disbelieved﴾; that is, they covered the lights of their intellects, so matters became confused for them and they went astray; ﴿to Hell﴾; that is, the rank which will meet them with sternness, just as they met the commands, the prohibitions, and those who upheld them, with the same; for that is necessarily bound to the covering of the intellect; ﴿in groups﴾; that is, companies, in divisions, some following upon others (so said Abu 'Ubayd), classes sorted, each person with those who suit him in path and company. Zumrah (group) is derived from al-zamr (ز م ر), which is a sound containing ambiguity, like the well-known zamr (wind instrument), because that sound is a necessary accompaniment of gathering.

When the closing of the door against the one who seeks it signifies his humiliation, that indicates their condition is likewise. By His saying, mentioning the end of the driving: ﴿until, when they reach it﴾; that is, in the attitude of abasement and humiliation; and the answer of "when" (idha) is His saying: ﴿its gates will be opened﴾; that is, it is hastened, as is done with the doors of prisons for the people of crimes, after they have gathered there, in opening them quickly, so that there will come out to them what had been confined by their closing, of the heat whose fire and sparks will meet them, in a state more bitter than meeting the arrows which they chose in the world over accepting what opposed their desires of fine speech.

When the afflicted one may perhaps hope for mercy, but if he finds someone who rebukes him, his rebuke is more painful to him than what he is in; He said: ﴿And their keepers will say to them﴾; in denunciation of them, reproach, and rebuke; ﴿Did there not come to you messengers﴾; and since the establishment of proof through one of their own kind is stronger, He said, describing "messengers": ﴿from among you﴾; that is, so that their being addressed would be easy for you.

When following up with reminder is more effective upon the soul, He said, bringing another attribute, expressing it by recitation, which is more fitting to what the aim of the surah revolves around of worship, because of the deficient shortcomings of souls which need continual reminder: ﴿reciting﴾; that is, they continuously follow; ﴿to you the verses of﴾; and since the command of the one who does good is lighter upon the soul, so it is more likely to be accepted, they said: ﴿your Lord﴾; that is, with glad tidings if you follow; and since warning is more forceful in deterrence, they said: ﴿and warning you of the meeting of this your day﴾; and since indication is higher in specification, they said: ﴿this﴾; pointing to the entire Day of Resurrection; that is, from the King, the Almighty, if you contend; the verse is of ihtibak (interlocking ellipsis): He mentioned "the Lord" first, indicating the omission of "the might" second; and "warning" second, as an indication of "glad tidings" first; ﴿They will say, "Yes"﴾; that is, indeed they came to us, recited to us, and warned us.

When their not turning to deliverance from what they had fallen into, though it was easy, is among the most astonishing of wonders, they explained its cause by their saying: ﴿But the word of punishment has become due﴾; that is, it became due with a due that conforms to reality, such that one cannot be freed from it; ﴿against the disbelievers﴾; that is, which had preceded in eternity against us; thus was the original; but they said: ﴿against the disbelievers﴾, specifying it to the people of this attribute, and explaining that it is what necessitates their entry, namely their covering of the lights which the messengers brought them.

When they had finished humiliating them with reproach, they were rebuked by the command to enter. He expressed it in the passive form (al-mabni li'l-maf'ul) to indicate that they had reached the utmost degree of abasement, such that they obey the word of every speaker, be he great or lowly. So it was said, in answer to one who might ask, "What befell them after this rebuke?": ﴿It is said﴾, i.e., to them, in reply to their speech: ﴿Enter the gates of Hell﴾, i.e., its levels, which are grim for those who enter them. And since the report of eternal abiding at the time of entering is more painful for them, they said: ﴿abiding therein﴾, i.e., (p-567) determining to abide ﴿therein﴾. And since the cause of their disbelief in the proofs was arrogance, he linked to the command to enter his saying, left without emphasis (because it is said in the Hereafter, where there is no denial that would call for emphasis, and nothing of the kind had preceded from them here, unlike in [Surah] al-Nahl, but rather acknowledgment and regret): ﴿So evil is the abode of the arrogant﴾, i.e., the dwelling place and residence; ﴿the arrogant﴾, i.e., those whose arrogance made the word of punishment binding upon them, and therefore they pursued its causes.

When he had mentioned the states of the disbelievers, he followed it with the states of their opposites, and said: ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to the Garden in groups﴾. Their being driven to the good place indicates that their station was good, because whoever is in the lowest of distress and is then prepared a pleasant place does not need to be driven to go there. How far apart are the two drivings: this is a driving of honour, and that is a driving of humiliation and retribution. By my life, this is one of the marvels of the kinds of al-badi' (rhetorical embellishment): that He, glorified is He, uses a word concerning the disbelievers that indicates their humiliation through their punishment, and then uses that very same word, in the same form, concerning the righteous, so that it indicates their honour through the goodness of their reward. Glory be to the One who sent it down, inimitable in its wording, firmly established in its meanings, sweet in its sources and its repetitions.

Since this is not for all the happy but only for the sincere among them, He indicated this by His saying: ﴿Those who feared﴾, meaning not all the believers, ﴿their Lord﴾, meaning those who, whenever He increases them in goodness, increase in awe of Him. Ahmad, Abu Ya'la, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih narrated from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A day whose measure is fifty thousand years." It was asked: "How long is this day?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, it will be made light for the believer until it is lighter for him than an obligatory prayer." [p-568]

Al-Tabarani and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "You will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection..." and he mentioned the hadith until he said: They said: "Where will the believers be on that day?" He said: "Thrones of light will be placed for them, and the clouds will shade them. That day will seem shorter to the believers than an hour of a day."

It is possible that the driving is an indication of the decree compelling each of the two groups toward the deeds that are the causes of the two abodes. ﴿To the Garden in groups﴾: the people of prayer, who devote themselves to it and increase in it, each group apart; likewise the people of fasting, and others according to the deeds whose effects appear upon the faces.

When he mentioned the driving, he mentioned its goal by His saying: ﴿Until, when they reach it﴾. Since closing the door against the one who arrives indicates contempt for him, and standing there until it is opened for him is a kind of humiliation, He said: ﴿and its gates are opened﴾, meaning, while the state is that its gates have already been opened, ﴿its gates﴾, as an honour to them before their arrival, by the very act of opening, and by what comes out to them of its fragrance, and what they see of its blossoms and its radiance, so that this becomes for them a second driving toward what they have never seen the like of, nor seen anything comparable to it.

When he mentioned their honour through the conditions of the abode, he mentioned their honour through the righteous guardians, and said, coordinating (by 'atf) with the answer to ﴿إذا﴾ (idha, "when"), with an implied meaning such as: "its guardians received them with everything that would delight them": ﴿And its guardians will say to them﴾, meaning upon arrival: ﴿Peace be upon you﴾, hastening their joy by the good news of safety, in which there is no ruin. Since it is an abode fit only for the purified, they said: ﴿You are good﴾, meaning you are fit to dwell in it, so there is no moving away from it at all. Then they gave the reason for that, as an indication that it is the abode of goodness, so that no one enters it except one who is suited to it, saying: ﴿So enter it﴾. This produced: ﴿abiding therein﴾. Perhaps the benefit of omitting the answer to ﴿إذا﴾ is that the soul may go in every direction of honour, and know that no description can encompass it. And among the most fitting things is that their entry should be without any barrier of a closed door or a prevented gatekeeper, but rather that they are permitted, welcomed, into the dominion of eternity.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 74:

Since the implied sense is "so they entered it" (fa-dakhalūhā), he joined to it his saying: ﴿And they said﴾; that is, all of those who entered. ﴿Praise﴾; that is, the comprehensive attribution of all the qualities of perfection. They turned to the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam), urging their own souls to call to mind all the attributes that they are able to know. So they said: ﴿to God﴾; that is, the Greatest King, ﴿who has fulfilled His promise to us﴾; in His saying: ﴿That is the Garden which We cause to inherit from among Our servants those who were God-fearing﴾ [Maryam: 63]. Thus His saying corresponded to the reality (al-waqi') (p-570) that we found in this very hour. ﴿And has made us inherit﴾; as He promised us; ﴿the earth﴾; which, in reality, has no other earth, and it is the earth of the Garden, in which there is no turbidity in any respect, and in which is everything that the souls desire and that the eyes delight in. He made our state therein one of complete possession, and of not being the cause of it in reality, the state of the heir who comes after his inheritance, with nothing after him and no contender for it, our state being ﴿that we may take up residence﴾; that is, we take for ourselves dwellings that are fit for one who has left them to desire to return to them. They specified the earth, in the place of the pronoun, by their saying: ﴿from the Garden﴾; that is, all of it; ﴿wherever we will﴾; because of its vastness, so that there is no need for anyone in it to contend with anyone over a place at all, and no one desires except his own place. Since it had this glorious description, its praise followed from it in His saying: ﴿How excellent is﴾ (fa-ni'ma) the reward of us; this is how the original would be; but He said: ﴿the reward of those who work﴾, as an encouragement toward deeds and an urging against reliance (on mere hope).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 39, verse 75:

When He, glory be to Him, mentioned those in whom He had placed desires, and the ranks they attained, He followed them with the people of honour (karamat), those with nothing to distract them from acts of worship (ibadat). He said, turning the address, because the report is elevated, to the highest of creation, that none other than him can truly bear the duty of this sight: ﴿And you will see﴾; expressing it with something more specific than seeing (ibsar), more specific than looking (nazar), as he explained in "al-Baqarah" in His saying (exalted is He): ﴿that power belongs entirely to Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 165]. ﴿The angels﴾, who stand over all the rights incumbent upon them; ﴿circling﴾, meaning encompassing, surrounding and going around, in throngs that none can count except Allah. From "al-haff", which is gathering; and "al-hafafah", which is the company of people and large numbers; and it is the plural of "hafif", which is one of an encircling company.

Since the greatness of a thing derives from the greatness of its owner, and none encompasses the greatness of the Throne in its true encompassing except Allah (exalted is He), He indicated this by introducing the preposition, saying: ﴿around the Throne﴾; meaning the place that revolves about it and is surrounded by it, from "al-hawl", which is encompassing, turning and revolving; encircling some of its edges, meaning its sides which can be encircled, nearby; there is heard in their circling a sound of glorification, praise, sanctification and trembling out of fear of their Lord. So the use of "min" conveys that they, despite their multitude to a degree none can count except Allah, do not fill what surrounds it. ﴿Glorifying with the praise of﴾ — and He turned the speech to the description of beneficence, as praise for them for hastening to thank the Benefactor, and as training for others — so He said: ﴿their Lord﴾; meaning, they exaggerate in declaring Him free of deficiency, such that someone might imagine that He needs a throne or something else, or that a place could contain Him; while affirming perfection to the One who benefits them, by obligating them to worship, without any preoccupation that occupies them, nor any rival of desire or portion that distracts them, delighting in His remembrance and honoured by sanctifying Him; and because it is His due that His greatness be manifested constantly, as His bounty is continuous.

Since the mention of judgment among the people of desires had preceded, with what was manifested against them of testimonies, (p-572) here He mentions the judgment between them and the angels, who debated the origin of their creation by saying: "Will You place in it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?" — the verse. So He said: ﴿And it will be judged between them﴾; meaning between the people of desires and the people of protection and steadfastness. Since the context is general in encouragement and warning, justice and grace, unlike the context of Surah Yunus — peace be upon him — He said: ﴿with truth﴾; by weighing them against what We revealed concerning them in the Books which We set for their reckoning, which is the reality. So whoever among them transgressed, We lodged him in "Laza" by Our justice; and whoever feared God, We bestowed bounty upon him in the Garden of Refuge by Our grace, for their striving against the desires within them, until they remained steadfast in obedience, despite what their natures drew them toward in ignorance. As for the angels, We left them in their state of worship. ﴿And it will be said﴾; meaning, by every speaker, at the end of all matters: ﴿The praise﴾; meaning the encompassing of all attributes of perfection; and He turned the speech to what is fitting for this station, saying: ﴿is for Allah﴾, Lord of majesty and honour. We knew this on this day with certainty of certainty, just as we used to know it in the world with knowledge of certainty.

Since that day is most worthy of the days for recognizing the comprehensiveness of lordship, because of the gathering of creatures, the opening of insights, and the breadth of hearts, He said, describing Himself, glory be to Him, with the attribute closest to the Greatest Name: ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾; meaning, He who originated them (p-573) first from non-existence; established them second by what He nurtured them with of management; returned them third after their annihilation, with the most perfect decree and measure; and kept them fourth, not for good alone. For He fulfilled His promise, as He sent down in His Book, and confirmed His threat against His enemies, as He said in His Book; so it became clear that it is His revelation. He concluded the matter by affirming perfection under the name of Praise at the entrance to the Gardens and the Fires, just as He began with it at the beginning of creation in the first of blessings. So to Him belongs the encompassing of perfection, that the matter is as His Book states in every state. The end thus fits the beginning: the Book is His revelation, because all that is in it corresponds to reality when its interpretation comes; and the Book that moves to piety, which causes Paradise, was sent down for the first preservation; whoever follows it has a cause for the second preservation. This last is the very beginning of Surah Ghafir. Glory be to Him who sent it down, its order inimitable, its beginning and end surpassing all powers. And may Allah send blessings upon our master Muhammad (ﷺ), his family, his companions, the People of his House, the pure and purified, and all his Companions.
